items.title: [Prod] Multi-tenancy with Postgres RLS (and connector customer_id)

milestone.title: Production readiness
milestone.description: Plan: docs/production-architecture.md

items.body:
> **Milestone:** Production readiness · **Plan:** [`docs/production-architecture.md`](https://github.com/Prateek1771/azentio-hr/blob/main/docs/production-architecture.md)

## Summary
The app has one workspace. The connector interface dropped the design spec's `customer_id` argument for that reason (`backend/connectors/base.py:4`), and no table, graph node or query carries a tenant id. production-architecture.md makes multi-tenancy a P2 stage goal: 10 tenants live, and no cross-tenant access in a dedicated security test. The design is a `tenants` table, `tenant_id` on every table enforced by Postgres row-level security, and per-tenant mailboxes, LLM budgets and data keys.

## Scope
- Migration: `tenants` table; `tenant_id NOT NULL` on every business table with a default tenant backfill; RLS policies `USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant')::uuid)`
- `shared/db.tx()` sets `app.tenant` from the request's session (`SET LOCAL`); jobs carry `tenant_id` in the payload and set it the same way
- Graph read model: a tenant property on projected nodes, or one graph per tenant (decide in the ADR)
- Connectors: restore the `customer_id`/workspace argument and per-tenant connector instances
- Per-tenant `SECRETS_KEY` data keys (pairs with the KMS issue), mailbox, LLM budget
- `tenant_id` in every log line

## Checkpoints
- [ ] ADR: RLS design, graph-per-tenant vs property, the migration strategy
- [ ] Add `tenants` + `tenant_id` columns with backfill (no RLS yet)
- [ ] Set `app.tenant` in `tx()` and in the job worker; enable RLS table by table
- [ ] Restore the connector `customer_id` argument and per-tenant connector instances
- [ ] Scope the graph projection and the policy chunk index by tenant
- [ ] Cross-tenant security test suite in CI
- [ ] Update the LLD, production-architecture §5.2 and AGENTS.md

## Test cases it must pass
- [ ] `test_tenancy.py::test_rls_blocks_cross_tenant_reads`: Given employees in tenants A and B, when a session for A lists employees or fetches B's id directly, then only A's rows come back and B's id is a 404
- [ ] `test_tenancy.py::test_job_runs_under_its_tenant`: Given a job enqueued by tenant A, when the worker runs it, then `current_setting('app.tenant')` is A and it can't read B
- [ ] `test_tenancy.py::test_missing_tenant_setting_fails_closed`: Given a connection with no `app.tenant` set, when any business table is queried, then zero rows (RLS default deny)
- [ ] `test_tenancy.py::test_policy_retrieval_never_returns_other_tenant_chunks`: Given policy chunks in A and B, when A's assistant retrieves, then no B chunk appears
- Always-on gate:
  - [ ] `uv run ruff check .` clean
  - [ ] `python scripts/check_boundaries.py` (and `--selftest` if a rule is added)
  - [ ] `test_core.py` · `test_phase0.py` · `test_phase1.py` · `test_phase2.py` · `test_phase3.py` green (a new phase adds its own `test_phaseN.py`)
  - [ ] `scripts/api_contract.py --check` passes, or `--capture` with the deliberate API change explained in the PR

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every business table has RLS on
- [ ] The dedicated cross-tenant test passes in CI
- [ ] Connectors are per tenant

## Dependencies
- #38 [Prod] Connector and field secrets: KMS envelope encryption
- #31 [Prod] Decide: policy and digest retrieval in FalkorDB vs pgvector; enable embeddings

## Risks / open questions
- The table-owner role bypasses RLS. The app must connect as a non-owner role.
- A large backfill migration. Do it table by table and keep each migration transaction-safe (AGENTS.md).

## References
- backend/connectors/base.py:4
- docs/lld.md §15 (row 1)
- docs/production-architecture.md §3 principle 7, §5.2, §7, §11
- docs/hld.md §1

---
<sub>Definition of done (hardening design §5–§7): the checkpoints and tests above pass · every new human action is audited under a named user (`audit.record_audit(..., conn=)`) · permissions only in `identity/perms.py` with a matrix row in `test_phase0.py` · LLD, the phase doc and `AGENTS.md` updated in the same PR · index: [`docs/backlog.md`](https://github.com/Prateek1771/azentio-hr/blob/main/docs/backlog.md)</sub>

items.body:
## Summary
Load the SEC Risk/Return quarterly datasets into the structured fund_rr_facts table.

## Description
Implement the RR half of `sec` (PUBLIC, structured facts, `source_class=law`, retire; "a structured cross-check, not a substitute for filings").

Arch: quarterly zip of text and numeric files (about 97 KB to about 78 MB, 82 MB cited in 6.7); no key; same SEC site limits and declared User-Agent; lag about 2 weeks; facts go to `fund_rr_facts`, not chunks. `version_key` = the quarter file id. The fact columns are the ones set in E11-T10 (this ticket does not change the table). Writer role `fa_etl_public`; stream the zip, do not load it fully into memory.

Out of scope: any use of the facts by the agent tools (E3/E4); 497K (E11-T16).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given the recorded small quarter zip then rows are inserted into `fund_rr_facts` with `tenant_id = PUBLIC` and the row count equals the numeric file's row count (test `backend/tests/connectors/test_sec_rr.py::test_quarter_loads_expected_rows`).
- [ ] Given the same quarter loaded twice then no duplicate rows and one observation (test `test_quarter_reload_idempotent`).
- [ ] Given an 82 MB synthetic zip then peak memory stays under the configured cap (`SEC_RR_MAX_RSS_MB`, test `test_large_zip_streams`).
- [ ] Given a quarter file removed from the listing twice then the facts are retired (valid range closed), not deleted (test `test_rr_withdrawal_retires`).

items.title: Connector: Microsoft Azure (Resource Graph, Monitor alerts, costs)

labels.name: connector
labels.description: Integration with an external source system

items.body:
Sync Azure resources into the CMDB and use Azure Monitor alerts as event input.

Uses the connector framework (#18).

## CI sync
- **Azure Resource Graph** (one query across subscriptions; cheap and fast) with a service principal or managed identity.
- Resource types to start with: VMs and VM scale sets, App Service/Functions, AKS clusters, SQL servers and databases, PostgreSQL/MySQL flexible servers, Cosmos DB, storage accounts, Key Vault, and load balancers/Application Gateway. The list can be configured per connector.
- Synced fields: resource ID (stable source ID), name, type, subscription, resource group, location, SKU, provisioning/power state, and tags (tags such as `service`, `owner` and `costcenter` drive group membership).
- Relationships from resource properties (VM → NIC → VNet, web app → App Service plan, database → server).
- Source URL: `https://portal.azure.com/#@<tenant>/resource<resourceId>`.

## Events
- Pull: Azure Monitor alerts (Alerts Management API), Service Health and Resource Health.
- Push: an action group with a webhook to `POST /api/events` using the Azure common alert schema.

## Costs
- Cost Management Query API: monthly cost per resource and per tag. See #27.

items.title: MCP connector: pin the read allow-list's remaining assumptions with tests
items.body:
Non-blocking notes from the standards review of #1074. Each is a claim in the code with no test that would catch it breaking.

1. **No tool sends a caller-chosen tenant.** `tools.ts` comments say a string-built `?tenant_id=` is always the grant tenant. Only `care_gaps` has a mutation (M18). Add one test that runs every allow-listed tool on a grant session and asserts that every engine URL carries only the grant tenant.
2. **The resource-type and id lists are copied from the engine.** `FHIR_RESOURCE_TYPES` and `RESOURCE_ID_PATTERN` copy the engine's list and `r6/resource_ids.py`. Add a test that fails if they drift apart. Drift fails closed today, so the risk is low.
3. **The nested-tenant tripwire.** `TENANT_ARGUMENT` strips only top-level arguments, and a comment says a tool with nested tenant input needs its own strip before it joins the allow-list. Make that a test: every allow-listed tool's input schema has no nested property named like a tenant.
4. **Body reads.** Pin "only `/internal/*` routes read a tenant from a request body" with a scan test over the engine's blueprints.

items.title: Connectors: SDK trait + Mail connector (IMAP/Gmail/Graph)
items.body:
## Scope

Define the **Connector SDK trait** and implement a **Mail connector** (IMAP, Gmail API, Microsoft Graph) that feeds documents into the same xberg → gaze pipeline.

## Connector Trait (in `hacienda-connectors` crate)

```rust
pub trait DocumentConnector: Send + Sync {
    /// Unique connector identifier (e.g., "folder", "gmail", "graph")
    fn connector_id(&self) -> &'static str;

    /// List discoverable documents (metadata only, no content)
    async fn list(&self, cursor: Option<String>) -> Result<ConnectorPage<DocRef>>;

    /// Fetch full document content for extraction
    async fn fetch(&self, doc_ref: DocRef) -> Result<ExtractedInput>;

    /// Optional: incremental sync token
    fn supports_incremental(&self) -> bool { false }
}

pub struct DocRef {
    pub id: String,                    // stable across syncs
    pub connector: String,             // "folder" | "gmail" | "graph"
    pub metadata: DocMetadata,         // title, modified, size, labels, etc.
    pub fingerprint_namespace: String, // "folder" | "gmail:user@example.com"
}

pub struct ExtractedInput {
    pub content: Vec<u8>,
    pub mime_type: String,
    pub filename: Option<String>,
    pub metadata: DocMetadata,
}
```

## Mail Connector Implementations

| Provider | Auth | API | Notes |
|----------|------|-----|-------|
| **IMAP** | User/pass + OAuth2 | `imap` crate | RFC 3501, supports IDLE for push |
| **Gmail** | OAuth2 (Google) | Gmail REST API | `gmail` crate, batch requests, label filters |
| **Microsoft Graph** | OAuth2 (Entra) | Graph REST API | `graph-rs`, delta queries for incremental |

### Shared Mail Logic

- Fetch message + attachments → each becomes a `DocRef`
- Extract inline images? (configurable, default off)
- Thread grouping → single `DocRef` per thread (configurable)
- Label/folder mapping → `DocMetadata.labels`
- Incremental sync: IMAP UIDNEXT / Gmail historyId / Graph deltaLink

## Config (hacienda.toml)

```toml
[connectors.folder]
enabled = true
path = "~/Documents"
watch = true

[connectors.gmail]
enabled = false
oauth_client_id = "xxx"
oauth_client_secret = "xxx"
refresh_token = "xxx"          # or use keychain
labels = ["INBOX", "Important"]
max_messages_per_sync = 1000

[connectors.graph]
enabled = false
tenant_id = "xxx"
client_id = "xxx"
client_secret = "xxx"
mail_folders = ["Inbox", "Sent"]
```

## Acceptance

- `Connector` trait compiles, `FolderConnector` (existing) implements it
- `GmailConnector` + `GraphConnector` compile, unit tests with mock servers
- `hacienda-backend sync --connector gmail` runs incremental sync
- Doctor checks validate OAuth tokens, API reachability, rate limits
- Engine-era fingerprint includes `connector` + `fingerprint_namespace`

## References

- Map: #11 (Platform map)
- Spec §8 (Workstreams), ADR-0002 (fingerprint namespace)
- `async-imap`, `gmail-api`, `graph-rs` crates

## Summary
Create the source registry and the append-only observations table with RLS and grants.

## Description
Alembic migration for two tables, owned by E11 (planning note: E11 to E13 tables are created by their owning epic).

Arch (deep-dive/05-1 section 5.9): `source_registry` key `(tenant_id, source_id)`; `connector` (`ecfr`, `sec`, `eurlex`, `legislation_gov_uk`, `fca_api`, `publisher`), `source_class` (`law`, `qa`, `fca_api`, `publisher`), `on_withdraw` (`retire`, `erase`), `cursor jsonb`, `overlap_s` default 172800, `last_listing_at`, `frozen boolean`, `frozen_reason`, `rate_limit_rps`, `enabled`. `source_observations` key `(tenant_id, id)`: append-only; `source_id` composite FK, `external_id`, `version_key`, `content_sha256`, `source_ts`, `observed_at` (DB clock, `clock_timestamp()`), `state` in (`present`, `revoked`, `withdrawn`, `pending`), `listing_run_id`; unique on `(source_id, external_id, version_key, content_sha256)`; index `(tenant_id, source_id, external_id, observed_at DESC)`; "No UPDATE or DELETE grant except the erasure of an erased source".

Add ENABLE + FORCE RLS with tenant-match policies in the pattern of E1-T8 (PUBLIC rows readable by every tenant per the "own-or-PUBLIC SELECT" rule only where the arch says so; `source_registry` for a firm source is that tenant's). Writers are the ETL roles only; `fa_app` gets no write.

Out of scope: `document_versions` (E11-T5), connector code.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given the migration applied then `source_registry` and `source_observations` exist with the columns, check constraints on the enumerated values and the unique index of 5.9 (test `backend/tests/test_source_tables_schema.py::test_columns_and_unique_index`).
- [ ] Given `fa_etl` role when it tries UPDATE or DELETE on `source_observations` then it is denied; INSERT is allowed (test `test_observations_append_only_grants`, `integration`).
- [ ] Given a row of tenant A when tenant B's role selects `source_registry` then zero rows are returned; `relforcerowsecurity` is true for both tables (test `test_source_tables_rls_leak`, part of the L0 leak matrix).
- [ ] Given `alembic upgrade head` then `downgrade -1` then `upgrade head` the schema is identical (migration round-trip test).

items.title: Hackathon [Feature]: Add VictoriaMetrics data-source connector
items.body:
### Problem Statement

Many teams run VictoriaMetrics instead of Prometheus. Their alerting and recording rules hold the same hand written knowledge: what broken means for each service, with a summary, a description and a runbook link.

The accepted Prometheus proposal (#5424) covers Prometheus itself and lists VictoriaMetrics as compatible but untested. So VictoriaMetrics users have no supported way to bring their rules into cognee.

### Proposed Solution

Add a `victoriametrics` connector in cognee-community, following the shape of the Notion connector and using the same rule document format as the Prometheus connector, so both read the same way in the graph.

* **Auth:** none by default, with optional basic or bearer auth. The tenant is configurable, for single node and cluster setups
* **Ingest:** alerting and recording rules, one document per rule, from the definition fields only. No samples and no queries
* **Incremental sync:** there is no change feed for rules, so each run reads the full rule list. Unchanged rules are not processed again
* **Forget on delete:** a rule removed from the server is removed from the graph on the next sync

### Watch out for

* It is close to Prometheus but not the same. In a live response from the public playground, the tenant is part of the address, rules carry their own ids, and some fields are spelled differently
* Each rule has a datasource type, so rules over logs come back in the same list. Keep that in the document
* The response mixes definitions with runtime state such as last evaluation time and health. Only definition fields go into the document, or every sync looks like a change
* Do not ingest metrics. They are numbers over time and belong in a dashboard, not a graph

### Acceptance criteria

* [ ] A user connects to a VictoriaMetrics server and selects a tenant
* [ ] Rules are ingested and searchable in cognee
* [ ] A repeat sync of an unchanged server changes nothing
* [ ] A rule removed upstream is removed from the graph on the next sync
* [ ] README with setup steps and a runnable example
* [ ] Tests covering the ingest path, an unchanged sync and a removed rule

### Alternatives Considered

* Pointing the Prometheus connector at VictoriaMetrics. It may partly work, but the tenant, the rule ids and the field names differ, and #5424 lists it as untested
* One shared connector for both. That would be the cleanest result, and I am happy to build this as an addition to the Prometheus connector if the maintainers prefer that

### Use Case

* Pointing the Prometheus connector at VictoriaMetrics. It may partly work, but the tenant, the rule ids and the field names differ, and #5424 lists it as untested
* One shared connector for both. That would be the cleanest result, and I am happy to build this as an addition to the Prometheus connector if the maintainers prefer that

### Implementation Ideas

Path B from the integration guide. dlt's REST source on the document path, with its own dataset and the rule id as the primary key. Text is written the same way every time, so a repeat sync creates no duplicates.

Tests on recorded responses, including the removal of the last rule, then a real run against a local VictoriaMetrics.

### Additional Context

Part of Mergetober. I would like to build this if it is accepted.

### Pre-submission Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues to ensure this feature hasn't been requested already
- [x] I have provided a clear problem statement and proposed solution
- [x] I have described my specific use case

items.title: One-ticket-per-finding push worker with dedup and idempotency

milestone.title: M7 - Triage, Reporting & Integrations
milestone.description: Triage (Gate 3), report export, tracker integrations, remediation & retest, baseline diff.

items.body:
## Summary
Push released findings to configured connectors exactly once each, tracked in `ticket_links`, with dedup (never two tickets for one finding/connector), idempotency and retries/backoff. Triggered when a finding is released (TRIAGE) and when a connector is newly linked to existing released findings.

## Context
`apps/worker` connectors activity (Temporal/BullMQ, WORKFLOW). `ticket_links` (§7) records finding↔ticket. Secrets resolved via SECRETS at push time (§8.7). Advances F27. Mirrors the "report the PoC/ticket" delivery of released findings.

## Scope
**In scope**: `ticket_links` schema/model; the push job (trigger on release); dedup; idempotency; retry/backoff/DLQ; update-on-change.
**Out of scope**: provider HTTP (CONNECT-005/006/007); inbound sync (CONNECT-008); mapping (CONNECT-003).

## Detailed requirements
1. `ticket_links` columns: `id uuid` (pk), `public_id text` (`tkl_`), `tenant_id uuid not null` (RLS), `finding_id uuid not null`, `connector_id uuid not null`, `external_id text`, `url text`, `provider_status text`, `last_pushed_at timestamptz`, `last_synced_at timestamptz`, `state text` (`pending|created|update_failed|create_failed`), base columns; unique `(tenant_id, finding_id, connector_id)` — the dedup guarantee.
2. On `finding.released` (TRIAGE audit/event or outbox), enqueue a push job per active connector bound to the finding's asset/tenant.
3. Push job: upsert `ticket_links` with a unique constraint acquiring intent; if no `external_id`, resolve secret → `buildTicketPayload` (CONNECT-003) → `createTicket`; store `external_id`/`url`. If `external_id` exists → `updateTicket` with changed fields only.
4. Idempotency: the unique constraint + an idempotency key (`finding_id:connector_id:contentHash`) ensures replays/duplicate events never create a second ticket.
5. Retries: exponential backoff on `CONNECTOR_RATE_LIMITED` (honouring `retryAfter`) and `CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_ERROR`; after max attempts → DLQ + `create_failed`/`update_failed` state + alert (NOTIFY).
6. Linking a connector later re-enqueues pushes for all currently released findings on its assets (bounded, fair).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Releasing a finding creates exactly one ticket per active connector; a replayed event creates none extra (dedup/idempotency).
- [ ] A changed finding updates the existing ticket, not a new one.
- [ ] Rate-limit responses back off and eventually succeed; permanent failures land in the DLQ with a `*_failed` state and an alert.
- [ ] Cross-tenant: a connector only receives its own tenant's findings.
- [ ] `ticket_links` unique constraint prevents duplicate rows under concurrency.

## Edge cases & failure modes
- Two release events for one finding (bulk + single) → single ticket (unique constraint).
- Connector deactivated between release and push → job skips with a recorded reason.
- Upstream creates the ticket but the response is lost → next attempt detects via the `finding:<publicId>` marker search (CONNECT-003) before creating, avoiding a duplicate.
- Secret rotated mid-flight → resolve fresh each attempt.
- Finding un-released (returned) → do not delete the ticket; sync updates status (CONNECT-008).
- Kill switch / tenant suspended → pushes pause; resume on re-enable.

## Security, privacy & audit
- Secrets resolved per attempt, in-memory only (§8.7); never logged.
- Audit `ticket.created|updated|push_failed` with finding/connector/external id (§8.8).
- Tenant isolation on `ticket_links` + job routing (§8.6).

## Observability
- Metric `connector_push_total{provider,result}`, `connector_push_retries`, `connector_dlq_total`; histogram `connector_push_ms`; log `findingPublicId`, `connectorPublicId`, `externalId`.
- Trace span `connector.push`.

## Test plan
- Unit: dedup/idempotency key; retry/backoff policy; update-vs-create decision.
- Integration (FakeConnector): release→one ticket; replay→no dup; rate-limit backoff; DLQ on permanent failure; concurrency unique-constraint; cross-tenant routing.

## Dependencies
Blocked by: CONNECT-001, CONNECT-003, FINDING, TRIAGE (release trigger), WORKFLOW, AUDIT. Related: CONNECT-005/006/007, CONNECT-008, NOTIFY (alerts), SECRETS.

## Implementation notes for Claude Code
Make the `(tenant_id, finding_id, connector_id)` unique constraint the dedup backbone; search by the `finding:<publicId>` marker before create to recover from lost responses. Resolve secrets per attempt. Trigger from the finding-released event/outbox, not from the HTTP handler.

items.title: Connector config model, schema, secrets-by-reference and connection test

milestone.title: M7 - Triage, Reporting & Integrations
milestone.description: Triage (Gate 3), report export, tracker integrations, remediation & retest, baseline diff.

items.body:
## Summary
Model connector configuration (`connectors` table) with per-provider settings, credentials held by secret reference (§8.7), and a config CRUD + connection-test API. This is where a tenant registers "push to this Jira project / this GitHub repo / this GitLab project" without any secret ever touching the database in plaintext.

## Context
`apps/api` connectors module + `packages/db`/`packages/domain`. Secrets via SECRETS (`secret_ref`, write-only API, §8.7). `connectors` is a tenant table with RLS (§7). The admin UI that calls this lives in ADMIN. Advances F27.

## Scope
**In scope**: `connectors` schema/model/repo; Zod config per provider; CRUD API; connection-test action using the connector's `testConnection`; secret-by-reference storage.
**Out of scope**: the abstraction (CONNECT-001); mapping (CONNECT-003); push (CONNECT-004); UI (ADMIN).

## Detailed requirements
1. `connectors` columns: `id uuid` (UUIDv7 pk), `public_id text` (`con_` prefix), `tenant_id uuid not null` (RLS), `type text not null` (`jira|github|gitlab`), `name text`, `config jsonb not null` (non-secret: base URL, project key/repo, default labels), `secret_ref text not null` (SECRETS reference to the token), `default_mapping_id uuid null`, `active boolean not null default true`, base columns; unique `(tenant_id, type, name)`.
2. Per-provider config Zod schemas: Jira `{ baseUrl, projectKey, issueType }`; GitHub `{ owner, repo, apiBaseUrl? }`; GitLab `{ baseUrl, projectId }`; validated at write.
3. CRUD API (`apps/api`): `POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE /v1/connectors`; secrets are supplied write-only (a token value in the create/update request is stored via the SECRETS write-only API and replaced by a `secret_ref`; the value is never returned or persisted in `config`).
4. `POST /v1/connectors/{id}/test` → resolves the secret (SECRETS), calls `connector.testConnection`, returns `{ ok, detail }`; never leaks the token.
5. Authz: `connector:manage` permission + Cedar; tenant-scoped.
6. Soft rules: deactivating a connector stops future pushes but keeps `ticket_links`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pnpm db:migrate` creates `connectors` with RLS and the unique constraint.
- [ ] Creating a connector stores the token via SECRETS and persists only a `secret_ref`; GET never returns the token.
- [ ] `POST /v1/connectors/{id}/test` returns ok for valid creds and a typed error for bad creds, without leaking the token.
- [ ] Cross-tenant connector access → 404.
- [ ] Per-provider config validation rejects malformed config.

## Edge cases & failure modes
- Token rotation → update replaces the secret via SECRETS (new version); old `ticket_links` keep working.
- Invalid base URL / unreachable host on test → `CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_ERROR`, no stored state change.
- Duplicate `(type,name)` → 409.
- Deleting a connector with existing `ticket_links` → soft-deactivate or block hard delete (configurable; default deactivate) with audit.
- Missing/garbled secret_ref → push/test fail closed.

## Security, privacy & audit
- Secrets by reference only; resolved in-memory at test/push; never logged or returned (§8.7).
- Audit `connector.created|updated|deleted|tested` (§8.8); test result records ok/fail, never the token.
- RLS + Cedar; cross-tenant denied (§8.6).

## Observability
- Metric `connector_config_ops_total{op,result}`, `connector_test_total{provider,result}`; log `connectorPublicId`, `provider` (no secrets).

## Test plan
- Unit: per-provider config schemas; secret-write-only flow.
- Integration: CRUD + RLS; test action with FakeConnector success/failure; cross-tenant 404; token never returned.

## Dependencies
Blocked by: CONNECT-001, SECRETS, DB. Related: CONNECT-003..008, ADMIN (UI), AUDIT.

## Implementation notes for Claude Code
Store only non-secret config in `config`; route every token through the SECRETS write-only API and keep just the `secret_ref`. Resolve secrets only inside the worker/test call. Add a test asserting GET responses never contain token material.

items.title: bug(connector): PostgreSQL CDC treats PRIMARY KEY INCLUDE columns as key columns
items.body:
## Describe the bug

When RisingWave auto-derives the schema of a PostgreSQL CDC table, primary-key discovery matches every attribute in `pg_index.indkey`:

```sql
JOIN pg_attribute a
  ON a.attrelid = i.indrelid
 AND a.attnum = ANY(i.indkey)
```

However, PostgreSQL stores both key attributes and non-key `INCLUDE` payload attributes in `indkey`. Only the first `indnkeyatts` entries are actual key columns.

As a result, for an upstream constraint such as:

```sql
PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, order_id) INCLUDE (payload)
```

RisingWave discovers `tenant_id, order_id, payload` as the primary key instead of `tenant_id, order_id`. The extra column can then become part of the RisingWave primary/distribution key and CDC snapshot pagination even though PostgreSQL does not enforce uniqueness on it and does not consider it part of the primary key.

The relevant query is:

https://github.com/risingwavelabs/risingwave/blob/c4a578bb71145dab308d64c676d8009033b00d01/src/connector/src/connector_common/postgres.rs#L44-L54

## Error message/log

```text
No error is reported. Schema discovery returns included payload columns as primary-key columns.
```

## To Reproduce

1. Create a PostgreSQL table with an included column in its primary-key index:

```sql
CREATE TABLE public.orders (
    tenant_id INT NOT NULL,
    order_id INT NOT NULL,
    payload TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, order_id) INCLUDE (payload)
);
```

2. Confirm PostgreSQL's index metadata:

```sql
SELECT
    a.attname,
    array_position(i.indkey, a.attnum) AS index_position,
    i.indnkeyatts
FROM pg_index i
JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.indrelid
JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
JOIN pg_attribute a
  ON a.attrelid = i.indrelid
 AND a.attnum = ANY(i.indkey)
WHERE n.nspname = 'public'
  AND c.relname = 'orders'
  AND i.indisprimary
ORDER BY index_position;
```

This returns all three attributes, while `indnkeyatts` is `2`.

3. Create a PostgreSQL CDC source and auto-derived table:

```sql
CREATE TABLE orders_cdc (*)
FROM pg_source TABLE 'public.orders';
```

4. Run:

```sql
DESCRIBE orders_cdc;
```

The derived primary key includes `payload`.

## Expected behavior

RisingWave should discover only the actual PostgreSQL primary-key attributes and preserve their index order:

```text
tenant_id, order_id
```

Primary-key discovery should restrict `indkey` to its first `indnkeyatts` entries. For example, it could filter on:

```sql
array_position(i.indkey, a.attnum) <= i.indnkeyatts
```

or use `unnest(i.indkey) WITH ORDINALITY` and retain ordinals through `indnkeyatts`.

PostgreSQL documents that `indkey` contains `indnatts` entries, including payload attributes, while only `indnkeyatts` entries are key columns:

https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/catalog-pg-index.html

## How did you deploy RisingWave?

Found by code inspection.

## The version of RisingWave

Current `main` at `c4a578bb71145dab308d64c676d8009033b00d01`.

## Additional context

This is adjacent to, but different from, #26846. PostgreSQL CDC already preserves composite primary-key index order with `ORDER BY array_position(i.indkey, a.attnum)`; the problem here is that the query does not exclude non-key `INCLUDE` attributes.

Vulnerability Details

MariaDB Connector/J is used to connect applications developed in Java to MariaDB and MySQL databases. From 3.0.0 until 3.3.7, 3.4.5, and 3.5.11, the ClientMessage.validateLocalFileName() check used a regular expression that could match LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE text inside quoted identifiers, string literals, or comments instead of requiring a real statement. A malicious or compromised server, or a machine-in-the-middle attacker, could return crafted database or table identifiers that the connector reused in metadata or updatable-result queries, then answer with a LOCAL INFILE request for a client file. With allowLocalInfile enabled, this caused the connector to stream any readable client-host file named by the crafted text, including through DatabaseMetaData.getImportedKeys(), DatabaseMetaData.getExportedKeys(), or ResultSet.updateRow() paths. This issue is fixed in versions 3.3.7, 3.4.5, and 3.5.11.

items.title: Task: classification editing: the approver sees what a pattern hits, one-thing doors match one thing, and three smaller fixes
items.body:
## What changes

Five small gaps in the editing of operation classifications are closed. They were found in the planning check of the change for #6038. They must be done before the switch `POLICY_CLASSIFICATION` is turned on in any install.

## The change

1. **The approver sees what a pattern edit hits.** The approval card of a `policy.classify` request made with a pattern shows the number of operations the pattern matches now, the first matches (up to a small limit, with "and N more"), and one sentence that the pattern also matches operations added later. The count is stored on the request when it is made (`bulk.py`, about lines 229-234).
2. **The doors for one thing match one thing.** The routes and tools that edit one connector, one group or one operation use the id as plain text, not as a pattern: wildcards (`*`, `?`, `[`) in the path or the argument are escaped or refused (`connectors_ingest.py` about 1480-1486 and 1566-1578, `policy_classification.py` about 403-409, `_connector_classification.py:126`).
3. **The admin MCP edit tools refuse `tenant_id` together with `category` or `labels`** (`connector_admin.py` about 526-534 and 609-617). Today the classification edit silently uses the caller's tenant.
4. **The dry run shows the value in force.** Next to the classification's own values, the console table and the preview rows show what applies after the minimum-level rules (`policy_classification.py:145`, `_classify_result.html` about 79-81). So "always wait: yes → no" does not look like the wait is gone when a minimum-level rule keeps it.
5. **Console details.** The "Category" column on the override page shows only when the switch is on (`ui/templates/connectors/overrides.html`). A person who is not an admin gets the right 403 text on `/ui/policy/classify`. The page text says what an install-wide row means. Fix the wrong comment in `_classify_result.html` about `hx-headers`.

## Acceptance

- A test per point: the card of a `*` edit shows the count and the sentence; a wildcard on a one-thing door is refused or matches only the literal id; `tenant_id` with `category` is refused; the dry run of an operation with a minimum-level rule shows that it still waits; with the switch off the override page has no "Category" column.
- `docs/codebase/policy-classification.md` says points 1, 2 and 4.

This changes how policy edits are shown and checked. The pull request waits for the planning session's check of the changes before it merges.

Code repo: evoila/meho
Ready for coding: yes

items.title: [Backlog] AlertRuleV2: /v2 alert rules with selectors, metric_key and declared quality policy
items.body:
## Context

V4 §9.2 schedules `AlertRuleV2` with "Telemetry v2". §7.3, §16.2 and §16.3 define the rule target as a selector (`asset | device | component | probe | integration | site`) with `metric_key` or health condition keys and a declared quality policy (`require_quality`, `allow_suspect`, `minimum_confidence`, `on_insufficient_data`). §19.2 lists `GET/POST /v2/tenants/{tenant_id}/alert-rules` and `GET /v2/tenants/{tenant_id}/alert-events`.

## Decision (P2 plan r2, D17)

This work is deferred from Epic #22 (P2). P2 delivers only the `/v1`-rule read adapter on `observation_numeric` (#71), which matches §24 Phase 2 "move the v2 alert adapter first" and §16.4. A generalized rule needs inputs that only exist after P3 (#15) and P6 (#17):
- health condition keys (`health.telemetry_stale`, `health.device_offline`, …);
- non-null quality confidence;
- calibration states;
- connector health.

Until then, native v2 probes are visible through `/v2` reads but do not drive alerts (D12).

## Entry gate

- [ ] #22 complete: the `observation_numeric` schema, the v2 window reader and parity are proven.
- [ ] #15 complete: trusted ingress, last-seen and connector health are available.
- [ ] #17 decisions: the quality/confidence semantics and the calibration states are frozen.
- [ ] A design is approved for rule selector storage (keys, no Scan), evaluator selector resolution, and migration of `/v1` rules (§16.4: preserve rule IDs, versions and current events).

## Scope (to be decomposed later)

- `/v2/alert-rules` CRUD with selectors and a declared quality policy.
- Evaluator selector resolution: asset/component/probe → series. Native probes become eligible.
- A `/v1` rule migration adapter that preserves IDs, versions and events.
- Health and connector condition families.

Refs #22, #15, #17, #14

### Problem Statement

cognee has no Microsoft-identity connector. Tenants run on Entra ID (users, groups, app registrations, sign-in/audit logs) and that knowledge ("who is Guest vs Member, which service principals own which apps, what sign-ins failed?") never reaches memory.

### Proposed Solution

Add an `entra` connector in cognee-community, following the shape of the existing connectors, over Microsoft Graph v1.0.

- **Auth**: OAuth2 client credentials (`ENTRA_TENANT_ID`, `ENTRA_CLIENT_ID`, `ENTRA_CLIENT_SECRET`), scopes `User.Read.All`, `Group.Read.All`, `Application.Read.All`, `AuditLog.Read.All`. No review for own tenant.
- **Ingest**: users (UPN, displayName, accountEnabled, userType), groups + transitive members, applications/service principals, sign-in logs + audit logs. One document per user (groups + apps folded); logs folded per user-day.
- **Selection**: `include_users/groups/apps/logs`, `user_type=["Member"]`, `sign_in_days=30`.
- **Incremental sync**: `$filter=... gt {cursor}` + `$orderby` + `@odata.nextLink` paging; **delta queries** (`/users/delta`, `/groups/delta` with `$deltatoken`) for true deltas including tombstones. Per-doc hash skips unchanged.
- **Forget-on-delete**: delta tombstones (`@removed`) map to deletes; full-snapshot fallback purges orphans. Empty-page-with-state aborts.
- **Privacy**: UPNs columns-only with hash in prose; client secrets/keys never fetched.

items.title: [Feature Request]: [Python/YAML] Add schema-aware Deduplicate transform in Beam YAML with key columns, time domain, and duration
items.body:
### Description

Deduplicating streaming at-least-once deliveries (e.g. from Pub/Sub, Kafka, or webhook retries) by one or more business columns (`event_id`, `[tenant_id, order_id]`) is one of the most common streaming requirements.

Currently:
1. `apache_beam.transforms.deduplicate.DeduplicatePerKey` / `Deduplicate` only operates on raw `(K, V)` pairs or full serialized elements, rather than named `beam.Row` schema columns while preserving the full input `Row` schema and element timestamp.
2. Beam YAML has **no** built-in `Deduplicate` transform provider, forcing users out of declarative YAML for basic idempotency.

### Proposed YAML & Python API

```yaml
pipeline:
  transforms:
    - type: Deduplicate
      input: ReadFromPubSub
      config:
        keys: [tenant_id, event_id]
        duration: 10m
        time_domain: processing_time   # or event_time
```

### Key Capabilities
1. **Schema-Preserving Composite Keys**: Deduplicate `beam.Row` streams by one or more key columns (`keys: [...]`), deterministically serializing composite/nullable keys while preserving input `RowTypeConstraint` and element event-time timestamps.
2. **Stateful TTL**: Use `ReadModifyWriteStateSpec` + `TimerSpec(TimeDomain.REAL_TIME | TimeDomain.WATERMARK)` to bound per-key state memory to `duration` without leaking Windmill/Flink state.
3. **Observability**: Emit standard Beam counters (`deduplicate_kept`, `deduplicate_dropped`) so operators can monitor duplicate rates in Dataflow/Flink.

items.body:
> 🤖 **Automated Agent Report** — *Google Antigravity Pair Programmer*
> **Part of Epic**: #345

## 1. Objective & Architectural Rationale
Enable frictionless human-to-agent and agent-to-human file exchange (PDFs, CSV datasets, images, generated reports) directly inside **Kurrier Drive** without requiring non-technical users to open the developer VS Code IDE (`/editor/`) or send oversized email attachments.

By pre-seeding named storage volumes in Kurrier Drive backed by local WebDAV (or optional S3 in cloud appliance mode) mapped to each agent's isolated workspace (`${BRAINSOS_DATA_DIR}/agents/<tenant_id>/workspace/`), files dropped into Kurrier Drive by the operator immediately appear inside the target agent's container at `/workspace/`, and artifacts exported by agents can be previewed or downloaded inline in the browser.

## 2. Scope & Key Touchpoints
1. **Local WebDAV Sidecar / Endpoint for Agent Workspaces (`docker/compose/compose.apps.yml`, `docker/kurrier/`)**:
   - Configure a lightweight internal WebDAV endpoint (or Kurrier's native WebDAV storage connector) mounted to `${BRAINSOS_AGENTS_DIR:-../../data/agents}` (and legacy `${BRAINSOS_AGENT_WORKSPACES_DIR}` fallback per Rule 9).
   - Expose per-agent workspace roots (`/agents/<tenant_id>/workspace/`) while strictly excluding `/memories` mounts so binary uploads can **never** pollute the Open Knowledge Format (OKF) Markdown memory plane (**Rule 1**).
2. **Idempotent Kurrier Drive Volume Seeding (`scripts/setup/setup-kurrier.sh`)**:
   - Dynamically read active fleet tenants from `config/default_settings/agents.yaml` and `${BRAINSOS_DATA_DIR}/settings/agents.yaml`.
   - Seed Kurrier's PostgreSQL storage volume tables with named Drive volumes for each agent (e.g., `Terrastella Workspace`, `Bawtford Workspace`, `Marvin Workspace`, `Operator Workspace`) plus a general `Shared Operator Drive` (`${BRAINSOS_COMMS_DIR}/kurrier/drive`).
3. **File Permissions & Multi-Tenant Boundary Enforcement (Rule 4 & Rule 9)**:
   - Ensure UID/GID mapping (`PUID`/`PGID`) allows seamless read/write between Kurrier Drive and the stateless agent runner (`hermes-runner`) inside each tenant's `/workspace`.
   - Enforce strict path traversal protection so a tenant's workspace volume cannot escape into another tenant's partition or `/memories`.
4. **Automated Verification (`scripts/verify/verify-kurrier.sh`)**:
   - Add an end-to-end test uploading a sample file via Kurrier Drive / WebDAV into an agent's workspace volume and verifying its immediate presence on disk in `agents/<tenant_id>/workspace/` and **zero** presence in `agents/<tenant_id>/memories/`.

## 3. Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every agent defined in `agents.yaml` automatically appears as a named folder/volume in **Kurrier Drive** on first boot.
- [ ] Dropping a file (PDF, PNG, CSV) into an agent's Drive volume makes it immediately readable/writable by that agent inside `/workspace`, and files written by the agent to `/workspace` render inline previews in Kurrier Drive.
- [ ] **Rule 1 Enforcement**: Zero binary uploads, WebDAV temp files, or Drive metadata ever touch `/memories` (`agents/<tenant_id>/memories/`).
- [ ] **Rule 9 Enforcement**: Path boundaries prevent cross-tenant leakage or traversal outside `workspace/`.

items.title: Hackathon [Feature]:  Add Power BI metadata and lineage connector
items.body:
### Problem Statement

**Power BI** has no cognee connector. Power BI workspaces contain reports, dashboards, semantic models, tables, columns, measures, data sources, and lineage that describe how an organization produces and consumes analytics. This metadata is already graph-shaped, but it is difficult to search across workspaces or use when investigating the impact of a data-model change.


### Use Case

A data team maintains dozens of Power BI reports built from shared semantic models and upstream databases. After syncing their metadata into cognee, an engineer can ask which reports depend on a particular table, where a measure is defined, who owns an affected workspace, and which dashboards may break when an upstream data source changes.

### Proposed Solution

Add a `power-bi` connector under `packages/connector/power-bi/` in cognee-community, following the existing pull-based connectors and using the Power BI Scanner REST APIs.

- **Auth:** a Microsoft Entra service principal using a tenant ID, client ID, and client secret. A Fabric administrator enables service-principal access to read-only admin APIs and the tenant settings for detailed metadata scanning.
- **Select:** explicit workspace IDs or workspace IDs returned by `GetModifiedWorkspaces`. Scans are submitted in batches of at most 100 workspace IDs, matching the Scanner API limit.
- **Ingest:** readable documents for workspaces, reports, report pages, dashboards, semantic models, tables, columns, measures, DAX and mashup expressions, and data sources. Stable Power BI IDs, web URLs, ownership, endorsement status, tags, and sensitivity labels are retained as metadata.
- **Relationships:** preserve lineage such as `data source → semantic model → report → dashboard`, together with workspace membership, table-to-column, table-to-measure, and upstream dataflow relationships.
- **Incremental sync:** call `GetModifiedWorkspaces` and scan only workspaces changed since the last successful cursor. Submit the asynchronous scan, poll `GetScanStatus`, and retrieve `GetScanResult` only after the scan reports `Succeeded`. Advance the cursor only after every requested workspace has been processed successfully.
- **Forget-on-delete:** maintain a complete snapshot for every selected workspace with `write_disposition="replace"`. Reports, dashboards, semantic models, and subartifacts disappear only after a successful scan confirms they are absent. Failed, timed-out, throttled, or unauthorized scans preserve the previous snapshot.

### Watch out for

Detailed semantic-model metadata and DAX or mashup expressions require tenant settings that only a Fabric administrator can enable. Service-principal authentication for the read-only admin APIs has different permission rules from delegated administrator authentication and must follow Microsoft's documented setup. Scan results are asynchronous, are available for a limited period, and are subject to request limits. Arbitrary DAX query execution and ingestion of report data are outside the first version because they introduce separate capacity, tenant-setting, throttling, and row-level-security requirements.

### Package layout to follow

```text
packages/connector/power-bi/
├── README.md
├── cognee_community_connector_power_bi/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   └── power_bi.py
├── examples/
├── tests/
└── pyproject.toml
```

### Acceptance Criteria

- A user selects explicit workspace IDs or enables modified-workspace discovery
- Authentication uses a Microsoft Entra service principal and read-only Scanner REST APIs
- Workspaces, reports, pages, dashboards, semantic models, tables, columns, measures, expressions, and data sources are rendered as readable documents
- Power BI IDs, source URLs, owners, endorsements, tags, and sensitivity labels are retained as metadata when returned by the API
- Data-source, semantic-model, report, dashboard, and subartifact relationships are preserved
- Modified-workspace discovery avoids rescanning unchanged workspaces
- The connector polls asynchronous scans and commits data only after a `Succeeded` status
- Removed artifacts disappear only after a complete successful workspace scan
- Authentication, throttling, timeout, and server failures preserve the previous snapshot and cursor
- README with Entra registration, Fabric tenant-setting requirements, and a runnable example under `examples/`
- Mocked tests covering authentication, workspace batching, scan polling, metadata rendering, lineage, incremental discovery, deletion, and failed scans
- An optional live test exercises the connector against a configured Power BI or Microsoft Fabric tenant

items.body:
## Contexto
O analista de plantão precisa saber do Incidente crítico no celular. O PWA de #9 viabiliza o push.

## Escopo
- `alert_rules (tenant_id, id, name, enabled, conditions jsonb, channels jsonb, quiet_hours jsonb)`. Condições:
  - Incidente aberto ou atualizado com severidade ≥ X, Ambiente e Integração;
  - taxa de erro acima de Y% por N min;
  - Conector em `failing`;
  - Diagnóstico publicado aguardando revisão por mais de N min.
- `notification_channels (tenant_id, id, type check in ('email','slack','teams','webpush'), config, secret_id)`. Slack via app OAuth; Teams via Incoming Webhook ou Workflows; e-mail transacional.
- `push_subscriptions (tenant_id, user_id, endpoint, keys, user_agent)`: Web Push com VAPID e suporte a iOS 16.4+ quando o PWA está instalado.
- Worker `notifier`: consome `incident.*`, `diagnosis.published` e `connector.failing`; avalia as regras; aplica deduplicação e agrupamento (1 notificação por Incidente a cada 15 min) e horário de silêncio (exceto crítico).
- Mensagens com link direto para o Incidente e **sem dados sensíveis** no corpo (apenas título, severidade e Integração).
- **Tela 20:** regras com toggle, canais do usuário e silêncio fora do plantão.

## UI — Tela 20
```text
┌──────────────────────────┐
│ ← Alertas          v0.3  │
│ Incidente crítico prd [on]│
│  → Push, Slack, Jira     │
│ Erro > 5% por 10 min [on]│
│ Meus canais              │
│ Push neste dispositivo ✓ │
│ Silêncio 22:00–07:00     │
└──────────────────────────┘
```

## Critérios de aceite
- **Dado** um Incidente crítico em prd, **então** o push chega em < 60 s ao celular com o PWA instalado.
- **Dado** 37 Execuções no mesmo Incidente, **então** há 1 notificação, não 37.

#9, #20, #24

items.title: P0: Establish canonical Cataran platform contracts and ownership before three-plane release
items.body:
## Why this is a release blocker

The current audit cannot find the planned `ugai-platform-contracts` or `ugai-platform-admin` repositories through the installed GitHub search. UGAI, IM19 and Notebook already carry overlapping task, identity, approval, event and artifact contracts. A 404/search miss is not proof a private/alternate repository does not exist, and this issue does not authorize creating a new repository.

## Required Master Architect decision

1. Identify and accept one canonical home for versioned platform contracts (existing repo, new repo, or a controlled transitional directory).
2. Assign a contract owner and change-control process. Runtime repositories consume versioned contracts; they must not independently redefine them.
3. Publish schema packages/specifications for:
   - Identity / Principal / Tenant / Membership / Project
   - Task / TaskState / TaskEvent / Idempotency
   - Approval / ApprovalReceipt / SideEffectPolicy
   - MCP connection / tool invocation / audit
   - A2A dispatch / callback
   - Evidence / provenance / artifact
   - Audit / outbox / replication / error envelope
4. Define stable identifiers, issuer/subject semantics, tenant scoping, actor semantics, timestamps, digest formats, version compatibility and deprecation policy.
5. Build language-appropriate generated/client types and contract test fixtures.
6. Publish a consumer matrix showing UGAI, IM19, Notebook, Cloudbrowser, RAG_Cerdas and Android Connector versions.
7. Add schema compatibility CI and a migration/rollback plan before changing runtime contracts.

## Initial observed conflicts

- Notebook API membership uses (tenant_id, subject, status), while Supabase Auth membership uses (tenant_id, user_id UUID) with a distinct role vocabulary.
- UGAI PR #23 carries a durable task/approval contract and IM19 client adapter.
- IM19 PR #33 has its own gateway/connector DTOs.
- Cloudbrowser task dispatch and callback need to use the same task/event identities.
- RAG_Cerdas provenance and artifact references need a stable evidence contract.

## Acceptance gates

- One reviewed schema source and a consumer compatibility matrix.
- Golden fixtures validated by every active repo's CI.
- Breaking contract changes fail CI until an explicit version bump and migration path exists.
- No duplicate MCP gateway responsibility.
- Architecture Owner review and exact-SHA CI results before production use.

## Scope / safety

No repository is created or renamed by this issue. Do not merge or deploy cross-repo runtime changes until the canonical contract location and ownership decision is recorded.

Library home page: https://mariadb.com/kb/en/mariadb/about-mariadb-connector-j/

Found in HEAD commit: 2ac4b7b0a321e6c4dcd73ed502a4c4c8028acb7c

Found in base branch: main

Vulnerability Details

MariaDB Connector/J is used to connect applications developed in Java to MariaDB and MySQL databases. From 3.0.0 until 3.3.7, 3.4.5, and 3.5.11, decoders for OK packet session-state blocks, column definition packets, text row data, or binary row data used server-declared lengths without confirming that the requested bytes remained in the receive buffer. The decoders could position reads, create sub-buffers, or decode strings beyond the packet boundary. A malicious or compromised server, or a machine-in-the-middle attacker, could trigger unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException or IllegalArgumentException failures inside JDBC calls and terminate connection handling. This issue is fixed in versions 3.3.7, 3.4.5, and 3.5.11.

items.title: go2 sync — drive the connector from the CLI
items.body:
**Why now.** `gdrive.py` is orphaned: 282 lines and 23 tests, imported by nothing. This ticket is the wiring, not new connector logic.

**Design.** `go2 sync --source gdrive [--limit N]`. Reuses the existing job queue and `ingest_document` — **no new ingestion path** (architectural invariant 2). Scope every write through `Scope(tenant_id, connection_id, source)` as local ingestion already does.

**Test cases**
- `test_synced_files_go_through_the_same_pipeline` — documents land with the same fields as a local ingest
- `test_sync_is_scoped_to_the_active_tenant` — a second workspace sees nothing
- `test_limit_stops_early` — `--limit 1` fetches exactly one
- `test_an_unsupported_file_is_skipped_not_failed` — status reflects skip, queue continues
- `test_one_bad_file_does_not_abort_the_run` — per-document boundary holds, as for local ingest
- `test_source_is_recorded_as_gdrive` — `list_documents(source="gdrive")` finds them

items.title: feat(model): each connection's terms get a display name, description and hidden flag on a Model page that survives a schema refresh

milestone.title: v1.9 — Analyst layer, authoring & sharing
milestone.description: Features and improvements, after the v1.6 connector core: the launch asks that are already built (copy a filtered link, dashboard tags, schema browser, guided query builder), the chart benchmark, the one-line installer, the NeoDash migration post and build-time docs diagrams, plus the bugs deferred from v1.5 and the code, test and CI cleanup. #1717 merges after #1714 and is rebased onto the v1.6 connector contract. The rest of Dependabot #1625 and #1494 is reshipped first-party here.

items.body:
## Problem

The connector's model exists in the product only as autocomplete. An analyst cannot see what a connection holds, nothing anywhere says what `cast_size` or `released` means, and a generated query has nothing to be grounded on. Owner vision, 2026-11-08 (vault `product/Vision.md`): the model is an **ontology**, per connection now, designed so a cross-connection layer can be added later.

## Today

1. Open a connection: no model view.
2. Open the widget editor: labels and columns appear only while typing.
3. `GET /api/connections/[id]/schema` (`SchemaManager.fetchSchema` → `use-schema` / `schema-store`) returns labels, relationship types and properties, or tables and columns. Nothing stores a description, a display name or a unit; a refresh forgets everything.

## Cause

Introspection was built for completion. There is no persistence for meaning, and no UI that reads the schema as a thing in itself.

## Expected

- A **Model tab on the connection page**: entities (labels or tables), relationships (relationship types; foreign keys where the connector reports them), properties with their type. Anyone who can use the connection reads it; creators and admins edit **display name, description, synonyms, unit, hidden** per term.
- The schema browser panel in the editor (#1693) shows the same names and descriptions; the builder (#1696) and query generation read the ontology, hidden terms excluded.
- An introspection refresh keeps annotations: terms are matched by a stable key (connection, kind, name, parent); a term that vanished is flagged as orphaned, not deleted.
- One ontology per connection. The key design leaves room for a later `concepts` layer mapping terms across connections; nothing of it is built now.

## Fix (default; the owner can override in a comment)

- One table `ontology_terms` (`tenant_id`, `connection_id`, `kind` entity|relationship|property, `key`, `parent_key`, `display_name`, `description`, `synonyms text[]`, `unit`, `hidden`, `orphaned_at`), unique on (`tenant_id`, `connection_id`, `kind`, `key`, `parent_key`). Ponytail: one table, not three; split when a kind grows its own columns.
- `GET /api/connections/[id]/ontology` merges introspection (structure) with stored terms (meaning); `PUT` upserts terms. Tenant filter per query; `usableConnection` for reads, creator/admin for writes.
- Model tab in `app/` from kit pieces (`SettingsSection`, `List`/`ListRow`, `Field`), inline editing, search, "show hidden" toggle. Relationships for SQL from foreign keys when `fetchSchema` reports them; otherwise entities and properties only.
- Not chosen: annotations inside the connection's `config` JSON (no per-term queries, invisible to the tenant ratchet). Not chosen: OWL/RDF import or export.
- Out of scope: the builder, generation, the chat, the Explore page; cross-connection concepts; changing the database schema.

## Required tests

- Unit (`app/src/lib/ontology/__tests__`): merge of introspection and stored terms: hidden term excluded from the "for generation" view, orphan flagged when introspection loses a term, synonyms round-trip. Each fails without the merge.
- Route tests: tenant filter from the session, `usableConnection` on GET, 403 for a reader on PUT, validation of kinds and keys.
- jsdom: Model tab renders entities and properties from the store; editing a description saves; "show hidden" toggles; empty, loading and error states.
- E2E (demo Neo4j connection): open the Model tab, `Movie` and `Person` listed with `ACTED_IN`; describe `released` as "release year"; open a widget editor on that connection and see the description in the schema panel.

items.title: Task: Azure connector — Entra ID reads: users, groups, directory roles, apps with expiring secrets
items.body:
**What will be true when done:**

- MEHO registers a separate Entra ID connector: product `entra`, implementation `entra-graph-1.0`, plus the wildcard row. A target is one Entra ID tenant.
- `entra.about` answers with the tenant id, its name and its verified domains.
- An agent lists users, groups and directory role assignments.
- An agent lists app registrations with the expiry dates of their secrets and certificates, filtered to those that expire within N days. Secret values and secret hints are never returned.

Ready for coding: not yet (the code is merged in PR #5192; only the live proof on the lab Azure tenant is left)

## What changes and why

- The Azure connector reads Azure resources. Directory objects (users, groups, apps) live in Microsoft Graph (`graph.microsoft.com`), a different API with its own permissions. So Entra ID is its own product.
- The login code from Task #5079 is reused with the scope `https://graph.microsoft.com/.default`. Graph pages with `@odata.nextLink`.
- Microsoft Graph facts (v1.0):
  - Users: `GET /v1.0/users`, permission `User.Read.All`; 100 per page by default, up to 999 with `$top`. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/user-list?view=graph-rest-1.0
  - Groups: `GET /v1.0/groups`, permission `GroupMember.Read.All` or `Group.Read.All`. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/group-list?view=graph-rest-1.0
  - Directory role assignments: `GET /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments`, permission `RoleManagement.Read.Directory`. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/rbacapplication-list-roleassignments?view=graph-rest-1.0
  - App registrations: `GET /v1.0/applications` with `passwordCredentials` and `keyCredentials`, permission `Application.Read.All`.
  - The tenant: `GET /v1.0/organization`.
  - These are application permissions, and each needs admin consent in the tenant. `Directory.Read.All` covers them all but is wider.
  - Graph publishes an official OpenAPI 3 description: https://github.com/microsoftgraph/msgraph-metadata/blob/master/openapi/v1.0/openapi.yaml

## What to build

1. Package `backend/src/meho_backplane/connectors/entra/`: registration (`product="entra"`, `version="1.0"`, `impl_id="entra-graph"`, plus the wildcard row), the connector class on the HTTP base, `host` = `graph.microsoft.com`, extras `tenant_id` and `cloud`, secret `tenant_id`, `client_id`, `client_secret` (an Azure target's secret can be reused).
2. Group `directory`, all `safe`:
   - `entra.about`.
   - `entra.user.list`: id, display name, user principal name, account enabled, user type, created time; optional filters for user type and enabled.
   - `entra.group.list`: id, name, group type, and the member count where it is cheap to get.
   - `entra.role.assignment.list`: role name, principal id and type, scope.
   - `entra.app.list`: app id, name, the nearest secret expiry and the nearest certificate expiry; filter `expiring_within_days`. Never return `secretText` or `hint`.
3. People data: results are tenant data like any other, but tests and docs use made-up names only.
4. The flight-recorder list and the other CI chores. The spec path check runs against the pinned Graph OpenAPI file; if that file is too big for the shelf, record an evidenced exclusion (`docs/decisions/spec-reconcile-guards-standard.md:189-197`). Docs: `docs/codebase/connectors-entra.md` and `docs/cross-repo/entra-onboarding.md` (the permissions and the admin consent).

## Rules

These rules are the same for every Task of this program.

- Typed and multi-step operations only. No spec ingestion. The pinned spec is used only by the CI check that every hand-written path exists.
- Risk level by effect. Reads are `safe`, also read-only POST queries. Starting work on the customer's side is `caution` and needs approval. Role assignment changes and download links are `dangerous` and need approval. No VM power actions and no resource deletes.
- Every operation has a group and `when_to_use` text. A `safe` op id contains no write word (`WRITE_WORDS` in `backend/src/meho_backplane/delete_names.py`, for example `patch`, `run`, `set`, `scale`, `power`, `import`).
- A list over 50 rows or 4 KB comes back as a link to the stored result (a result handle), never as the raw list.
- Secrets never reach audit text, logs, traces or stored results: no tokens, client secrets, download links, keys or connection strings. Text from Azure (names, descriptions, messages) is untrusted data (#5032).
- The operation contract test passes (`backend/tests/test_operation_contracts.py`). Add nothing to `backend/tests/data/operation_contract_gaps.yaml`.
- File layout like `backend/src/meho_backplane/connectors/vra8/`: `_paths.py` (hand-written paths), `typed_reads.py` (operation bodies), `_llm_instructions.py`, `typed_ops.py` (op table, group texts, registrar), and the registrar wired in `__init__.py`. The connector class sits on the HTTP base (`connectors/adapters/http.py`).
- CI chores in the same pull request: `cd cli && make snapshot-openapi && make generate && make cli-docs`; `cd backend && uv run python scripts/generate_reference_docs.py`; the flight-recorder list (`_EXPECTED_TYPED_IMPLS` in `backend/tests/test_flight_recorder_typed_spans.py`) when a new implementation appears; every new vendor path in the spec path check.
- Before the pull request: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests/ -q -n auto`, `uv run ruff check src/ tests/`, `uv run ruff format --check src/ tests/` and `uv run mypy src/` pass. No change to `CHANGELOG.md` (the release pull request adds the line).
- Tests and fixtures use made-up names and ids, never a real tenant, subscription or object id.
- Plain language in code comments, docs and the pull request text.

## Lab proof (done when)

Login (P1) and live read of real objects (P10), on the lab tenant:

- [ ] A tenant admin grants consent for the four Graph permissions to the lab's read-only login. This is needed before the live proof.
- [ ] `entra.about` returns the lab tenant. The token cache keeps the Graph token apart from the Azure token of the same login.
- [ ] Users, groups and role assignments list real objects, and the counts match the Entra admin center. The proof note records counts only, no names.
- [ ] `entra.app.list` shows the lab logins' own app registrations with their secret expiry dates, and no secret value or hint.
- [ ] The result is recorded in the lab proof log, and a comment on this Task says so.

## Depends on

Depends-on: #5081

Parent initiative: #5077

items.title: [feature] a ClickHouse query source for lookup tables

milestone.title: v0.7.0
milestone.description:
**Lookup tables.** Enrich each record in the pipeline from an in-memory table, taking the lookup off the sink's insert path. A table loads before the pipeline starts and reloads in the background, and keeps serving its previous version when a reload fails. Tables come in IP-range and exact-key layouts. They load from object storage or a ClickHouse query, in CSV, TSV, JSON Lines, mmdb or Parquet, and several sources can merge into one table. Each table reports metrics, load events and its status on the admin server.

Tracking issue: #681. No due date until v0.6.0 ships.

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
### What kind

A change to an existing connector

### Which components

ClickHouse sink (spate-clickhouse)

### What you are trying to do, and what stops you

Part of #681. Teams moving enrichment out of ClickHouse often keep the table's data in ClickHouse, where their current dictionary reads it from. A lookup table should be able to load from the same place.

What this adds is a `LoadSource` in `spate-clickhouse`, behind a feature:
- It runs a query and streams the rows as RowBinary into the table's `RowSink`, using the client the sink already has.
- A `version_query` is run each tick, and a load happens only when its result changes. This is the part `invalidate_query` plays for a ClickHouse dictionary.
- Columns map by name, and the key column names its form (`cidr`, `range`, `exact`).

The source lives in `spate-clickhouse` so that the ClickHouse-specific parts, and the docs that name ClickHouse, stay on the connector's own pages.

**Docs.** A `04-connectors/lookups/clickhouse/` page, separate from the sink's page.

**Blocked by:** #686 and #688.

### What the API might look like

```yaml
lookups:
  tenants:
    exact:
      sources:
        - clickhouse:
            query: "SELECT tenant_id, plan, region FROM tenants FINAL"
            version_query: "SELECT max(updated_at) FROM tenants"
            key: { exact: tenant_id }
```

### Semver impact, as best you can tell

Additive — nothing existing changes

### Does this touch any of these?

- [ ] INV-1 — delivery semantics, or anything that could commit a watermark past unacknowledged data
- [x] INV-2 — the source poll loop, which must never block on a channel send
- [ ] INV-3 — the checkpoint tracker, which is synchronous and free of async runtimes
- [ ] INV-5 — the sink intake path, which must not await outside its `select!`
- [ ] INV-6 — adding a connector or 0.x dependency type to a public signature in `spate-core`
- [ ] INV-8, INV-9 or INV-10 — metric naming, cardinality, or gauge ownership

INV-2: the query runs on the I/O runtime, never on a source or driver thread.

### Would you want to implement it?

Yes, if the design is agreed

items.title: MCP connector sign-in: let claude.ai and ChatGPT connect through OAuth
items.body:
With the authorization server in place, make `/mcp` follow the MCP authorization spec. Hosted clients such as claude.ai custom connectors and ChatGPT can then connect with "Connect → sign in → Allow" instead of a pasted token. Phase 1 access tokens (#79) keep working alongside this.

## Resource server (`/mcp`)

- Publish Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728) at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, naming the authorization server and the scopes.
- Answer an unauthenticated request with `401` and a `WWW-Authenticate` header that carries `resource_metadata`.
- Accept two kinds of credential:
  - an OAuth token with the `/mcp` audience (RFC 8707 `resource`)
  - a phase 1 household access token

  Both resolve to the same principal shape: `sub`, `tenant_id`, `role`, scope.

## Client registration

Connectors can't be pre-registered, so support what the current MCP spec revision and the target clients require:

- **Client ID Metadata Documents**, and/or
- **Dynamic Client Registration** (RFC 7591), rate-limited, with registrations that expire if unused.

Check the spec revision and what claude.ai and ChatGPT actually use before choosing.

Treat dynamically registered clients as untrusted. Consent is always shown, and the consent screen shows the client's name **and redirect host**, so a lookalike name can't hide where the code goes.

## Scopes

- `mcp:read` and `mcp:write`, with the same meaning and enforcement as the read-only / read and write choice on household access tokens (#79).
- The consent screen shows which scope the connector asked for, and lets the user grant read only even if write was requested.
- A grant can never exceed the user's current role.

## Gating

The same `Mcp` subscription-feature check as #79, on every request. A tenant without the feature is refused at the consent step and again on each call.

## Acceptance

- Adding Famick as a custom connector in claude.ai completes sign-in and consent, and the tools work.
- The grant appears in Settings and can be revoked. The next call after revoking fails.
- A tenant losing the `Mcp` feature is refused on the next call.

Depends on #80.

items.title: OCR delta sweep (dev/v2.0.0) (PARTIAL) 2026-11-08: 8 findings

labels.name: ocr-sweep
labels.description: Findings from the scheduled Open Code Review (OCR) sweep

items.body:
OCR delta sweep of `dev/v2.0.0` (PARTIAL) found 8 high/critical findings. Full JSON in the run artifact:
https://github.com/cbtw-apac/HarborRAG/actions/runs/42457448133
Some files were not reviewed; the marker was not advanced and they will be retried.

- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/ingestion_control/connection_records.py:48-48`
  All operations in this repository accept a bare caller-supplied `tenant_id` and never receive or validate a `StorageOperationContext`. A caller can therefore pass another tenant's ID to read its documents/tasks or purge its records, bypassing the required storage-boundary tenant check. Require the context on these operations and reject a tenant mismatch rather than treating the ID as authorization.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-app/src/harborrag_app/api/v1/admin/connection_schemas.py:100-102`
  These request models accept raw connector secrets (including arbitrary string values), and `put_connection`/`test_connection` pass them directly into the credential-writing/testing service. This violates the API security rule that HTTP requests must never supply connector credentials and exposes secret material to API request handling and any request telemetry; remove credential values from both HTTP bodies and provide a separate approved provisioning mechanism.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-app/src/harborrag_app/workflow_control/control_plane/connections.py:333-337`
  The default `origin="api"` only blocks new `env:` references; raw strings in secret fields still pass through `_plan_credentials` and are persisted by this writer. The HTTP PUT route supplies those values directly, and `test()` likewise resolves raw form values into a connector. This violates the API rule that requests must not supply connector credentials. Reject raw secret values on API-origin writes/tests (or route clients through a non-secret credential mechanism) before storing or resolving them.
- **critical**  `packages/harborrag-core/src/harborrag_core/domain/connection_snapshot.py:40-40`
  Only `credentials` are checked here. A snapshot can be constructed or restored with sensitive fields in `config` or `tuning`, and `to_json()` persists those values while `secret_refs` only tracks credential references. Validate all three mappings before accepting a snapshot so plaintext secrets cannot enter persisted revisions through these fields.
- **high** bug `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/ingestion_control/connection_records.py:104-109`
  This unconditionally deletes pending/running/paused task rows. The connection-deletion flow checks for an active run before beginning removal, but that check is not synchronized with sync admission/submission; a sync can register its task after the check and continue while this purge removes it. Coordinate deletion with the sync lease or reject/serialize purge while an active task exists so a worker cannot run against a removed task/connection.
- **high** security `packages/harborrag-app/src/harborrag_app/api/ops.py:48-48`
  `ApiSettings.metrics_scrape_token` accepts an empty `SecretStr`. With that configuration, `token` is `b""` and an `Authorization: Bearer ` header passes this comparison, exposing `/metrics` to any caller on the ops port. Reject empty configured tokens or treat an empty token as unset/unauthorized.
- **high** bug `packages/harborrag-app/src/harborrag_app/api/v1/chat/replay.py:43-43`
  Persisted chat idempotency claims keep the request hash across deployments, but the old schema serialized `tenant` and `max_steps` while this schema serializes `tenant_id` and omits `max_steps`. Since existing chat claims are retained, retrying an otherwise identical completed request after upgrade hashes differently and is rejected as a conflict instead of replaying the saved result. Normalize the fingerprint across schema versions (or migrate retained hashes) so the documented safe-retry behavior survives upgrades.
- **high** bug `packages/harborrag-app/src/harborrag_app/workflow_control/control_plane/connections.py:532-534`
  This active-run check is not coordinated with `sync()`: sync acquires `connection-sync:...`, but delete neither acquires that lease nor atomically marks the connection deleting before checking. A sync can pass its checks, then delete can observe no task, mark deleting and start removal while the sync submits/starts its task. Use a shared per-connection guard or an atomic status transition and recheck submissions so ingestion cannot begin after deletion has committed its state.

items.title: CVE-2026-114456 (Medium) detected in snowflake-jdbc-4.0.1.jar
items.body:
## CVE-2026-114456 - Medium Severity Vulnerability
Vulnerable Library - snowflake-jdbc-4.0.1.jar

Snowflake JDBC Driver

Library home page: https://www.snowflake.net/

Sample Path to Dependency File: /trino/plugin/trino-iceberg/pom.xml

Path to vulnerable library: /trino/plugin/trino-iceberg/pom.xml,/trino/plugin/trino-lakehouse/pom.xml,/trino/plugin/trino-snowflake/pom.xml

Found in HEAD commit: 2ac4b7b0a321e6c4dcd73ed502a4c4c8028acb7c

Found in base branch: main

Vulnerability Details

Multiple Snowflake client drivers implementing the "authenticator=externalbrowser" single sign-on flow could have allowed an attacker to interfere with a user's login attempt through weaknesses in the local loopback callback listener used to receive the identity provider's response. The listener reflected an arbitrary request's Origin header into its CORS response headers and accepted the first token-bearing request it received during the login window without verifying a CSRF state value bound to that specific login attempt. An attacker able to reach the listener during an active login might have leveraged this to submit a forged callback response, causing the authentication attempt to fail. The fix is available in Snowflake Connector for Python 4.8.0, Snowflake Go Driver v2.3.0, Snowflake JDBC Driver 4.4.0 (including the snowflake-jdbc-fips and snowflake-jdbc-thin artifacts), Snowflake Node.js Driver 3.4.0, Snowflake Connector for .NET 6.3.0, Snowflake ODBC Driver 4.0.0, Snowflake PHP PDO Driver 4.3.0, and libsnowflakeclient 2.11.1. Go v1 users must migrate to the latest major version of the module. Users must manually upgrade.

items.body:
### Description

```python
def update_tenant_edge_connector(vmanage, tenant, mt_edge):
```

items.body:
> 🤖 **Automated Agent Report** — *Google Antigravity Pair Programmer*

## 1. Overview & Architectural Rationale
Migrate the **Layer 7 Communications & Operator Cockpit** webmail/groupware interface from **SOGo** (`sogod` + GNUstep + AngularJS 1.x + custom Nginx `sub_filter` CSS/JS injection) to **[Kurrier](https://www.kurrier.org/)** (`kurrier-org/kurrier`), a modern open-source self-hosted workspace built on **Next.js, TypeScript, and Nitro**.

### Key Architectural Invariants
1. **Zero Disruption to Agent Mail Backbone**: Autonomous agents interact strictly with `mail-server` (Alpine Postfix SMTP `:25`, Dovecot IMAP `:143`, RFC 4314 anti-deletion ACLs, and Pigeonhole Sieve doorbell webhooks) via `packages/brainsOS-mail`. Replacing SOGo with Kurrier requires **zero changes** to agent tools, Dovecot Maildirs, or inbound webhook routing.
2. **Unified Multi-Inbox Fleet Oversight**: Instead of relying on legacy IMAP shared folder trees or fragile CSS overrides, Kurrier's background worker (`kurrier-worker`) connects to `mail-server` over `brainsos-internal-net`, providing the human operator with native dark mode, conversation threading, local full-text search, CalDAV/CardDAV sync, and unified multi-inbox switching across all fleet agents (`terrastella`, `bawtford`, `marvin`, `operator`).
3. **Kurrier Drive → Agent Workspace Bridge**: Pre-configured WebDAV storage volumes in Kurrier Drive map directly to each agent's isolated `/workspace` partition (`${BRAINSOS_DATA_DIR}/agents/<tenant_id>/workspace/`), giving users a OneDrive-style drag-and-drop file exchange with agents while keeping `/memories` 100% pure Markdown (Rule 1).
4. **Zero-Trust SSO & Database Isolation**: Kurrier's PostgreSQL store (`kurrier-db`) and Redis queue (`kurrier-redis`) remain strictly isolated from `brainsos-control-litellm-db` (Rule 6), and operator authentication integrates with Authentik SSO via OIDC inside the Thin-Spine Portal (`⌘1` Comms).

---

## 2. Child Deliverables & Native Task List
- [ ] #341 [Comms / Infra] Deploy Kurrier Container Stack (Web, Worker, Isolated DB & Redis) & Retire SOGo
- [ ] #342 [Comms / Bootstrap] Automated Multi-Tenant Fleet Mailbox & IMAP/CalDAV Connector Provisioning for Kurrier
- [ ] #346 [Comms / Drive] Pre-Configured Kurrier Drive Volumes for Per-Agent Workspaces & Operator File Exchange
- [ ] #343 [Ingress / Portal] Caddy Subdomain/Subpath Routing, Authentik OIDC SSO & Thin-Spine Comms Integration
- [ ] #344 [Comms / Ops] Operational Lifecycle Scripts, System Telemetry Health Probes & Architecture Documentation

Dependency order: **#341 → (#342, #346, #343) → #344**.

---

## 3. Operational Guardrails
- **Rule 1 (Memory Plane Purity)**: Zero database files, Redis dumps, search indices, binary Drive uploads, or `.ics` calendar artifacts inside `/memories`. All Kurrier state resides under `${BRAINSOS_COMMS_DIR}/kurrier/` and Drive volumes target `agents/<tenant_id>/workspace/` exclusively.
- **Rule 3 (Hardware Serialization & Footprint)**: Native `linux/arm64` execution without emulation; combined memory footprint audited in `verify-kurrier.sh`.
- **Rule 6 (Control Plane Database Isolation)**: `kurrier-db` runs in its own isolated PostgreSQL container on `brainsos-internal-net`, with zero access to `brainsos-control-net` or `brainsos-control-litellm-db`.
- **Rule 8 (Script-Driven Discipline)**: All database seeding, connector encryption, Drive volume provisioning, OIDC wiring, and verification checks must be codified idempotently in `scripts/setup/setup-kurrier.sh` and `scripts/verify/verify-kurrier.sh`.
- **Rule 9 (Multi-Tenant Partitioning)**: Individual agent containers continue authenticating exclusively to their own Dovecot Maildir and `/workspace` partition; only the human operator workspace in Kurrier aggregates fleet mailboxes and Drive volumes.
- **Rule 14 (Two-Repository Architecture)**: All persistent Kurrier state resolves dynamically via `${BRAINSOS_DATA_DIR}/comms/kurrier`.
