> *Filed by AI from the hostile review of #3315.*

## What exists

Two small leftovers around basal injections and the data source pages:

1. **Index.** `basal_injections` lacks the `ix_<table>_tenant_history` index (`tenant_id, sys_updated_at, id`) that `boluses` and the other treatment tables have. From #3315 the status last-modified read for the treatments group reads the newest `sys_updated_at` of basal injections on every status call, which has no index to use. The table is small today (MDI users of one connector), so the cost is small. `NocturneDbContext`'s `V4HistoryPagedEntities` list is where the other tables get it.
2. **A second label map.** `ConnectorDangerZone.svelte` keeps its own `recordCountLabels` map of data type keys to labels, beside `lib/utils/data-type-labels.ts`. A new key has to be added to both, and #3315 missed one until review.

## What it must become

1. `BasalInjectionEntity` joins the history-paged entities, with a generated migration (`dotnet ef migrations add`, concurrent index build through `ConcurrentIndexBuilder` if the house rule requires it for existing tables).
2. The danger zone takes its labels from `data-type-labels.ts` (with a lower-case form if the sentence needs one), and its own map is deleted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `HistoryPagedIndexTests` lists basal injections and passes; `has-pending-model-changes` is clean.
- [ ] One map of data type labels in the web app.

items.body:
Found while working on #705 (PR #751); not verified yet.

The pipeline editor's Test Connection buttons fetch `http://localhost:9500` (db-producer), `http://localhost:9300` (db-consumer) and similar: there are about 8 hardcoded `localhost:9x00` fetches in `ui/src`. From the production UI they can't reach anything, so Test Connection probably doesn't work there.

The workers' `/test-connection/` handlers on those aux ports have no auth, send CORS `*`, and dial any host they are given. If that port is reachable from outside the pod (Service, Ingress) it's an unauthenticated SSRF and port scanner inside the cluster.

Acceptance criteria:
- Check (from the manifests in `infrastructure/kubernetes/**`, read-only) whether the aux ports are exposed by any Service or Ingress, and say so in the PR.
- Test Connection goes through the management API (authenticated, tenant-scoped, `pkg/safeurl` / `pkg/connectorurl` rules) instead of the browser calling worker ports; the worker aux handlers accept calls only from inside the cluster (or are removed if the API does the check itself).
- No hardcoded `localhost:9x00` left in `ui/src` outside dev-only code.
- Tests for the API path (auth, tenant scope, refused private address).

Security, auth and possibly manifests: PR plus `agent:needs-human`.

items.body:
## Contexto
O entregável 2 da v0.1 é "conecte um projeto GCP **ou importe logs manualmente**". A Importação manual é o caminho mais curto para o piloto avaliar incidentes históricos.

## História de usuário
Como **Analyst**, quero enviar um arquivo de logs exportado, para diagnosticar falhas de sistemas que ainda não têm Conector.

## Escopo
- Bucket privado `raw-logs` no Supabase Storage, com caminho `{tenant_id}/imports/{import_id}/{filename}`. Policy do Storage: escrita e leitura apenas quando `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = app.current_tenant_id()::text`.
- Upload direto do navegador com **URL assinada de upload** emitida pela API (`POST /api/v1/imports` retorna `upload_url` e `import_id`). Upload resumível (TUS) para arquivos acima de 6 MB.
- Limites: 50 MB por arquivo e formatos `.json`, `.ndjson`, `.csv` (checagem por extensão **e** por magic bytes e parse). Outros formatos são recusados.
- Tabela `imports (tenant_id, id, integration_id, filename, size_bytes, sha256, format, status check in ('uploaded','processing','done','failed','rejected'), total_lines, accepted, rejected, duplicates, secrets_removed, error, created_by, created_at)`.
- Tabela `raw_log_objects (tenant_id, id, storage_path, sha256, size_bytes, source check in ('import','connector','api'), expires_at)`.
- Ao concluir o upload (`POST /api/v1/imports/{id}/complete`), grava uma mensagem `ingestion.raw` na outbox. O worker de #12 faz o parse em streaming.
- CSV: tela de mapeamento de colunas para o Contrato de evento, com sugestão automática por nome de coluna e mapeamento salvo por Integração.
- Linhas rejeitadas guardadas com o motivo (`import_rejections`), para download.
- Tela 13: área de upload, progresso em tempo real (Realtime em `imports`) e resultados.

## UI — Tela 13
```text
┌──────────────────────────┐
│ ← Importar logs          │
│ Integração [Pedidos ▾]   │
│ ┌ ⇪ Escolher arquivo ──┐ │
│ │ JSON, NDJSON, CSV 50MB│ │
│ └──────────────────────┘ │
│ sap-order….ndjson [Norm.]│
│ ████████░░ 8.120/12.600  │
│ bapi-errors.csv [Concl.] │
│ 2.004 ev · 14 rej · 3 seg│
└──────────────────────────┘
```

## Critérios de aceite
- **Dado** um arquivo `.xml`, **quando** enviado, **então** a importação fica `rejected` com a mensagem "Formato não permitido".
- **Dado** o mesmo arquivo (mesmo sha256) enviado duas vezes para a mesma Integração, **então** a segunda importação é marcada como duplicada e não gera Eventos novos.
- **Dado** um arquivo de 12 mil linhas, **quando** processado, **então** o progresso atualiza ao menos a cada 2 s na tela.
- **Dado** um usuário do tenant B, **quando** tenta ler o objeto de A no Storage, **então** recebe `403`.

## Segurança / LGPD
- O Log bruto expira conforme a retenção (30 dias padrão, #29) e não aparece em listagens públicas.
- O conteúdo passa pela Sanitização (#13) **antes** de virar Evento.

## Testes
- Fixtures CSV e NDJSON com linhas inválidas, encoding latin-1 e BOM.
- Teste de isolamento das policies do Storage.

## Dependências
#8, #10

items.title: Contract review: ai.pipestream.integration.v1 connector platform
items.body:
**Status: design for review.** Fable agents designed it, and an Opus agent reviewed it twice (13 must-fix findings, then 5 more). All of those findings are folded in. The proto set passes `buf lint` (STANDARD + COMMENTS) and `buf build`. Kristian and other LLMs: please weigh in here, or on the per-area tickets. This is the language-neutral connector contract for splitting grpc-confluence into three repos: a shared core (grpc-data-integration, name not final), grpc-confluence, and grpc-microsoft. Connectors can be written in any language and only speak gRPC. Map and Project come built in through CEL. Connectors can register pre and post hooks. Every action works on one entity, so the facade doubles as a document-repository view. Each per-area ticket below carries its full `.proto` file. This ticket carries the design note and `buf.yaml`. **Per-area tickets, in build order:** #12 entity, #13 hook, #14 connector, #15 transform, #16 sink, #17 ledger, #18 catalog, #19 entity_service, #20 migration map, #21 conformance kit. **Cross-cutting rules to accept here** (details below): - **Revisions.** `revision_id` changes whenever any emitted field changes. A derived entity's `revision_id` is `hash(derived_from, producer_id, producer_version)`. The same revision with a different fingerprint is `REVISION_CONFLICT`. Partial envelopes are never compared and never overwrite a full one. - **Supersede and cascade.** A producer's new outputs for a source replace its earlier ones. A source DELETE cascades through lineage. - **Checkpoints.** Cursors merge by scope, and the checkpoint is stored only after every FAIL_ACTION POST hook succeeds. - **Reconcile** applies to depth-0 rows only. - **Sinks** deliver only when the ledger reports `written = true`. The idempotency key is `(asset_id, revision_id, operation)`. The protomolt `operation_id` is a fixed-length hash with no run_id. - **No size cap** anywhere in the contract. `max_bytes` is only the caller's optional ceiling. The 512 MB Redis maximum is an implementation note. - **Post-release:** field-level deltas between steps (ai-pipestream/protomolt#572). `Entity.body` is a oneof so that change can be added later without breaking anything. **Done when** the owners sign off on the design and the proto set.
buf.yaml ```yaml # Buf STANDARD + COMMENTS, the same bar as grpc-confluence. Lint only; # codegen is each connector's own concern (protoc, buf generate, ...). # # google/rpc/status.proto is vendored under third_party/googleapis because the # design environment could not reach buf.build (egress proxy refused the # connection). In the real repo replace the second module with # deps: # - buf.build/googleapis/googleapis # and run `buf dep update`. version: v2 modules: - path: proto - path: third_party/googleapis lint: use: - MINIMAL lint: use: - STANDARD - COMMENTS breaking: use: - FILE ```
--- # Design note (DESIGN.md) ## Files | File | Holds | |---|---| | `entity.proto` | `Action`, `KindRef`, `EntityRef`, `EntityRevision`, `Lineage`, `Relation`, `Content`, `Entity`, `Change`, `ActionSupport`, `KindCapabilities`, `EntityKind`, `ConnectionContext`, `ScopeCursor` | | `hook.proto` | `HookRegistration` (phase, order, failure policy, timeout, `emits`, `types`, `non_deterministic`); `HookService.Invoke`; `HookResult`, `HookOutcome` | | `connector.proto` | `ConnectorDescriptor`; `ConnectorService` (Describe, Probe, Discover, Extract, Fetch); `ExtractEvent` (change, entity_error, scope_completed, pass_completed); `FetchFrame` | | `transform.proto` | `Mapping`/`MappingRule` (CEL, `id`, `fan_out`), `Projection`, stored `Transform` | | `sink.proto` | `SinkService` (DescribeSink, Deliver), `SinkBinding`, `DocumentAccession` | | `ledger.proto` | `LedgerService` (reads, Watch) and core-internal `LedgerWriteService` (RecordAsset, DeleteAsset, Reconcile, PutCheckpoint) | | `catalog.proto` | `CatalogService`: connectors, schemas, hooks, sinks, sink bindings, transforms, connections | | `entity_service.proto` | `EntityService`: the per-entity facade (actions, probe, discover, runs, fetch, read content, reconcile, map, project, lineage) | ## Entity and action model An **entity** is a generic typed envelope. `EntityRef` (`connector_id`, `connection_id`, `kind`, `native_id`) is its identity. The first three may not contain `:`, so the ledger key `asset_id` = `{connector_id}:{connection_id}:{kind}:{native_id}` is derived and split with limit 4. APIs always pass `EntityRef`. `Entity.body.payload` is the producer's own protobuf message as `google.protobuf.Any`. `body` is a oneof so a field-level delta arm (protomolt #572) can be added later. `Entity.content` carries bytes by claim check (`reference`) for binary kinds. **Namespacing of derived entities.** `connector_id` is the id of the producer that owns the kind. A derived entity carries the hook_id or transform_id as its `connector_id` and copies the source's `connection_id`. Connector, hook, transform, and sink ids share one catalog namespace (`ALREADY_EXISTS` on collision), so kind names are scoped per producer and cannot collide. **Revision contract.** `revision_id` changes whenever any emitted field changes. It can be an etag, a version, a composite, or the core's deterministic `fingerprint` when the source has none. For derived entities the core sets `revision_id = hash(sorted derived_from, producer_id, producer_version)`. Recording the same `(ref, revision_id)` with another fingerprint is `FAILED_PRECONDITION / REVISION_CONFLICT`. **Partial envelopes** (a `metadata_only` pass, or a Fetch whose options change the representation) set `Entity.partial`, and the core records an `options_fingerprint`. Fingerprints are compared only between non-partial envelopes. A partial envelope never raises a conflict and never overwrites a stored full one. `previous_revision_id` and `schema_fingerprint` ride on every entity and ledger row. **Kinds** are declared by producers: connectors (`ConnectorDescriptor.kinds`), hooks (`HookRegistration.emits`), and transforms (`output_kind`). Each kind lists `ActionSupport{action, options_type}` and `KindCapabilities` (`supports_revision_fetch`, `incremental_reports_deletes`, concurrency and rate hints). `options_type` is the connector's own message for per-request options, so a UI or MCP layer can build input schemas from descriptors. Examples: Confluence `FetchOptions{body_format}` and `DiscoverOptions{space_keys}`; Microsoft `ExtractOptions{folder_path}` and `FetchOptions{include_content}`. **Actions** are one closed enum. Describe, Probe, Discover, Extract, and Fetch belong to the connector; Reconcile, Map, and Project belong to the core. `EntityService.ListActions` returns `ActionDescriptor{action, scope CONNECTOR|CONNECTION|ENTITY, rpc, core, options_type, hookable, hook_ids}`. Custom verbs can come later as `custom_action_id` strings, not as new enum values. ## Registration and schemas 1. The operator calls `CatalogService.RegisterConnector(endpoint, replace, allow_breaking)`. Rebinding an existing `connector_id` without `replace` fails with `ALREADY_EXISTS / CONNECTOR_EXISTS`. 2. The core calls `Describe` and fingerprints `types`. On refresh it checks compatibility against the stored fingerprint and fails with `SCHEMA_INCOMPATIBLE` unless `allow_breaking` is set. It then registers the types and the declared hooks. An empty hook endpoint means the connector's own. 3. Every descriptor set ever registered is kept by fingerprint and readable with `GetSchema`, so rows recorded under an older set still decode after a breaking refresh. The core compiles against its own copy of this package. 4. Sinks register the same way. Hooks from other services use `RegisterHook`. Transforms are stored with `PutTransform`, versioned and fingerprinted, and boot files may seed them. **Settings and secrets** are two typed messages (`settings_type`, `secrets_type`), for connectors and sinks alike. `Connection.secrets` and `SinkBinding.secrets` are write-only: - cleared on every read, - merged on update, - removed by `clear_secrets`. `stored_secrets` lists which fields hold a value. `UpdateConnection` takes a `FieldMask` into `settings`. Secrets reach only the connector (in `ConnectionContext`) or the sink (in `DeliverRequest`). ## Hooks A hook is a `HookService` endpoint. `InvokeRequest` carries ids, the facade request as `Any`, the POST `subject` entity, and a `chain_token`. It never carries settings or secrets; a hook gets bytes from `EntityService.ReadContent` by claim check. - **PRE hooks** may `veto`, which always aborts the action with `FAILED_PRECONDITION / HOOK_VETOED`. They emit nothing and cannot rewrite requests in v1. - **POST hooks** run once per output entity, only on depth-0 outputs of the primary action, never on other hooks' outputs. - **Re-entrancy.** A hook that calls back into the core forwards the chain token as gRPC metadata. The core refuses actions that carry it (`HOOK_REENTRANT`) but allows `ReadContent`, `GetLineage`, and ledger reads. - **Repeat runs.** The core skips a hook it already ran for `(hook_id, asset_id, revision_id)`. A deterministic hook (the default) that re-emits a derived revision with a different fingerprint hits `REVISION_CONFLICT`. A hook registered `non_deterministic` gets a nonce in its derived revision ids, and its earlier outputs are superseded instead. - **Failure policy.** `FAIL_ACTION` blocks the Extract checkpoint. `CONTINUE` reports a `HookOutcome` (`COMPLETED | VETOED | FAILED | TIMED_OUT`, with `subject`) and moves on. - Describe and Probe accept no hooks. ## 1:M, lineage, supersede, reconcile Hooks, Map, and Project emit `Change{UPSERT, entity}` with `Lineage{derived_from, produced_by, producer_kind, producer_id, producer_version, depth}`. Producers give deterministic `native_id`s: Mapping has a required CEL `id`, and Projection uses the source id. **Supersede:** the outputs of producer P for a new revision of source S replace P's earlier outputs for S. The core tombstones the ones that weren't re-emitted (`DELETE`, `CHANGE_SOURCE_DERIVED`). A source `DELETE` cascades to derived rows by lineage. **Reconcile applies to depth-0 rows only.** Derived rows die only by supersede or cascade. `GetLineage` walks upstream or downstream, bounded by a server maximum depth and paginated. ## Map and Project via CEL - **Map** (`Mapping`) is keyed on `source_type`. Its rules are protomolt's mapper inputs in wire form: text rules in the `ProtoFieldMapper` grammar, applied as `map(source, target, rules)`, plus CEL `filter`/`selector` as in `CelProtoMapper`. CEL binds `source`, `target`, `envelope`, and `item`. `fan_out` yields 1:M. This is a wire shape for those inputs, not a byte-for-byte copy of the Java record. - **Project** (`Projection`): the output kind's payload type carries protomolt's `(ai.protomolt.proto.projection.v1.sources/from/default_from)` options. The core runs the same projection with the payload bound as `source`. - Inputs are recorded `EntityRevision`s. Inline inputs or inline definitions are dry runs. `record = true` requires a recorded input and a stored transform. ## Extract as a run, cursors, checkpoint `StartExtract` returns a `Run`. `WatchRun` streams `ExtractEvent`s, derived changes, and hook outcomes, and ends with `ExtractCompleted{cursors, checkpoint_stored, counts, errors, reconciled}`. `GetRun` and `CancelRun` manage the run. The core stamps `run_id` and records it on every ledger row the pass touches; connectors don't echo it. Cursors are `ScopeCursor`s: 1. The core sends the stored entries for the requested scopes as `since`. 2. The connector returns one cursor per covered scope in `PassCompleted`. 3. The core **merges them into the checkpoint by scope**, replacing only the covered scopes. The merge happens only after the pass and every `FAIL_ACTION` POST hook succeeded. An expired cursor fails the call with `FAILED_PRECONDITION / CURSOR_EXPIRED` instead of resetting in-band. A reset would silently turn an incremental pass into a full one, multiplying volume and sink deliveries without the operator's consent. Failing closed lets the operator start a full run with `reconcile = true` on purpose. ## Content reads `EntityService.ReadContent` streams bytes by claim check or revision. It uses the core's stored copy when there is one. Otherwise it does a lazy connector `Fetch` through the saved connection. The current revision always works. A past revision works only when the kind has `supports_revision_fetch`; otherwise the call fails with `CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE`. After a lazy fetch, the core may store the bytes under a claim check. ## Sinks `SinkService.Deliver` is a bidi stream of recorded `Change`s with per-delivery acks. - **What gets delivered.** A change is delivered only when `RecordAsset` (or a tombstone write) reports `written = true`. Replays and partial envelopes are not delivered. - **Guarantees.** At-least-once, ordered per asset within a run. The idempotency key is `(asset_id, revision_id, operation)`, so a DELETE is never deduplicated against its UPSERT. - **Retries.** `UNAVAILABLE` and `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` are retried with backoff that honours `RetryInfo`. Other errors are recorded on the `Asset` as `FAILED`. - **Bindings.** `SinkBinding` holds the sink, a connection or the default, kinds, typed settings, and write-only secrets. It replaces `ConnectionOutput`, `RuntimeSettings`, the Kafka settings, and the MCP `connection_set_output` / `app_set_*` tools. The protomolt sink saves through the parts-based `DocumentService`: - `operation_id = sha256hex(asset_id \n revision_id \n operation)`: 64 characters, no run_id, within the 200-character limit. - `ExpectedRevision` comes from `DeliverRequest.base`; none when unset. - `derived_from` is translated through `SourceAccession`s. - It returns a `DocumentAccession`, which the ledger stores on the row. ## Sizes No payload or content size cap is part of this contract. `Fetch.max_bytes` is the caller's optional ceiling (0 = none). `Fetch`, `ReadContent`, and sink delivery stream bytes of any length. Inline bytes are discouraged but never capped by the contract. Any server-side limit is implementation configuration. Implementation note only: the platform's agreed storage ceiling is 512 MB, the Redis max value size. It is not a proto constant. ## Errors Errors use the gRPC status plus `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` (domain `integration.pipestream.ai`): | Reason | Status | Note | |---|---|---| | `UPSTREAM_UNAUTHENTICATED` | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | credentials rejected | | `RATE_LIMITED` | `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` | with `RetryInfo` (upstream 429) | | `CURSOR_EXPIRED` | `FAILED_PRECONDITION` | metadata `scope` | | `CONTENT_TOO_LARGE` | `FAILED_PRECONDITION` | caller's `max_bytes` exceeded | | `CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE` | `FAILED_PRECONDITION` | past revision not stored, no revision fetch | | `HOOK_VETOED` / `HOOK_FAILED` / `HOOK_REENTRANT` | `FAILED_PRECONDITION` | metadata `hook_id`; reads allowed under a chain token | | `REVISION_CONFLICT` | `FAILED_PRECONDITION` | same revision, other fingerprint (full envelopes only) | | `SCHEMA_INCOMPATIBLE` | `FAILED_PRECONDITION` | refresh without `allow_breaking` | | `CONNECTOR_EXISTS` | `ALREADY_EXISTS` | register without `replace` | Per-entity failures inside Extract are `EntityError{ref, Status}` events. ## Reuse from protomolt | protomolt | Here | |---|---| | `derived_from` / `SourceRevision` | `Lineage.derived_from` / `EntityRevision` (string revision) | | `NodeAddress` + revision | `DocumentAccession` | | `ExpectedRevision` | driven by `DeliverRequest.base` | | mapper grammar, CEL filter/selector | `MappingRule` | | projection options | reused as is | | `IntakeOrigin` string `connector_id` | same | | `acquire/pull` bounded pass, caller-held cursor | same | Payloads are `Any`, not `Document`. The protomolt sink is where an entity becomes a document. ## Today's RPCs and tools on the new contract | Today | New | |---|---| | Confluence `ProbeConnection`, Microsoft `GetMe` | `ProbeConnection` (saved or inline) | | Confluence `ListSpaces` (`keys`), Microsoft `ListSites` | `DiscoverEntities`; keys via `options` | | Microsoft `ListDrives` | `DiscoverEntities(parent = site)` | | Confluence `ListPages`/`ListBlogPosts`, `ListAttachments`, Microsoft `ListChildren` (`folder_path`) | `StartExtract` scoped + `kinds`, `options`; or `LedgerService.ListAssets(parent, kinds)` | | Confluence `GetPage`/`GetBlogPost` (`body_format`), Microsoft `GetItem` | `FetchEntity` with `options` (partial envelope when options change the body) | | Confluence `GetAttachment`, Microsoft `DownloadItem` (`include_content`) | `FetchEntity(include_content)`, chunked | | Confluence/Microsoft `Sync` (`since_cursor`, `include_bodies`) | `StartExtract` + `WatchRun` (`resume`, `metadata_only`) | | `ConfluenceChange`/`MicrosoftChange`, `ChangeSource`, `ChangeOperation` | `Change`, `ChangeSource`, `ChangeOperation` | | `ConfluenceSnapshot`/`MicrosoftSnapshot` (`snapshot_id`, counts, metadata) | `ScopeCompleted` | | `SyncTableService` Upsert/Get/List/Watch/Delete/Reconcile/Checkpoints, `AssetPhase`, `attachments_only`, `ASSET_SYNC_STATUS_PENDING` | `LedgerService` + `LedgerWriteService`; `AssetPhase`, `kinds` filter, `ASSET_STATUS_PENDING` | | `ConnectionService` CRUD, `ConnectionKind`, `RecordProbe` | `CatalogService` connections; string `connector_id`; probe records status | | `CONNECTION_STATUS_PENDING` ("not probed yet") | `CONNECTION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED` ("never probed") | | `ConnectionOutput`, `RuntimeSettings`, `GetSettings`/`UpdateSettings`, MCP `connection_set_output`, `app_set_output`, `app_set_kafka` | `SinkBinding` (default or per connection) via `PutSinkBinding` | | Output SPI (filesystem, S3, OKF, protobuf/JSON formats), Kafka sink | `SinkService` implementations | | MCP `confluence_*`, `microsoft_*`, `connection_*`, `sync_table_*`, `app_*` | generated from `EntityService`, `CatalogService`, `LedgerService` | **Intentional drops:** | Dropped | Why | |---|---| | `ASSET_PHASE_SNAPSHOT` | it is a `ScopeCompleted` event, not a row | | `GetConnectionRequest.include_secret` | secrets never leave the catalog | | `Connection.base_url/email/token/space_keys/tenant_id/client_id/client_secret/site_id/drive_ids` | replaced by connector-owned settings and secrets types | | `Asset.source` | now `EntityRef.connector_id` | | `Asset.attachment` | now `EntityKind.binary` | | `Checkpoint.scope` string | `ScopeCursor.scope` is an `EntityRef` | | size-capped unary `GetAttachment` / `DownloadItem` | streams instead | | `ConfluenceEntity` / `MicrosoftEntity` oneof wrappers | `Any` + declared kinds | | `CONNECTION_STATUS_PENDING` as a distinct value | folded into UNSPECIFIED | **Not adopted from the reviews, with reasons:** | Not adopted | Why | |---|---| | in-band `cursor_reset` event | fail closed instead (see above) | | `ListConnectors` / `ListSinks` pagination | bounded by operator registrations | | `SKIPPED` hook result | a skipped hook is never invoked, so there is no outcome | | streaming `ExtractEntities` twin of the run resource | `WatchRun` gives the same stream | | `ListRuns` | can be added later without breaking anything | ## Open questions 1. Should `WatchRun` replay from a persisted event log after the core restarts, or only while the run is in memory? 2. Should transforms keep version history (`GetTransform(version)`) so a lineage edge's `producer_version` can be re-read later? 3. The vendored `google/rpc/status.proto` must be replaced by the BSR dep once the repo can reach buf.build.

items.title: Reliability and performance: verified defects from the 2026-10-19 audit of main
items.body:
**Phase:** 1–2 (production readiness). Parent: #937. Baseline: `main@c8e5213`.

This is a read-only audit with local reproduction. PostgreSQL numbers come from one PG16 container with synthetic data: they show how the access pattern changes and are not production capacity. Each fix should land as its own small PR with a regression test.

## High
- [ ] **Temporal connect has no timeout and runs inside an open DB transaction.** In `workflow_runtime.py:259-265`, `Client.connect` has no deadline. Measured: against a blackholed address it hung for 135 s, even with `AXIS_TEMPORAL_SIGNAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=2`. `record_demo_action_run` stayed `idle in transaction` throughout. A failed connect is not cached and there is no lock, so about 15 hung requests exhaust the default pool (5+10, 3 s timeout) and every request then returns 500. The same unbounded connect stalls `ApprovalDecisionOutboxDispatcher.run_once`. **Fix:** an `asyncio.timeout` on connect and signal, an `asyncio.Lock` around client creation, and a negative cache with backoff.
- [ ] **`audit_events` lacks `(tenant_id, created_at, id)` and `(tenant_id, event_type, created_at, id)` indexes.** These back `persistence.py:1609-1640` and many routes. Measured with 2M rows: the query took 350 ms and read 64.6k shared buffers; with the index it takes 0.15 ms and reads 19 buffers. **Fix:** a `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` migration, following the 0065 pattern. Then review `action_runs`, `connector_runs` and `approval_records`.
- [ ] **Source ingestion loops forever when extraction outlives the claim lease.** In `connector_source_ingestion.py`, S3/REST completion with `require_unexpired=True` returns "fenced" without dead-lettering, so `attempt_count` grows past `max_attempts` indefinitely. Reproduced: 6 passes, 0 completed, attempts 1→6 with max 3, and the source re-read on every pass. The default lease of 120 s has no renewal, against up to 20 selections × 30 s. **Fix:** renew the lease per selection, validate the timeout against the budget in settings, and count fenced-after-expiry outcomes toward `max_attempts`.
- [ ] **Postgres extraction holds the Axis transaction across the source read and the object-store put, and commits partial batches.** In `connector_source_ingestion.py:1141-1316`, a dead-lettered request still committed the first selection's batch and audit event. **Fix:** align it with the S3/REST shape: prepare, read without a transaction, then a fenced commit.

## Medium
- [ ] **Worker activities are `async def` but do synchronous DB and live-sync I/O on the event loop that also runs the pollers and outbox loops**, with no heartbeat. Files: `connector_live_sync_activities.py` and `maintenance_activities.py`. **Fix:** a thread-pool activity executor, `heartbeat_timeout` and heartbeats.
- [ ] **A concurrent duplicate action run returns 500 instead of a replay, and the signal is sent before the commit.** In `action_runs.py:839-895`, measured on PG: `UniqueViolation` → 500. **Fix:** apply the ADR 0003 phase contract, or catch `IntegrityError` and replay.
- [ ] **TypeDB request-path calls use the driver's default 2-hour timeout.** Files: `ontology/queries.py:94` and `ontology/mutations.py:165`. The lazy connect has no lock, and every read makes an extra `databases.contains` round trip.
- [ ] **MinIO/S3 clients use the library defaults (300 s connect/read, 5 retries).** In `object_storage.py:350-353`, and the startup warm-up blocks the lifespan.
- [ ] **JWKS refresh has no stale-if-error fallback.** In `identity.py:232-270`, an unreachable JWKS endpoint failed 8 of 8 verifications even with a valid cached key.

## Low
- [ ] N+1 queries in `GET /operations/workflows/runs` (`workflow_queries.py:126-135`, 1+N statements). Timelines are also capped at the 100 oldest events, so the newest are dropped.
- [ ] N+1 queries in the credential-handle registry (`connector_credential_handles.py:134-143`).
- [ ] Every cookie-authenticated request runs an `UPDATE` on its browser-session row (`persistence.py:1436`). **Fix:** throttle to about 60 s.
- [ ] Console shell overhead:
  - `ConsoleProvider` re-renders all consumers every 30 s.
  - The shell fetches the full approvals inbox and overview only for counts and badges.
  - A `/notifications` waterfall follows `/identity/session`.
- [ ] Web requests have no timeout (`apps/web/lib/axis-api.ts`). **Fix:** `AbortSignal.timeout`.
- [ ] The worker creates 4 independent pools (up to 60 connections), pool size is not configurable, and there is no API `statement_timeout`.

## Already documented, still open
- The four async handlers without the phase contract (ADR 0003).
- The unbounded `list_all_current_connector_manifests`: the response grows from 14 KB to 130 KB going from 5 to 50 connectors.
- Model invocations stuck in `requested` are never reaped.
- `list_search_index_states` loads a whole tenant index.

## Verified sound
- `/ready` and its probe design.
- Route limit clamping, and constant SQL counts across 58 tenant-scoped GET routes.
- Outbound connector timeouts and the model httpx timeout.
- Outbox fencing and jittered backoff.
- Workflow determinism.
- Redis rate-limit timeouts.
- `useAxisQuery` abort and invalidation.

items.title: feat(connectors): complete connector lifecycle — update, status transitions, delete wiring
items.body:
## Problem

The connector lifecycle is half-built. `ConnectorStatus` (`src/arc/domain/models.py:27`) defines ACTIVE/INACTIVE/ERROR but no code path ever writes INACTIVE or ERROR (`ConnectorService` only creates ACTIVE; `ConnectorSyncService` never touches `config.status` — verified by search). The API exposes list/create/sync/credentials (`src/arc/api/controllers.py:1639-1973`) but there is no update endpoint, no get-by-id, and the service-level `get_connector`/`delete_connector` (`services/connectors.py:55-70`) have no routes. A connector whose credential is revoked or whose provider errors can never reflect that state; a tenant cannot rename/retarget or remove a connector through the API.

## Current state

- `ConnectorService`: create/get/list/delete, trusted-`TenantContext` only, no auth (correct — auth lives in dependencies).
- `connector_configs` table: `UNIQUE(tenant_id, provider, name)`, tenant FK cascade.
- Sync failures are recorded in `connector_sync_records` (error_kind) but never surface on the config row.
- Frontend `ConnectorsPage.jsx` lists/creates/syncs only.

## Scope

1. Add update path (rename/retarget; provider immutable after create) with tenant-scoped repository support.
2. Define status-transition rules: who may set INACTIVE (tenant), when the system sets ERROR (e.g. repeated auth failure — coordinated with the sync error/retry issue), when ERROR clears (successful sync). Keep the state machine to three states; no new states.
3. Wire missing routes (update, delete, get-by-id) behind existing `connector:create/read/sync` permissions — no new permissions unless proven necessary.
4. Frontend: expose only what the API now supports (edit + delete controls); no new pages.

## Out of scope

- Sync scheduling/periodicity, retry policy, cursor logic (sync issues).
- Credential rotation UX beyond what exists (credential CRUD already shipped).
- New permissions or roles.

## Architecture

External System → Connector (config lifecycle, THIS ISSUE) → normalization → source/index → retrieval → Ask Arc. Pure control-plane work: no fetch, ingestion, or retrieval behavior changes.

## Security / tenant isolation

All routes use the trusted `TenantContext` + path-tenant consistency + existing connector permissions, following the established controller pattern. Cross-tenant config access stays denied at SQL + API level (extend the existing isolation tests to update/delete paths).

## Testing

Deterministic, PostgreSQL-backed API tests (existing `test_connector_api.py` pattern): update validation, status-transition rules, delete cascade (configs → sync records → credentials?), cross-tenant 403/404 on every new route, UNIQUE(tenant, provider, name) conflict behavior. No external credentials; fakes only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Update, get-by-id, delete routes exist, permission-gated, tenant-scoped.
- [ ] INACTIVE/ERROR are reachable through documented transitions only; ACTIVE is the create default.
- [ ] A connector with revoked credentials can reach ERROR via the sync-failure path (contract with the retry issue, implemented there if ordering requires).
- [ ] Existing list/create/sync behavior unchanged (full connector suite green).
- [ ] Frontend exposes edit/delete without new routes/pages.

## Dependencies

Status-on-sync-failure transition depends on the sync error/retry taxonomy issue (define the contract here, implement the hook there if needed). Otherwise independent — can start in parallel with the metadata-contract issue.

## Non-goals

No fetch/sync behavior change. No executable actions (#304). No new provider adapters.

items.title: feat(connectors): source-level authorization model decision for connector content
items.body:
## Problem

ARCHITECTURE GAP — REQUIRES DECISION. Retrieval authorization today is tenant-wide: any member with `knowledge:read` reads all tenant knowledge, including all connector-synced content (`RetrievalService.approved_search` filters by trusted `tenant_id` only, with per-match re-validation). There is no source-level authorization: nothing distinguishes "all engineers may read GitHub-synced docs" from "only #leadership members may read Slack #leadership-synced docs". Connector work that ignores this either over-builds (per-source ACLs nobody asked for) or under-protects (sensitive channels synced into a tenant-wide corpus). The decision must land before the retrieval-integration issue ships its filter design.

## Current state

- AuthZ: 26 permissions × 5 ApplicationRoles, fail-closed (`security/authorization.py`); connector perms are `connector:create/read/sync/manage_credentials`.
- Retrieval: tenant-scoped SQL + `MIN_RELEVANCE_SCORE` + `source_type: KnowledgeSource` filter — no principal-aware or source-aware filtering.
- `UserRole` (OWNER/MEMBER/VIEWER, DB membership) is independent of `ApplicationRole` (ADR-008).
- Webhook pipeline precedent: `system:webhook` principal with minimal `WEBHOOK_PROCESSOR` role — scoped machine principals are an established pattern.

## Scope

1. Decide, with written rationale: Option A — tenant-wide `knowledge:read` remains sufficient for V1 connector content (document why; likely: tenant = trust boundary per AGENTS.md/CURRENT_STATE, coarse roles already gate who sees knowledge at all). Option B — introduce source-level scoping (e.g. connector-config-linked read rule) with a concrete minimal design.
2. If Option A: define the guardrails that keep it safe (which sources must NOT be connected, e.g. guidance against syncing restricted channels; per-connector visibility note in the connector record).
3. If Option B: define the enforcement point (retrieval filter vs controller check), the permission/role delta (new permissions need ADR-level justification), and the migration for existing connector docs.
4. Either way: cross-tenant protection proof for connector docs (tenant A's GitHub sync never retrievable by tenant B) as explicit acceptance tests.

## Out of scope

- Implementing retrieval filters (retrieval-integration issue implements whatever this decides).
- New roles, new OAuth, per-user provider credentials (settings.py explicitly defers tenant-owned OAuth).
- Changing the 26-permission matrix without an ADR.

## Architecture

External System → Connector → normalization → source/index → retrieval (AUTHZ DECISION POINT, THIS ISSUE) → Ask Arc. The model/LLM is never the enforcement point — enforcement stays in retrieval/controllers regardless of option chosen.

## Security / tenant isolation

This issue IS the security analysis: tenant boundary preservation is non-negotiable under both options; the open question is intra-tenant source scoping only. Document the threat model: malicious/broad connector target configured by a permitted user, exfiltration via Ask Arc citations, offboarding (deleted connector → what happens to its docs' readability).

## Testing

Decision record + tests (no customer credentials): cross-tenant connector-doc isolation tests (A syncs GitHub, B searches — zero bleed, at SQL and API levels); for Option A, a test proving a tenant member with `knowledge:read` CAN read connector docs (documenting the accepted posture); for Option B, denied-source tests. Deterministic fakes only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Written decision (A or B) with threat-model rationale, stored where ADRs live if it changes architecture, otherwise in the issue.
- [ ] If B: enforcement point + permission delta + migration specified, no LLM-side enforcement.
- [ ] Connector-doc lifecycle on connector delete/tenant offboard specified (docs stay? cascade? — decide, don't drift).
- [ ] Cross-tenant isolation tests for connector-sourced documents green.

## Dependencies

Depends on the metadata-contract issue (need to know what source identity looks like before scoping rules to it). Blocks the retrieval-integration issue's filter design.

## Non-goals

No filter implementation. No executable actions (#304). No per-user credential vaulting.

items.title: feat(connectors): provider-origin normalization and source metadata contract
items.body:
## Problem

Connector-synced content reaches Company Brain without a structured provider-origin identity. `KnowledgeSource` (`src/arc/domain/models.py:42`) is a semantic taxonomy (policy / procedure / incident_report / troubleshooting / internal_knowledge / solution) — it has no provider axis. Today `ConnectorSyncService.sync` (`src/arc/services/connector_sync.py:166`) ingests every record as `KnowledgeSource.INTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE` with provider identity smuggled in opaque strings (`provenance=f"connector:{provider}:{source_id}"`, `external_id=f"{provider}:{source_id}"`). Consequences: retrieval's `source_type` filter (`RetrievalService.search` / `approved_search`) cannot select "all GitHub docs" or "all Slack docs"; `ProviderRecord` (`connector_providers/base.py:59`) carries only `source_id/title/content/url` so author, timestamps, thread/parent links and repo/channel identity are dropped at the fetch boundary and can never be recovered downstream.

## Current state

- `ProviderRecord`: source_id, title, content, url only (`src/arc/services/connector_providers/base.py`).
- GitHub parse: number/title/body/html_url (`github.py:95`); Slack parse: text/ts only (`slack.py:134`).
- Ingestion: `KnowledgeService.ingest_document(context, source, provenance, content, external_id)` with ADR-003 identity `(tenant_id, source, external_id)` (`services/knowledge.py:60`, `domain/models.py:409`).
- Retrieval already filters on `source_type: KnowledgeSource | None` — reuse, don't duplicate.

## Scope

Define and implement the minimum provider-origin metadata contract:

1. Decide where provider origin lives: extend the `provenance`/`external_id` convention with a documented grammar, or add explicit structured fields — without a schema change if possible, with a migration-backed ADR if not.
2. Extend `ProviderRecord` with only the fields the retrieval/Ask Arc path actually requires (candidate floor: provider, external object id, url, author, timestamps, parent/thread reference, repo/workspace/channel identity). Every field must justify itself against a retrieval or citation use-case; speculative fields are rejected.
3. Pin the GitHub and Slack field mappings to the contract (what maps where, what is dropped and why).
4. Document the convention where a future reader will look (code docstrings + short docs note, not a new doc system).

## Out of scope

- Fetching new object types (PRs, comments, threads) — covered by the GitHub/Slack scope issues.
- Retrieval filtering UI/API on the new metadata — covered by the retrieval-integration issue.
- Schema migration unless proven necessary; prefer convention-first, migrate only with an ADR.

## Architecture

External System → Connector (fetch, unchanged) → normalization/source metadata (THIS ISSUE: the contract) → source/index (KnowledgeService, unchanged) → retrieval → Ask Arc. This issue is the narrow waist: everything provider-specific stops here, everything downstream stays provider-agnostic.

## Security / tenant isolation

Metadata is tenant-scoped by construction (ingested under the trusted `TenantContext`; identity includes `tenant_id`). No credential, token, or raw auth material may enter metadata. Author names/handles pass through the PII Guard boundary with content (verify Presidio behavior on handles in tests; never bypass sanitization to preserve metadata).

## Testing

Deterministic only, no customer credentials: unit tests over frozen GitHub-issue and Slack-message payloads asserting exact `ProviderRecord` mapping (including dropped-field behavior and malformed-payload fail-closed); re-ingestion idempotency tests through `KnowledgeService` proving one logical document per `(tenant, source, external_id)`; no live API calls.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Contract documented in code (docstrings) stating exact fields, grammar, and what is deliberately excluded.
- [ ] GitHub issue → record mapping preserves url + author + timestamps; Slack message → record preserves channel identity + ts + thread parent where present.
- [ ] Malformed provider payloads still fail closed (`ProviderResponseError`).
- [ ] Re-sync of identical records is idempotent (no duplicate documents, no version bump).
- [ ] No new speculative metadata fields without a cited retrieval/citation consumer.

## Dependencies

None — this is the foundation issue; GitHub/Slack scope issues and retrieval integration depend on it.

## Non-goals

No executable action/tool integration (see #304, which owns external actions). No agent/skill changes. No second retrieval system. Google Drive stays conditional per ADR-002.

items.title: Feat: Service Principal (client credentials) auth mode to the ADLS Gen2 sink connector
items.body:
## Summary

The `kafka-connect-azure-datalake` sink currently supports three auth modes (`config/AuthModeSettings.scala`):
`Credentials` (account key), `ConnectionString`, and `Default` (`DefaultAzureCredential`, worker-level). 
There is no way to authenticate to storage with a **per-connector Service Principal** (Entra ID App Registration:
`client_id` / `client_secret` / `tenant_id`) using client-credentials OAuth.

I'd like to add a `ServicePrincipal` auth mode backed by `ClientSecretCredentialBuilder` from `com.azure.identity`,
which is already a project dependency (`azure-identity`, see `project/Dependencies.scala`) and already used for
`DefaultAzureCredentialBuilder` in `auth/DatalakeClientCreator.scala`. No new dependency is required.

### Rational
Usually security standards require secrets to be short-lived and scoped. A storage account key or connection string is a long-lived,
account-wide credential. `DefaultAzureCredential` is a worker-level setting, not something that can be configured per connector. 

A Service Principal with a scoped RBAC role and short-lived OAuth tokens, configurable per connector instance, closes
that gap while keeping all the existing sink functionality.

## Proposed change

I think the actual changes should be quite small and dependeny-free.

1. **Configuration** — `config/AuthModeSettings.scala`: add an `AuthMode.ServicePrincipal(clientId, tenantId,
   clientSecret)` case, plus config keys (e.g. `connect.datalake.azure.client.id`, `.tenant.id`, `.client.secret`),
   wired into `getAuthMode`.
2. **Authentication** — `auth/DatalakeClientCreator.scala`: add a
   `createDataLakeClientWithServicePrincipal(...)` path using
   `new ClientSecretCredentialBuilder().clientId(..).tenantId(..).clientSecret(..).build()`.
3. **Tests & docs** — unit tests for the new auth mode, and an update to the public connector docs (auth mode
   table currently lists `Credentials` / `ConnectionString` / `Default`).

I'm happy to implement this myself and submit a PR per the project's "Contributing" guidance. 
Before starting, I wanted to check: 
is this something the maintainers would be open to accepting, 
and is there any existing work or design preference I should be aware of (e.g. naming of config keys, whether `ClientSecretCredential` should be exposed directly or wrapped in a broader "explicit credential" auth mode)? 

Happy to align on approach before opening a PR.

items.title: Spike: verify Pick agent policies/permissions in container env (top + child level) - StrikeKit parity (matrix#3891 counterpart)
items.body:
### Question to answer

Can Pick's policies and permissions be configured **correctly** in the
container environment so that they hold for both **positive** (authorized
action is allowed) and **negative** (unauthorized action is denied) test cases,
at both the **top level** (parent tenant / org) and the **child level** (child
sub-tenant), for Pick (the operator-deployed agent) as it is orchestrated for
StrikeKit engagements?

This is the **Pick-side counterpart** to the StrikeKit/Matrix spike in
Strike48/matrix#3891 - together they cover both halves of "for StrikeKit and
for Pick". Where #3891 asks the platform question, this issue asks the
agent-side question.

Concretely, the spike must answer:

1. **Top level** - when Pick runs under a parent-tenant/org policy in its
   container/sandbox, are authorized tool actions permitted and unauthorized
   ones denied (tool/action allowlist, connector auth scope, sandbox policy)?
2. **Child level** - when the same Pick agent is scoped to a child sub-tenant,
   do its permissions scope down correctly *without inheriting or leaking
   parent-tenant authority* (no cross-tenant action, no wider connector scope
   than the child is entitled to)?
3. **Parity** - does the container-environment permission model behave
   consistently between how StrikeKit expects it (#3891) and how Pick actually
   enforces it, so there is no gap between the platform's intent and the
   agent's enforcement?

**MVP dependency**: this spike is **required for the Red Team MVP** - the answer
gates whether Pick's permissions can be trusted in the shipped container
environment, so it is release-blocking rather than exploratory.

_Intended investigators: Josh, Chihwei, Nitin (owners TBD by GitHub handle)._

### Success Criteria

[DRAFT] Documentation on Forge plus artifacts (a policy/permission test matrix
and its passing/failing runs) that demonstrate, for Pick x {top level, child
level}:

- at least one **positive** case where an authorized action is permitted, and
- at least one **negative** case where an unauthorized action is denied,

with all four combinations exercised **in the container environment**, and the
Pick policy/permission configuration that produced each result referenced in
code or config. A "correct" outcome means every negative case is denied (no
authz-boundary leak, no cross-tenant action, no over-scoped connector) and
every positive case succeeds. Results should reconcile with the StrikeKit-side
findings in #3891.

### Out of scope

[DRAFT]
- Building **new** policy/permission features in Pick - this spike only verifies
  whether the *existing* controls can be configured correctly and proves them
  with tests.
- Non-container environments (local dev, bare-metal) except as a comparison
  baseline.
- Performance / load testing of the enforcement layer.
- Production tenant data - use synthetic tenants/fixtures only.

### Foundation flags
- **Change surface**: neither - [DRAFT] investigation spike; deliverable is
  documentation + a test matrix, not a shipped product change (a follow-up
  implementation issue would carry the real change surface).
- **Security boundary**: yes - the spike exists to verify Pick's tenant authz
  and permission enforcement (top vs child level); a wrong result is a
  cross-tenant isolation leak or an over-scoped agent.
- **Screen recording expected on PR**: no - [DRAFT] the deliverable is docs and
  test evidence, not a user-facing UI change.

### Definition of Done
- [ ] Documentation exists on Forge that answers the Question above
- [ ] Artifacts exist that prove the Success Criteria have been met

### Product
Strike Kit

### Priority
P1

### Target
2026-09-25

items.title: The tenant boundary is unenforced: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, the curie_app role, SET LOCAL wiring, and the CI policy-coverage gate
items.body:
Implements step 11 of [ADR 0155](https://github.com/curie-eng/curie/blob/main/docs/adr/0155-tenant-boundary-and-principal-identity-land-together.md), ADR-0008's decisions 1 and 2. Lands last, after every column it depends on exists; highest blast radius since a misconfigured role or a missing `SET LOCAL` can lock out a working deployment.

**Scope**
- `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` on every tenant-scoped table, policy `USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::uuid)`.
- A dedicated non-superuser runtime role (`curie_app`, `NOBYPASSRLS`), migration-provisioned (`CREATE ROLE IF NOT EXISTS`), chart wires the connection string.
- `SET LOCAL app.tenant_id` issued once per request-scoped transaction (new FastAPI dependency wrapping the existing async session factory) and once per worker/runner claim transaction.
- New `apps/api/tests/test_rls_coverage.py`, run in `ci.yaml`: introspects `pg_policies` and fails if any table in a maintained tenant-scoped table list lacks a `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` policy.
- Health endpoint extended to report RLS-policy coverage count and default-tenant presence.

**De-risk evidence:** a throwaway spike (never committed) already confirmed the load-bearing mechanism against this codebase's exact engine shape (`create_async_engine(url, pool_pre_ping=True)`, asyncpg, default SQLAlchemy pool, no pgbouncer): two tenants isolated under a non-superuser `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` role even under a size-1 pool forcing full connection reuse, and a transaction that skips `SET LOCAL` denied (not served a leaked tenant's rows) both on a connection that just served another tenant's transaction and on a connection that has never touched the GUC at all. Sixteen interleaved concurrent transactions across a 2-connection pool showed zero cross-tenant reads. One implementation note the spike surfaced: the deny path throws two different exception types depending on connection history (`InvalidTextRepresentationError` on a warm connection vs. `UndefinedObjectError` on a cold one) -- the new session dependency should catch `DBAPIError` broadly around the query, not pattern-match one specific exception class.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Two tenants' bots, provider installations, and identity links cannot be read or written across the RLS boundary: a dedicated test connects as `curie_app` and asserts a cross-tenant SELECT/UPDATE returns zero rows.
- The CI gate fails when a tenant table in the maintained list lacks a policy.
- A restart-recovery test asserts no connection-pool-level tenant leakage across pooled connections.
- Enabling this by default needs the widest test coverage in the set, per ADR 0155.

**Depends on:** #2906, #2911, and every other `+ tenant_id` amendment (approvals, console_sessions, thread_workspaces, agent_actions, workflow_state_entries, credential_redemption_audit_entries, approval_audit_entries, action_audit_entries).

items.title: Hackathon [Feature]: Add Microsoft Teams data-source connector
items.body:
### Problem Statement

cognee has **five** data-source connectors today (`confluence`, `gmail`, `google-drive`, `notion`, `slack`) against roughly 25 planned. Data sources are the thinnest surface in the project — agent integrations number 20 and store adapters 25.

**Microsoft Teams** is on the roadmap and has no connector.

### Proposed Solution

Add a `teams` connector under `packages/connector/teams/` in [cognee-community](https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee-community), following the shape of the five existing connectors.

- **Auth:** Microsoft Graph with an Entra ID app registration
- **Ingest:** channel messages and threads for selected teams/channels
- **Incremental sync:** Graph delta queries
- **Forget-on-delete:** deleting upstream must remove the record from the graph on the next sync

### Watch out for

Message-history scopes need **tenant admin consent** — an end user cannot self-serve, so the setup docs matter more than usual. Start with channels only; skip 1:1 and private chats. Coordinate with the SharePoint and Outlook issues: all three share one Graph app registration, so agree who builds it first.

### Package layout to follow

```
packages/connector/teams/
├── README.md
├── cognee_community_connector_teams/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   └── teams.py
├── examples/
├── tests/
└── pyproject.toml
```

Read `packages/connector/notion/` first — it is the closest working reference.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A user connects via Microsoft Graph with an Entra ID app registration and selects what to ingest
- [ ] Selected content is ingested and searchable in cognee
- [ ] Incremental sync picks up only what changed since the last run
- [ ] Deleting the source upstream removes it from the graph on the next sync
- [ ] README with setup steps and a runnable example under `examples/`
- [ ] Tests covering the ingest path and the incremental cursor

### Context

Part of the **05.09 hackathon** — data-source connectors. Connectors are fully parallel work: each is self-contained, so contributors don't block each other.

---

### Build it on dlt — use the REST API source

**All cognee connectors are dlt sources.** There is no dlt verified source for this service, so **do not hand-write HTTP calls** — use dlt's declarative REST API source:

📦 **https://dlthub.com/docs/dlt-ecosystem/verified-sources/rest_api**

It gives you pagination, auth, incremental cursors and retries declaratively, which is most of the work in a connector. Hand-rolled `requests` loops will be sent back.

Then layer cognee's semantics on top:

1. Configure the endpoints, pagination and auth via `rest_api`.
2. Decide **document path vs relational path** — set `DOCUMENT_SOURCE_ATTR` for prose, leave it unset for structured rows.
3. Set `write_disposition` deliberately (`replace` for full snapshot so deletions propagate via `orphan_cleanup`; `merge` only if the API has a real delete feed).
4. Wrap it in the standard `packages/connector/<name>/` layout with a single `<name>_source` factory.

Coordinate with #4543 and #4544 — all three sit on Microsoft Graph, so the `rest_api` client config (auth, paging, delta) should be written once and shared.

items.title: Harden from_secret, connector egress, and SA automount before enabling the connector reconciler (ADR-0090)
items.body:
**This is a precondition to land BEFORE `worker.connectorReconciler.enabled` is ever turned on, not a live vulnerability.** Filing it now because ADR-0090 makes `from_secret:` the very mechanism that lets an unattended in-cluster identity apply connectors — and that is the moment the trigger for the issues below drops from "operator" to "anyone who can push to an agent repo."

Refs ADR-0090, #1184, #1163. Introduced by #1186.

## Why it is not a vulnerability today

Stated plainly so this is not mistaken for a security incident:

- The only wired path that applies connector objects is `curie cluster deploy` (`cli/src/main.rs:2624` → `sync_connectors`). It requires the platform API key **and** namespace kubectl-write.
- That principal already has the credentials trivially: `cli/src/ops.rs:2196-2204`, `discover_api_key`, reads the chart Secret directly via `read_release_secret(namespace, release, "apiKey")`. The operator fetches `<release>-secrets` as a routine step of running the command.
- The product is single-tenant by construction — ADR-0008:7-8, *"Curie is single-tenant by construction today, which is correct for the self-host case: one install is one company"* — and `grep -rn "tenant_id" --include=*.py --include=*.rs apps/ packages/ cli/` returns nothing.
- `charts/curie/values.yaml:592-593` has `connectorReconciler.enabled: false`, and the reconciler modules have no non-test caller.
- `apps/api/src/curie_api/gitflow.py` contains zero occurrences of `connector`, so the push-triggered path provably does not apply connector objects.

So no trust boundary is crossed at this commit. What follows is what changes when #1184 lands.

## What changes when the reconciler is wired

ADR-0090:104-110 scopes the reconciler to `from_secret:` connectors precisely because a reconciler cannot resolve credentials but can point at a Secret that already exists. That is the right design. Its consequence is that the principal who chooses the Secret reference stops being the operator running `cluster deploy` and becomes whoever authors `connectors.yaml` in the agent repo.

At that point the three gaps below become reachable by a repo-pusher.

## Gap 1 — `from_secret` is unfenced

`packages/plugin-format/src/plugin_format/connectors.py:246` accepts any nonempty Secret name and key. Nothing constrains the reference to connector-credential Secrets. `packages/plugin-format/src/plugin_format/connector_render.py:210` places it into the env of the bundle-supplied image.

The chart's platform Secret has a predictable release-derived name (`charts/curie/templates/secrets.yaml:32`) and holds `apiKey`, `githubToken`, `slackBotToken`, `postgresPassword`, `agentCredentials`, and the Langfuse credentials together. Real render output for a connector referencing it:

```
validation_errors=[]
rendered_env=[{"name": "STOLEN_PLATFORM_KEY", "valueFrom": {"secretKeyRef":
  {"key": "apiKey", "name": "audit-curie-secrets", "optional": false}}}]
```

Kubernetes itself does not restrict which Secret in its namespace a pod may reference, so the control has to be at the Curie layer. The only restriction present today is ownership-based (`connector_apply.py:93-100` refuses objects lacking this agent's `curie.dev/connector-owner` label), which does nothing about the *contents* of an object it does accept.

This is a genuine capability increase over "the operator runs an arbitrary image in a connector pod", because the connector pod's ServiceAccount has no Secret-read RBAC of its own.

Note this is **not** #1129, which covers the secret-name character class and reserved names, and whose AC3 pushes toward *loosening* the hosted path.

## Gap 2 — connector pods are outside the default-deny egress rail

`charts/curie/templates/security-networkpolicy.yaml:79-83` selects sandbox pods; the connector Deployment's labels (`connector_render.py:346-350`) do not match that selector. So a connector pod is not covered by the rail that would otherwise bound where it can send what it has mounted.

## Gap 3 — connector pods automount a ServiceAccount token

No `automountServiceAccountToken: false` on the rendered Deployment.

## Suggested fix, all three before the reconciler is enabled

1. Reject a `from_secret` reference that names the chart's platform Secret (`curie.secretName` / the `<release>-secrets` pattern). Stronger and preferable: require an opt-in label on the target Secret, so the referencable set is declared by the operator rather than denied by pattern.
2. Attach the default-deny egress rail to connector pods, or give them their own equivalent policy.
3. Set `automountServiceAccountToken: false` on the connector Deployment.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `connectors.yaml` whose `from_secret` names the platform Secret fails `validate_bundle`, with a negative mutation proving the check bites.
- A rendered connector Deployment is selected by an egress NetworkPolicy — asserted against the rendered chart, not against the helper, and proven by a selector-mismatch mutation going red.
- The rendered connector Deployment sets `automountServiceAccountToken: false`.
- A note on #1184 that these are preconditions for enabling `connectorReconciler`.

Found by an independent (non-Claude) review engine and confirmed against the real validator, the real renderer, and a rendered chart. The HIGH security framing it originally carried was refuted on the principal and tenancy grounds set out at the top; this issue is the accurate residue.

items.title: Personal AI cannot access account-owned Gmail/Calendar and incorrectly falls back to workspace scope
items.body:
## Problem

In **Personal Operly / `/channels/@me`**, account-owned Google capabilities are not being resolved as personal capabilities. The runtime still appears to peg the user to a workspace/tenant when invoking Google Calendar/Gmail.

Observed behavior:

- The user has a **Personal Google** account connected to their Operly profile.
- From Personal AI, asking for the personal Google Calendar causes Operly to say the Google account is not linked to **"My workspace"** and therefore Calendar cannot be read.
- In another Personal AI conversation, explicitly asking it to use `google.calendar` makes it check the **ANHITRA workspace** because that is the workspace with an active Calendar connection.
- This means a private/account-scoped request is being resolved through workspace connector availability instead of the user's own account-owned connector.
- Gmail appears to suffer from the same scope problem, which also explains why personal Gmail-backed scheduled tasks can fail even though the personal Google account is connected.

This is not the desired Personal AI model. Personal AI should be rooted at the authenticated **user/account principal**, not at a default or currently selected workspace.

## Expected behavior

For a request made in Personal AI:

```text
Personal AI request
  -> authenticated user principal
  -> discover account-owned capabilities/connectors
  -> resolve user's Personal Google connection
  -> invoke gmail/calendar under that user principal
```

It should **not** require the Personal Google connector to be attached to `My workspace`, ANHITRA, or any other workspace.

Workspace-owned Google connectors should remain separately discoverable when Personal AI intentionally reaches into a workspace the user is authorized to access, but they must not replace or shadow the user's personal connector.

## Scope / likely bug

Please inspect the Personal AI capability-resolution path for assumptions such as:

- requiring `tenant_id` / active workspace before connector lookup;
- looking up connector installation by workspace first or exclusively;
- using a default workspace as the principal for `/channels/@me`;
- capability-availability logic that only enumerates workspace-owned installations;
- Google plugin bindings keyed only by workspace/tenant;
- scheduler execution rehydrating a workspace context for a personal task;
- fallback behavior that silently substitutes a workspace connector when an account-owned connector is unavailable to the resolver.

The key invariant should be:

```text
/channels/@me => account scope first
workspace channel => workspace scope
```

Personal AI may deliberately traverse authorized workspaces, but the reverse must not be implicit and personal connectors must be first-class.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user with a Personal Google connection can ask Personal AI to list today's Calendar events without connecting Google to any workspace.
- [ ] Personal AI can search/read the user's personal Gmail using the account-owned Google connector.
- [ ] Personal Google capabilities appear in capability discovery for `/channels/@me` independently of workspace installations.
- [ ] The runtime does not require or synthesize a `tenant_id` merely to execute an account-scoped read.
- [ ] If both personal and workspace Google connectors exist, the resolver preserves ownership/scope and does not silently substitute one for the other.
- [ ] A Personal AI request that explicitly asks for a particular workspace's Calendar may use that workspace connector only after normal authorization checks.
- [ ] Personal scheduled tasks (for example Gmail summaries) rehydrate the **user/account principal** and can use personal connectors without a workspace binding.
- [ ] Tests cover Personal AI with zero workspace Google connections and at least one account-owned Google connection.
- [ ] Tests cover multiple workspace Google connections plus one personal connection and verify correct connector selection/provenance.

## Related

- #84 — Separate personal account scope from workspaces and require explicit delegation of personal data
- #110 — Add principal-scoped approvals for Personal AI connector side effects

#110 is primarily about governed **side effects/approvals**. This issue is the more basic resolver/runtime bug: even read-only Personal Google capabilities are currently being treated as if they must belong to a workspace.

items.title: release-blocker: reconcile RLS migration with append-only policy and staging ledger
items.body:
## Status: BLOCKED — no database changes made

### Verified evidence
- `scripts/self_audit.py` defines append-only migration history against reviewed baseline `c7976fa555ce5721f112bb0fb03e5b8b2e078c73`; existing migrations cannot be edited/deleted without explicit human review of the policy baseline.
- `supabase/migrations/20261008050300_saas_rls_performance_hardening.sql` creates `tenant_id` policies across workspace-scoped tables.
- Read-only Supabase migration ledger for known QROS Staging ref `yebwhcntiockckhdvawt` lists 46 entries and ends at `20261005050000_dataset_version_feed_reconciliation`; it does not list `20261008050300`.
- Read-only schema inspection on that ref shows the affected tables have no `tenant_id` columns, generally have `workspace_id`, and no legacy `tenant_select/insert/update/delete` policies. This establishes staging schema/ledger drift; it does not establish the production target or its migration history.
- PR #775 is closed and unmerged. Its proposed forward-only cleanup cannot by itself fix a fresh replay if the earlier migration fails before the forward migration is reached.

### Required next actions
1. Identify and verify the actual production Supabase project and read its migration ledger/schema. Do not infer production identity from the separately accessible `Boljoo_Project` project.
2. Decide through explicit maintainer review whether the append-only baseline/policy needs a governed exception or whether the legacy migration can be made replay-safe under an approved policy. Do not silently change the baseline or rewrite migration history.
3. Build a disposable clean-database replay test against the exact main migration sequence, then add a forward-only, fail-closed reconciliation only if it works for both clean replay and existing staging state.
4. Assert workspace membership isolation and server-only denies; rerun Supabase DB security tests and all required CI on the exact head SHA.
5. Apply no migration to staging or production until project identity, ledger, SQL replay, and approval are documented.

### Acceptance criteria
- Exact target project IDs and migration ledgers recorded (staging and production separately).
- Clean replay passes without editing historical migrations unless an explicitly reviewed policy exception authorizes it.
- Workspace-scoped RLS is preserved; no client policies added to server-only tables; no `tenant_id` legacy policy recreated.
- Exact-head CI and Supabase security tests pass.
- Production deployment remains blocked until all release evidence is attached.

References: PR #775 https://github.com/bi421/QROS/pull/775 ; self-audit policy docs https://github.com/bi421/QROS/blob/main/docs/operations/SELF_AUDIT.md
