items.title: Google Health connector: improve first-time setup guidance and add a screenshot-based walkthrough

labels.name: portal
labels.description: The meta-website, for the docs, config generation, etc.

labels.name: get-involved
labels.description: Not necessarily code-related, but things that are actionable issues

labels.name: effort:S
labels.description: One layer, under about 150 lines, no migration, no design call

items.body:
## Context and positive outcome

We observed four people live while they configured the Google Health connector. The participants had little or no technical experience.

**All four successfully connected their accounts.** This is a positive result: the connection flow was achievable. However, most experienced it as difficult because the interface did not provide enough direct guidance about where to start, what each step expected, and what to do after connecting.

This issue collects the first usability feedback for a later follow-up. It covers first-time setup guidance and user-facing documentation.

## Findings and proposed improvements

### 1. Make Google Cloud setup an obvious starting point

The **Google Cloud setup** section sits relatively far down the connector page. Participants did not immediately recognize that it was clickable or that it was the place to begin on their first installation.

- Bring the setup entry point near the top of the first-time flow.
- Give it a clear action label, such as **Start here: set up Google Cloud**.
- Make its expandable/clickable behavior obvious, or show the essential instructions by default when no configuration has been saved.
- Distinguish first-time setup from editing an existing connection.

### 2. Put the setup documentation link before the instructions

The **Google setup documentation** link currently appears below the four steps. It should appear above them, with a short invitation to use the guide for detailed instructions before continuing.

Provide a prominent link to a Nocturne-specific walkthrough as well as the relevant official Google documentation. Readers should understand which guide explains the complete Nocturne flow and which link provides Google's reference instructions.

### 3. Make the four setup steps more specific

Although participants could follow the steps, they were often unsure what result was expected.

Explain, for each step:

- Which Google Cloud screen to open and which button or field to use.
- What project, application and OAuth client names to enter, with examples.
- Which names are arbitrary labels, which appear on the consent screen, and which values must match exactly.
- How to enable the API, configure consent, add the correct test account, choose the Web application client type, and register Nocturne's exact callback URL.
- Where the client ID and client secret come from and where to paste them in Nocturne.
- How to recognize that the step is complete and safely proceed to the next one.

Avoid assuming familiarity with Google Cloud, OAuth clients, consent screens or redirect URIs.

### 4. Make the Client Secret field invite the correct action

The current placeholder, **Leave empty to keep the saved secret**, discouraged participants from entering a secret, including during first-time setup. They interpreted it as an instruction to leave the field empty.

Use wording appropriate to the state:

- **First setup:** invite the user to paste their Google OAuth client secret, for example **Paste your client secret here**.
- **Existing configuration:** explain that the saved secret is retained unless they paste a replacement, preferably as helper text rather than an instruction occupying the input.

Removing the placeholder is also preferable to wording that looks like a prohibition. Explain secret handling without exposing the saved value.

### 5. Explain that connecting is not the final synchronization step

After connecting to Google, participants still needed to review and confirm the data types to synchronize. This was not immediately obvious.

- Distinguish **Google account connected** from **Data selection confirmed / import started**.
- Show the next action prominently after authorization: review the available data, select the desired supported types, then choose **Save selection and import**.
- Explain why this confirmation is needed and how to tell that synchronization has actually started.
- Keep the next-step guidance visible until the user has completed the required selection.

### 6. Document the required Google Health app and the data-source chain

The Google Health mobile app is a prerequisite, not an optional recommendation. Users need to install/open it and link their Google Health profile to the **same Google Account** they authorize in Nocturne, before starting the consent flow. This requirement should be visible at the beginning of setup.

Also explain the relationship between **Google Health**, **Health Connect**, and other apps or devices that supply health data. Participants should understand how supported third-party data can reach Google Health through other routes, and consequently become available to this connector.

Document supported routes, permissions and limitations explicitly. Do not imply that all data stored locally in Health Connect, or every third-party data type, automatically becomes available through the Google Health API.

Google's reference material:
- [Link Google Health before OAuth consent](https://developers.google.com/health/setup#link-google-health-before-oauth-consent)
- [Health Connect and the Google Health app](https://support.google.com/googlehealth/answer/14506680?hl=en)

## Explain what Google Cloud/API setup actually does

Participants did not understand the impact of setting up the API and OAuth client, or why these resources were necessary.

Add a plain-language explanation of how the connector works:

- The user enables Google's existing Health API and creates OAuth credentials for their own project; they are not creating a new health API or a new source of measurements.
- Explain what the project, consent configuration, client ID, client secret and callback URL each do.
- Explain what access the user grants, which read-only data permissions Nocturne requests, and where imported data is stored.
- Explain how credentials are protected and how access can be revoked or the connector disconnected.
- Describe applicable API-access prerequisites, testing/publishing behavior, quotas and any billing implications using current official references; avoid unexplained assumptions about availability or cost.
- Show a simple data-flow explanation from the originating app/device, through the supported Google Health/Health Connect route, to the Google Health API and Nocturne.

## Publish a complete, discoverable walkthrough

There needs to be a clear, permanent home for an extensive **Google Health connector guide** in the central [Nocturne documentation](https://getnocturne.dev/docs), for example under **Connectors → Google Health**.

The existing [technical Google Health document](https://github.com/nightscout/nocturne/blob/main/docs/google-health.md) is useful background, but users need a complete walkthrough linked directly from the connector page. The central site's documentation sources currently live in `src/Web/packages/portal/src/content/docs`.

The guide should include:

- Prerequisites, including the Google Health app/account link and the role of Health Connect where relevant.
- A step-by-step Google Cloud and OAuth walkthrough with annotated screenshots, example names, and the expected outcome after each step.
- The corresponding Nocturne fields and screenshots showing exactly where to paste each value.
- The consent/connection flow, followed by data selection, confirmation and starting the first import.
- Screenshots showing successful connection, confirmed selection, and visible import/sync progress.
- Common setup mistakes and how to recognize and resolve them.
- An explanation of the connector's data flow, permissions and the impact of enabling the API.

Screenshots must use example accounts and redact secrets, tokens and personal health data. Keep the walkthrough discoverable from both the documentation navigation and the connector's first-time setup interface.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] First-time users can immediately identify where to start Google Cloud setup.
- [ ] Documentation links appear before the setup steps and explain why readers should open them.
- [ ] Every setup step states the required action, example values where appropriate, and the expected result.
- [ ] Client Secret wording clearly distinguishes first-time entry from preserving/replacing a saved secret.
- [ ] The post-connection interface makes data selection and import confirmation an explicit next step.
- [ ] The Google Health app/account prerequisite and supported Health Connect/third-party data routes are documented before authorization.
- [ ] The purpose and impact of Google Cloud/API/OAuth setup are explained in plain language.
- [ ] A dedicated central documentation page provides a complete, screenshot-based walkthrough and is linked from the connector.
- [ ] Repeat the first-time setup test with nontechnical participants and check whether they can identify and complete the steps without live prompting.

items.title: Task: Azure connector — inventory reads, tags, Resource Graph across allowed subscriptions, bulk targets
items.body:
**What will be true when done:**

- An agent lists subscriptions, resource groups, resources (filtered by type), tag names with their values, and locks.
- An agent changes tags on one resource after a person approves (merge or remove, nothing else).
- `azure.graph.query` runs a read-only Resource Graph query (KQL) over a set of subscriptions. MEHO checks each subscription against the caller's permissions first. The result and the audit row list the requested, completed, denied and failed subscriptions.
- `azure.inventory.summary` counts resources by type, subscription and location. Three fixed queries list VMs, AKS clusters and network resources across the same set.
- `meho targets discover azure --seed-target <target>` lists the subscriptions the seed's login can see that are not targets yet, ready to register in bulk with `meho targets import`.

Ready for coding: not yet (the code is merged in PR #5161; only the live proof on the lab Azure tenant is left)

## What changes and why

Paths below are under `backend/src/meho_backplane/` unless they start with `cli/` or `docs/`.

- MEHO checks permissions per operation and per target (`docs/codebase/agent-permission-model.md`; `resolve_verdict` in `auth/permissions.py:383`). A Resource Graph query reads many subscriptions in one Azure call, so MEHO must check each subscription itself before it sends the query. Azure then returns only what the login can read. What the login could read never widens what the caller gets.
- No shipped multi-step operation runs across many targets yet. A child call can name another target (`operations/composite.py:353-356`, 469-496).
- `meho targets discover` calls `Connector.list_candidates` (`api/v1/targets.py:1047-1099`). The base returns `[]` (`connectors/base.py:247-266`), and no connector overrides it yet. The operator reviews the candidates; `meho targets import` (`cli/internal/cmd/targets/import.go`) registers many targets from one file.
- The audit row keeps a `payload` (`AuditLog`, `db/models.py:465`). Check what the dispatcher writes there and make sure the subscription lists show in it.

Azure facts (Microsoft docs):

- Subscriptions: `GET /subscriptions?api-version=2022-12-01`.
- Resource groups `GET /subscriptions/{s}/resourcegroups`, resources `GET /subscriptions/{s}/resources` with `$filter=resourceType eq '<type>'`, tag names `GET /subscriptions/{s}/tagNames`: all `api-version=2021-04-01` (the spec also has 2025-04-01; it is not proven live in every region, so use it only if the lab shows it works).
- Locks: `GET /subscriptions/{s}/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/locks?api-version=2020-05-01`.
- Tags on one resource: `PATCH {resourceId}/providers/Microsoft.Resources/tags/default?api-version=2021-04-01` with `operation` `Merge` or `Delete` (`Delete` removes only the named tags).
- Resource Graph: `POST /providers/Microsoft.ResourceGraph/resources?api-version=2024-04-01`. Body: `query`, `subscriptions[]`, `options` (`$top`, `$skip`, `$skipToken`, `resultFormat`). At most 1,000 rows per page; no `$skipToken` when the query uses `limit`, `take` or `sample`; a query times out after 30 seconds; send fewer than 300 subscriptions per query; above 10,000 subscriptions the answer is cut and says `x-ms-tenant-subscription-limit-hit: true`; results can lag a little behind changes. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/resource-graph/concepts/work-with-data

## What to build

1. Reads (group `inventory`, `safe`): `azure.subscription.list`, `azure.resource_group.list`, `azure.resource.list` (optional `type` and `resource_group`), `azure.tag.list`, `azure.lock.list`. All use the paging helper; big lists return a result handle.
2. `azure.tag.update` (group `inventory`, `caution`, approval): `resource_id`, `mode` (`merge` or `remove`), `tags`. The resource id must sit in the target's subscription. Safe to run twice: the same merge or remove gives the same end state.
3. Subscription set, shared code for every wider read: the parameter `subscriptions` holds names of other registered `azure` targets; the calling target is always in the set. For each name MEHO checks that it is an `azure` target of the caller's MEHO tenant, that the caller may run this operation on it (`resolve_verdict`), and that it uses the same secret reference as the calling target (one login per query; a target with another login is denied with that reason). The result carries `subscriptions: {requested, completed, denied, failed}`, each with its reason, and the audit row's payload shows the same lists.
4. `azure.graph.query` (group `inventory`, `safe`): `query`, `subscriptions`, optional `page_size`. MEHO fills `subscriptions[]` itself and never sends `managementGroups`. It pages with `$skipToken`, in batches of fewer than 300 subscriptions. Denied subscriptions, failed pages, the 10,000-subscription cut and the stored-result cap become named omissions.
5. `azure.inventory.summary` (`safe`): `Resources | summarize count() by subscriptionId, type, location` over the same set.
6. Fixed queries (`safe`): `azure.inventory.vm.list`, `azure.inventory.aks.list`, `azure.inventory.network.list`. Starting points (property names from Microsoft's samples, not yet checked live):
   - VMs: `Resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.compute/virtualmachines' | project name, subscriptionId, resourceGroup, location, size=tostring(properties.hardwareProfile.vmSize), os=tostring(properties.storageProfile.osDisk.osType), power=tostring(properties.extended.instanceView.powerState.code)`
   - AKS: `Resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' | mv-expand pool=properties.agentPoolProfiles | project cluster=name, location, k8s=tostring(properties.kubernetesVersion), pool=tostring(pool.name), vmSize=tostring(pool.vmSize), nodes=toint(pool['count']), mode=tostring(pool.mode)`
   - Network: virtual networks, network security groups, public IP addresses and load balancers, with name, subscription, resource group, location and address spaces.
7. `list_candidates(seed_target)`: one candidate per subscription the seed's login can see that is not yet a target, with the seed's secret reference, `host`, `tenant_id` and `cloud`. If `meho targets discover` has no output that `meho targets import` can read, add it.
8. Tests: the set check (denied, other login, unknown name); omissions; `nextLink` and `$skipToken` paging; a query whose text names another subscription stays inside the set; the tag update request shape.

## Rules

These rules are the same for every Task of this program.

- Typed and multi-step operations only. No spec ingestion. The pinned spec is used only by the CI check that every hand-written path exists.
- Risk level by effect. Reads are `safe`, also read-only POST queries. Starting work on the customer's side is `caution` and needs approval. Role assignment changes and download links are `dangerous` and need approval. No VM power actions and no resource deletes.
- Every operation has a group and `when_to_use` text. A `safe` op id contains no write word (`WRITE_WORDS` in `backend/src/meho_backplane/delete_names.py`, for example `patch`, `run`, `set`, `scale`, `power`, `import`).
- A list over 50 rows or 4 KB comes back as a link to the stored result (a result handle), never as the raw list.
- Secrets never reach audit text, logs, traces or stored results: no tokens, client secrets, download links, keys or connection strings. Text from Azure (names, descriptions, messages) is untrusted data (#5032).
- The operation contract test passes (`backend/tests/test_operation_contracts.py`). Add nothing to `backend/tests/data/operation_contract_gaps.yaml`.
- File layout like `backend/src/meho_backplane/connectors/vra8/`: `_paths.py` (hand-written paths), `typed_reads.py` (operation bodies), `_llm_instructions.py`, `typed_ops.py` (op table, group texts, registrar), and the registrar wired in `__init__.py`. The connector class sits on the HTTP base (`connectors/adapters/http.py`).
- CI chores in the same pull request: `cd cli && make snapshot-openapi && make generate && make cli-docs`; `cd backend && uv run python scripts/generate_reference_docs.py`; the flight-recorder list (`_EXPECTED_TYPED_IMPLS` in `backend/tests/test_flight_recorder_typed_spans.py`) when a new implementation appears; every new vendor path in the spec path check.
- Before the pull request: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests/ -q -n auto`, `uv run ruff check src/ tests/`, `uv run ruff format --check src/ tests/` and `uv run mypy src/` pass. No change to `CHANGELOG.md` (the release pull request adds the line).
- Tests and fixtures use made-up names and ids, never a real tenant, subscription or object id.
- Plain language in code comments, docs and the pull request text.

## Lab proof (done when)

Permission boundary (P3), paging and omissions (P4), and live read of real objects (P10):

- [ ] Each read lists real objects in the lab subscription: resource groups, resources of a known type, tags, locks. An empty list proves nothing.
- [ ] `azure.inventory.summary` counts match the portal's resource count, or the small difference is explained.
- [ ] A caller allowed only target A cannot read subscription B: not through `azure.graph.query`, not through a resource id in `azure.tag.update`, not through a paging link, not through a multi-step operation. Use a second lab subscription if access to one is granted; otherwise fixtures, and the proof note says so.
- [ ] Resource Graph with a forced small page size reads all pages. A denied subscription, a failed page and a result over 10,000 rows (fixtures) show as named omissions.
- [ ] `azure.tag.update` waits for approval, then merges one tag on a lab test resource; running it twice gives the same tags. (The write login needs the Tag Contributor role on the test resource group; ask the lab team.)
- [ ] `meho targets discover azure --seed-target <lab target>` lists the subscriptions the login sees.
- [ ] The result is recorded in the lab proof log, and a comment on this Task says so.

items.title: Task: Measure the tool and start-text changes that v0.46.0 turned on for every session, or put them behind a switch

labels.name: sandbox-test
labels.description: A test Task that a sandbox seat runs live against the sandbox MEHO

items.body:
**Parent:** #4067
Code repo: evoila/meho
Work type: Sandbox test
Ready for coding: yes for the measurement; a switch only if the score drops

**In short:** v0.46.0 changed some tool texts and the session start text for every MCP session, with no switch. Nobody measured them. This Task runs one before-and-after benchmark batch. If the score drops, the change goes behind a switch that is off by default.

## Goal

We know if the always-on text changes of v0.46.0 help, hurt or do nothing, for a small open model and for Claude.

## Why

- The rule of 8 November 2026 (see #4067): a change to what the model sees ships behind a switch that is off by default, or it is measured before it becomes the default.
- These changes reached every session in v0.46.0 with no switch and no score:
  - #5981: `meho_connector_list` takes `target` and shows which connectors fit it. The tool text is longer.
  - #5992: `meho_status` shows the server time in UTC. Its text was cut to stay under the size limit.
  - #5997: the shorter `query_topology` text. (The switch in that PR only covers taking the tool off the list.)
  - #5951: `search_knowledge` and `search_memory` take filters and `scope`; hits carry `tenant_id` and `shared`. Other tool texts were cut to stay under 70,000 characters.
  - #5995: more cuts to the `search_knowledge` and `add_to_knowledge` texts for the size limit.
  - #6020: a session that is not an agent gets a shorter broadcast part in its start text; `meho_broadcast_announce` starts with "Agents only".
  - #5993: a call on a target of another kind answers `target_connector_mismatch`.
- Each PR wrote a measurement plan. None has numbers. The benchmark MEHO still runs the 7 November build, so no batch has seen these changes yet.

## How

1. Before: a batch on a build from before these changes (the 7 November build the benchmark already uses is fine).
2. After: the same tasks, models, harness and runs on a v0.46.0 build (all switches at their defaults).
3. One small open model and Claude Sonnet 5.5. Three runs per task. Add one task where the agent first picks a target of the wrong kind (from the #5993 plan).
4. Compare per task and per model: pass rate, tool calls before the first right `call_operation`, tokens, made-up op ids.
5. Write both tables on this Task and on #4067.
6. If a model's score drops, open a follow-up PR that puts the change behind a switch that is off by default.

## Done when

- [ ] Both batches ran on one task list and one harness. The two build ids are written down.
- [ ] The before-and-after table is on this Task and on #4067.
- [ ] Each listed change is marked "keep" or "put behind a switch", with the reason.
- [ ] Every change marked "put behind a switch" has its own follow-up Task.

items.title: [ME-05] Tenant-scoped dead-letter self-service
items.body:
Allow tenant administrators to view and replay their own failed async jobs without
requiring platform-admin intervention. Server enforces tenant isolation — callers
can only see and replay jobs where `job.data.tenant_id` matches their canonical JWT
`tenant_id`. This is a later capability after the underlying queues and redaction rules
are proven.

Queues exposed to tenants (jobs that directly impact their operations):
  - credential.state-update — failed to correlate a webhook from the agent to an Operation
  - webhook.dispatch — delivery to the tenant's registered webhook URL failed after all retries
  - audit.write — failed to persist an audit log entry
  - credential.bulk-item — a single item in a bulk issuance/revocation batch failed

Endpoints:
  - GET /api/v1/tenants/:tenantId/events/dead-letter
      Query params: queue (filter), since, until, cursor, limit
      Returns: TenantDeadLetterJob[] — redacted of sensitive fields; correlation IDs only
  - POST /api/v1/tenants/:tenantId/events/dead-letter/:jobId/replay
      Validates job.data.tenant_id === jwt.tenant_id before calling boss.resume(id)
      Returns 404 if job not found or belongs to another tenant (indistinguishable by design)
      Returns 202 on success

Security:
  - tenant_id filter applied server-side from JWT (never from request params)
  - Job data is redacted before returning — only correlation IDs (operation_id, external_id,
    webhook_id) are exposed, not raw credential attributes or connector secrets
  - Requires tenants:admin scope

Implementation note:
  - Queries `pgboss.job` WHERE state = 'failed' AND data->>'tenant_id' = $1
  - Index on `(data->>'tenant_id', state)` required for acceptable query performance
  - Add GIN index on job.data for JSONB path filtering

### Dependencies
- Blocked by #90

### Definition of Done
- [ ] Implementation complete and builds without errors
- [ ] Unit/integration tests pass
- [ ] PR reviewed and approved
- [ ] No regressions in existing functionality
- [ ] API endpoints documented (if applicable)

items.title: ⚙️[기능추가][Connector] 범용 데이터 연동 프레임워크와 물품 표준 모델
items.body:
## 📝 왜 필요한가

외부 시스템 데이터를 우리 안으로 들여오는 일이 앞으로 계속 생긴다. 그런데 원천은 회사마다·
시스템마다 다르다. 엑셀로 주기도, JSON으로 주기도, API로 주기도 한다.

원천마다 Java 코드를 새로 쓰면 세 가지가 따라온다.

- 새 발주사·새 원천이 붙을 때마다 배포가 필요하다
- 원천 양식이 바뀌면 코드를 고쳐야 한다
- 도메인 로직과 파싱 코드가 뒤엉켜 어느 쪽도 손대기 어려워진다

**연동 정의를 데이터로 두면 셋 다 사라진다.** 새 원천은 화면에서 커넥터를 하나 더 만드는
일이 되고, 양식 변경은 매핑 버전을 올리는 일이 된다.

재고 정합성 대사(#49)를 첫 구현체로 삼되, **연동 엔진 자체는 도메인을 모르게** 만든다.

## 🛠️ 작업 상세 내용

### 1. 새 모듈 `palim-connector`

범용 연동 엔진. 도메인을 모른다. `palim-automation` 이 이 위에 얹힌다.

- [ ] `settings.gradle.kts` 에 모듈 추가, `palim-common` 만 의존
- [ ] `palim-automation` → `palim-connector` 의존 추가

`palim-automation` 안에 두면 나중에 다른 도메인이 붙을 때 재고 코드에 의존이 생긴다.

### 2. 연동 정의 계층 (마이그레이션 V15)

- [ ] `target_model` — 목표 모델. `kind`(BUILTIN/CUSTOM) · `storage`(TABLE/JSONB) · `natural_key_fields`
- [ ] `target_field` — 필드 정의. 키 · 표시명 · 타입 · 필수 · 기본값 · 순서
- [ ] `connector` — 연동 하나. 원천 유형 · 접속 정보 참조 · cron · 증분 커서
- [ ] `connector_mapping` — **매핑 버전**. DRAFT/ACTIVE/ARCHIVED · 원천 스키마 스냅샷
- [ ] `connector_field_map` — 필드 연결 + 변환 규칙
- [ ] `unit_conversion` — 단위 환산 규칙 (품목별/전역)
- [ ] 전 테이블에 `tenant_id`. 지금은 기본 테넌트 하나로 운영하되 **나중에 넣으면 재작성**이다

### 3. 실행 계층

- [ ] `connector_run` — `run_mode`(TEST/LIVE) · 트리거 · **사용한 매핑 버전** · 건수
- [ ] `connector_run_error` — 실패 행을 **원본째로** 보존
- [ ] `custom_record` — 커스텀 모델 데이터 (JSONB + GIN)

### 4. 기본 제공 물품 표준 모델

물품이면 무엇이든 담기도록 성격이 다른 셋으로 나눈다. 빈 칸을 허용해 업종을 가리지 않는다.

- [ ] `item` — 품목 마스터 (식별·분류·공급·단위·금액·상태)
- [ ] `stock_snapshot` — 시점별 재고 (기준시각·위치·로트·수량·금액)
- [ ] `stock_movement` — 입출고 이력 (구분·수량·위치·전표)
- [ ] `outbound_order` — 출고 주문. **이 모델만 개인정보를 담는다**(수령자 정보). 보존기간·
      마스킹·접근권한을 여기에만 걸 수 있도록 분리
- [ ] 전 모델에 `attributes` JSONB 확장 슬롯 — 표준에 없는 컬럼을 버리지 않는다

처음에는 필요 없어 보이던 컬럼이 나중에 필요해지는 일이 반복된다. 버렸다면 원천에서 다시
받아야 하는데 **과거 시점 데이터는 다시 받을 수 없다.**

### 5. 저장 방식 — 하이브리드

- [ ] 기본 제공 모델은 정식 테이블, 커스텀 모델은 `custom_record` JSONB
- [ ] 둘 다 같은 파이프라인을 타고 **저장 직전에만 갈라진다**
- [ ] **런타임 DDL 금지** — 스키마 변경은 전부 Flyway. 앱 계정에 DDL 권한을 주지 않는다

동적 DDL은 마이그레이션과 충돌하고, 실패 시 롤백 경로가 없다.

### 6. 단위 환산

- [ ] 수량은 원본(`quantity`/`unit`)과 환산값(`base_quantity`/`base_unit`)을 **둘 다** 저장
- [ ] 품목별 규칙 → 전역 규칙 순으로 조회
- [ ] **규칙이 없으면 1:1로 넘기지 않고 실패시킨다**

조용히 통과시키면 BOX 12개가 EA 12개로 둔갑하고, 그 오류는 대사 결과가 이상해질 때까지
아무도 모른다.

### 7. 증분 수집과 자연키

- [ ] `incremental_mode`(FULL/INCREMENTAL) · `cursor_field` · `cursor_value`
- [ ] **성공한 실행만 커서를 전진**시킨다
- [ ] 적재는 INSERT 가 아니라 자연키 기반 **UPSERT**

재시도가 안전해야 자동화가 안심되고, 안심돼야 사람이 실제로 자동화를 켠다.

### 8. 온보딩 흐름 (8단계)

- [ ] 연동 만들기 → 원천 붙이기 → (선택) AI 분석 → 관리자 확인 → **테스트 연동** →
      후처리 설정 → 확정·cron 등록 → 운영
- [ ] 각 단계에서 중단·재개 가능 (매핑 `DRAFT` 보존)

### 9. AI 는 보조, 수동이 1급

- [ ] **AI 버튼을 한 번도 안 눌러도 전 과정이 완주된다**
- [ ] 헤더에서 필드 목록 추출은 코드가 한다. AI 는 매핑 초안만 제안
- [ ] AI 출력은 **구조화 출력(json_schema)** 으로 받아 코드가 검증
- [ ] **매일 도는 실행에는 AI 가 개입하지 않는다** — 비용 0, 같은 입력에 같은 결과

### 10. 후처리

- [ ] 선언적 규칙 (값 변환·필터·파생 컬럼·기본값) — 화면에서 선택
- [ ] py 훅 — 규칙으로 안 되는 커스텀. `04-CONVENTIONS` py 규약 준수
- [ ] **SQL 직접 실행은 넣지 않는다** — 공개 저장소이고 한 번 뚫리면 DB 전체가 열린다

py 훅은 DB 에 직접 손대지 않는다. 데이터를 받아 가공된 데이터를 돌려줄 뿐이라 잘못 짜도
테이블이 날아가지 않는다.

### 11. 안정성 장치

- [ ] **스키마 드리프트 감지** — 원천 필드가 스냅샷과 다르면 적재하지 않고 중단 + 알림
- [ ] **부분 실패 허용** — 성공분은 적재, 실패 행만 원본째 보존
- [ ] **실행 단위 롤백** — `run_id` 로 한 실행분만 정확히 삭제
- [ ] **동시 실행 차단** — 커넥터 단위 락 (cron 과 수동 실행이 겹치는 순간은 반드시 온다)
- [ ] **비밀값 분리** — API 키는 기존 암호화 저장 재사용, `connector` 에는 참조만

최악의 실패는 *원천 양식이 바뀌었는데 조용히 잘못된 데이터가 들어가는 것*이다.

### 12. 화면

- [ ] 커넥터 목록 · 만들기 위저드 · 매핑 편집기 · 미리보기 · 테스트 실행 결과 ·
      실행 이력 · 목표 모델 관리 · 단위 환산 규칙

### 13. 예외

- [ ] `ErrorCode` 추가 — `CONNECTOR_NOT_FOUND` · `CONNECTOR_ALREADY_RUNNING` ·
      `CONNECTOR_SOURCE_UNREACHABLE` · `MAPPING_NOT_ACTIVE` · `SCHEMA_DRIFT_DETECTED` ·
      `REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING` · `FIELD_TYPE_MISMATCH` · `UNIT_CONVERSION_NOT_FOUND` ·
      `HOOK_EXECUTION_FAILED` · `HOOK_TIMEOUT` · `TARGET_MODEL_IN_USE`
- [ ] `errors.properties` / `errors_en.properties` 각 한 줄씩
- [ ] 새 예외 클래스는 만들지 않는다

### 14. 테스트

- [ ] 단위 — 변환 규칙 엔진 · 단위 환산(규칙 없을 때 실패하는지) · 자연키 · 드리프트 감지
- [ ] 통합(Testcontainers) — **롤백이 정확히 그만큼만 지우는지**, **증분 재실행에 중복이
      없는지**

이 둘이 깨지면 사람이 시스템을 믿지 못하고, 믿지 못하면 쓰지 않는다.

## 📚 참고 자료

- 설계 문서: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-12-connector-framework-design.md`
- 첫 구현체: #49 재고 정합성 대사
- 코드 규약: `docs/04-CONVENTIONS.md` (예외·py 규약)
- 모듈 배치: `docs/02-ARCHITECTURE.md`

## ⚠️ 착수 전 정리할 것

| 항목 | 내용 |
|---|---|
| **`CLAUDE.md` 6번 개정** | 연동 정의 생성 시 원본 파일 전체를 AI 에 보내기로 결정했다. 현행 규칙("필요한 컬럼만, 개인 식별자 마스킹")과 충돌한다. 규칙을 고치거나 예외를 명시해야 리뷰·CI 에서 혼선이 없다. 완화 요소 — AI 호출은 **최초 연동 설정 1회**뿐이고, 개인정보를 담는 모델은 `outbound_order` 하나뿐이다 |
| ERP API 인증키 | 확인한 계정이 회사 마스터가 아니어서 발급 권한이 없었다. 마스터에게 요청 필요 |
| WAREHOUSE API 유료 결정 | 초기 세팅비 + 월 이용료. 발주사 판단 사항. 결정 전까지는 엑셀 업로드 경로로 진행 |
| 커스텀 모델 필드 타입 범위 | 문자열·숫자·날짜·불린까지인지, 배열·중첩 객체까지인지 |

## 🔎 범위 밖 (지금 만들지 않는 것)

| 항목 | 이유 |
|---|---|
| BOM 계층 구조 | 세트는 매핑 배수로 충분. 다품목 세트 실사례가 아직 없다 |
| 환율 변환 | 해외 거래가 없다. `currency` 필드만 남긴다 |
| 커스텀 모델 간 관계 | 요구가 없다. 넣으면 미니 ORM 을 만들게 된다 |
| 원천 유형 확장 (DB·FTP·이메일·웹훅) | 어댑터 인터페이스만 열어두면 클래스 추가로 끝난다 |
| 품목 마스터 이력(SCD) | 스냅샷이 원본 품명을 보존하므로 과거 설명은 가능하다 |

items.title: CF-01: Provision isolated Cloudflare staging integration
items.body:
## Objective
Complete CF-01 against isolated staging resources only. Do not change Production Cloudflare resources or the PRODX-ORG production database.

## Verified Cloudflare inventory (2026-11-11)
- Hyperdrive configurations: 0.
- Staging Queues exist: `prodx-pos-ingest-staging` and `prodx-pos-ingest-dlq-staging`.
- Both staging Queues currently have 0 producers and 0 consumers.
- Deployed Workers currently contain `prodx-oci-bridge`; `prodx-pos-edge-sync-staging` is not deployed.
- The existing Edge Sync Wrangler config still has placeholder Hyperdrive IDs and placeholder Access audiences.
- The existing Access inventory has only the broad `All Workers` application; no dedicated POS staging audience was verified.

## Database prerequisite
A separate `PRODX-POS-PREVIEW` Supabase project exists and reports ACTIVE_HEALTHY, but the Supabase connector could not authenticate to its database (PostgreSQL 28P01). No preview database password/connection string is available through the current connector context.

Do not reuse the PRODX-ORG production PostgreSQL credentials or decrypt Vercel production environment secrets for staging. Obtain a dedicated connection string for PRODX-POS-PREVIEW, or explicitly approve a separately costed development branch before creating one.

## Blocking finding: Access JWT claims do not match Edge Sync
The current Edge Sync `src/auth.ts` reads top-level `tenant_id`, `terminal_id`, and `role` from the Cloudflare Access JWT.

Cloudflare's documented service-token JWT contains `common_name` (the service token Client ID), `aud`, `iss`, `exp`, and related standard claims; it does not include the tenant/terminal claims required by `authenticate()`. Cloudflare documents custom IdP SAML/OIDC claims under the JWT's `custom` object, not as those top-level service-token claims.

Therefore, a Service Auth policy alone will not satisfy the current Edge Sync claim contract; requests will fail authorization before the mTLS/terminal mapping step. The tenant-operator path has the same top-level `role`/`tenant_id` expectation.

## Blocking finding: Free-plan device authentication is unresolved
The repository already contains `docs/edge-sync-free-plan-device-auth-rfc.md`, whose status is **Proposal only — not approved for implementation**. It records that Access mTLS CA/settings are not configured. Cloudflare documentation (last updated 2026-11-02) states Access mTLS is available only on Enterprise and pay-as-you-go Zero Trust plans, not Free. The connected account currently has zero Access certificate authorities and zero Cloudflare zones. The Vercel Preview proxy cannot preserve the original TLS identity of a physical POS terminal.

Do not implement that RFC or replace the current mTLS check without an explicit architecture decision. Keep the current authentication gate intact until a Free-compatible terminal identity design is approved and proven with tests.

## CI interpretation
The repository's Delivery Gate includes PostgreSQL/Edge unit and chaos checks. Its own Edge Sync README states that the 300-terminal CI harness uses `POS_CI_MODE=true` against the PostgreSQL CTE directly; it does **not** prove a deployed Cloudflare Worker, real Durable Object alarms, or a live Cloudflare Queue consumer. A green CI load test must not be reported as Cloudflare staging E2E.

## Updated implementation sequence (supersedes the earlier Hyperdrive-first sequence)
1. Use the owner-approved existing `PRODX-POS-PREVIEW` project (`jciucoqfmjuenssleyzo`, PostgreSQL 17.11, ap-southeast-1) as the isolated Staging database.
2. Refactor the Edge Worker so it does not write financial data directly to the legacy Edge schema. All sale commits must call the trusted backend integration endpoint and the existing `CheckoutService`.
3. Finalize B1–B8 contracts: service/device identity, mTLS certificate mapping, signed offline price proof, sequence/HLC authority, idempotency scope, payment/tender semantics, RLS/grants, and queue receipt semantics.
4. Decide whether any non-financial Edge persistence is still required. If yes, define its schema and least-privilege role first. Do not create Hyperdrive merely to support the current legacy direct-write code. Hyperdrive may be omitted entirely if the Worker only calls the backend.
5. Obtain Preview connection details through the Supabase Dashboard and configure any required database connection directly in Cloudflare securely. Never paste credentials into chat, source control, or reuse Production/Vercel secrets; do not reset the password as a workaround.
6. Configure a dedicated staging Access audience and approved device identity/mTLS mechanism; the current account inventory has no dedicated POS app or Access certificate CA.
7. Bind the existing staging Queues to the refactored Worker and deploy only after the trusted adapter and identity contracts are implemented and reviewed.
8. Verify live staging Worker -> Queue -> backend -> existing CheckoutService -> committed receipt -> Edge acknowledgement, including RLS, replay, retries/DLQ and reconciliation.
9. Keep Production configuration and data untouched.

## Owner decision and latest verified state (2026-11-11)
- Owner confirmed `PRODX-POS-PREVIEW` as the CF-01 Staging database.
- Preview has 39 PRODX public tables, RLS enabled on all 39, 36 policies and 50 Supabase migration records. The `prodx_app` login role is `NOBYPASSRLS`; all 39 PRODX tables are owned by `postgres`.
- Cloudflare inventory: 0 Hyperdrive configs; the two staging Queues exist but have 0 consumers; only `prodx-oci-bridge` is deployed; no `prodx-pos-edge-sync-staging` Worker; one broad `All Workers` Access app; 0 Access short-lived certificate CAs.
- The current Edge Worker still directly reads/writes legacy tables (`terminal_devices`, `terminal_sync_state`, `pos_idempotency`, `sales`, `sale_lines`, `inventory_ledger`, `audit_logs`). None of those legacy Edge tables exist in the Preview database. The established PRODX financial tables are `prodx_orders`, `prodx_order_items`, `prodx_payments`, `prodx_cash_movements`, `prodx_inventory_ledger`, and `prodx_audit_log`.
- Therefore, do not apply `prodx-pos-edge-sync/migrations/001_pos_ledger.sql` and do not provision Hyperdrive for the current direct-write Worker implementation. The Worker must call the trusted backend adapter; Hyperdrive is optional and should only be created if a reviewed non-financial persistence requirement remains.
- The Supabase MCP connection can perform read-only queries, but no Preview database password is available to configure Hyperdrive. Do not reset it or use Production credentials.
- No database schema, roles/grants, Cloudflare resources, secrets, Worker deployments, or Production settings were changed.

## Safety
- No Cloudflare resource was created or modified while gathering this inventory.
- No secret values were read, copied, or committed.
- No Production deployment, database migration, or merge is authorized by this issue.

References:
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/applications/http-apps/authorization-cookie/application-token/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/service-credentials/service-tokens/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/request/


## OCI Bridge dependency status (2026-11-11)
- PR #374 is Draft and unmerged: https://github.com/prodxowner-png/PRODX-POS/pull/374
- OCI Bridge contract tests: 9/9 passed; TypeScript and Wrangler dry-run passed; all 12 PR checks passed, including 300-terminal PostgreSQL CI load and SQL reconciliation (0 anomalies).

items.title: [RFC] Direct Mooncake Store event ingestion for shared KV-aware routing
items.body:
# RFC: Event-driven shared KV placement from Mooncake Store

Parent: #294 · Related: #414, #528, #426, #489, #554

## Summary

Add an opt-in **direct Mooncake Store event source** to the Router's placement view. The Router subscribes to the Store Master's object lifecycle stream, converts supported connector-specific object keys into verified shared-cache placement, and combines that evidence with existing worker-local placement and load when selecting a target. The Router does not store or move KV tensors; the engine's connector performs the actual lookup and transfer.

This is a design proposal, not an implemented capability. It is an alternative or complement to the Conductor-backed provider in #414 / #528: both answer placement queries, but this design consumes Store events inside each Router. Reuse the placement/provider contract and existing scoring where appropriate; do not double-credit one physical copy when multiple sources describe it. The default deployment and routing behavior remain unchanged.

The first delivery targets a **version-pinned, validated vLLM MooncakeStoreConnector layout and full-attention model**. Do not credit unsupported key layouts, ambiguous connector events, or hybrid cache groups. The current Store stream supports shadow observations but does not, by itself, satisfy #294's active-credit freshness requirements. Active routing is gated on the trust and validation requirements below.

## Motivation

Consider two compatible workers attached to the same shared pool. W0 has the first 32 tokens on its GPU; the Store has a complete, connector-readable copy through token 64. A 65-token request can potentially reuse W0's GPU prefix and fetch the remaining Store-backed portion. W1 may also read the shared copy if it has the same verified pool and connector capability. The pool owns the shared copy; neither the publishing worker nor `medium=CPU` proves that W0 alone owns it.

The Router already indexes worker events and has a cache-owner concept, but the current `CacheOwner` also carries a source/rank and its `target()` resolves to a worker. That representation alone is not proof that other targets can fetch from a shared pool. Store object events also differ from engine block events: the master publishes raw object keys, not token IDs or a reproducible block-hash chain. We need an explicit pool owner, a verified access relation, a connector-specific key codec, and loss-aware source state.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  E["vLLM workers"] -->|"engine KV events"| EI["existing local placement"]
  E -->|"connector put/get"| S["Mooncake Store"]
  S -->|"Master: stored / removed / cleared"| SUB["Store event subscriber"]
  SUB --> DEC["wire decoder + key/layout adapter"]
  DEC --> P["pool-scoped object presence + trust"]
  CAP["verified target ↔ pool capability"] --> Q["placement query / merge"]
  EI --> Q
  P --> Q
  REQ["request tokens + cache identity"] --> Q
  Q --> SCORE["kv_aware: compatible reuse + load"]
  SCORE --> E
```

The Store adapter is an event source for the #294 placement model, not a second authority for worker health or cache transfers. Its physical-object presence is evidence for proving a logical cache record complete; it must not become an independent competing residency authority. First adapt the existing index, and align logical record ownership with #489's proposed unified authoritative record model as that work lands. The subscriber runs asynchronously. The request path reads a bounded in-memory snapshot; it must not wait for replay, reconciliation, a Store RPC, or an actual cache transfer. All configuration names and types below describe proposed contracts, not existing flags or stable APIs.

### Separate identity, ownership and access

Conceptually keep the following distinct:

```text
PoolId          = configured Store backend / isolation domain
CacheIdentity   = tenant + model/weights + adapter + salt + verified hash/layout profile
ObjectKey       = raw connector-produced Store key
SharedCopy      = (PoolId, CacheIdentity, ObjectKey, medium)
ExecutionTarget = (instance_id, dp_rank, incarnation)
AccessContract  = target → pool + connector/version + compatible identity and layout
```

The Store's `group_id` groups objects and is **not** automatically a vLLM hybrid KV `group_idx`. A pool is not a worker. A worker restart or worker clear removes only that worker's local state and access binding; it must not clear the shared pool. A Store removal or clear retracts only the matching pool/tenant/medium scope, not independent GPU/host copies. Events from an engine connector and the Store may describe the same underlying copy; define a single authoritative source per copy, or deduplicate it, before assigning credit. If source/ownership cannot be distinguished, withhold the affected local/shared credit or remain in shadow mode; never infer local versus shared solely from `CPU` or `STORAGE`.

An access binding is a verified operator/worker capability, not an assumption that every registered target can read every pool. At minimum it identifies pool, tenant, model/weights, adapter/salt rules, compatible connector and layout, TP/PP/PCP/DCP arrangement and relevant block/chunk geometry. It is invalidated on worker replacement, config/connector change or pool binding change. Health, worker role and capacity are filtered separately. A missing or mismatched binding gives that target no shared-pool credit.

### Event protocol and object mapping

For the documented Store publisher, accept the ZMQ multipart frames `[topic, sequence, msgpack payload]`, where sequence is unsigned big-endian and the payload carries a timestamp, an array of events, and rank metadata. Iterate the full batch; validate frame sequence and stream-level `event_id` ordering according to the publisher contract. The envelope's `dp_rank` alone does not identify the shared owner or an eligible execution target. Store events contain `event_type` (`stored`, `removed`, `cleared`), `backend_id`, `tenant_id`, and for object events an `object_key`, `medium`, and possibly `group_id`. `cpu` and `disk` identify Store media; `disk` can represent several non-memory backends, not necessarily a worker's local disk. The Store does not decode its keys: its `seq_hashes` / legacy `block_hashes` are empty and `token_ids`, `parent_hash` and `base_block_idx` are nil. Legacy `type` tags do not change those semantics. See the [Mooncake subscriber guide](https://kvcache-ai.github.io/Mooncake/design/conductor/subscriber-guide.html).

Require object-key publication. Validate framing, sequence, event and field sizes, backend/tenant scope, known media and supported key grammar. Unknown versions, keys, or missing/contradictory metadata provide no placement credit. An undecodable or ambiguous removal/clear must revoke the affected source scope; if the scope cannot be proven, invalidate every scope on that publisher. Silently discarding a possible retraction can leave a stale positive. Limit batches, key length, object count and memory; on capacity overflow invalidate the affected source's credit rather than silently retaining a misleading partial view. Do not expose raw prompt tokens, raw object keys, tenant identifiers or salts as metric labels or in normal logs.

Use a versioned `StoreKeyCodec` for a **verified producer and layout**, with golden vectors generated by the real connector, not heuristic parsing of an arbitrary key. For a request, reproduce the connector's chained chunk keys from the exact prepared tokens and identity; account for connector retrieval granularity, chunk boundaries, group, namespace and all required TP/PP/PCP/DCP objects. If multimodal inputs, prompt embeddings, per-block extra keys or any other engine hash input cannot be reproduced exactly, v1 gives that request no shared credit. One object event is not necessarily one complete reusable KV chunk. A logical chunk is available at a given medium only when every object required by the target's access contract is known available; removing any required object revokes that proof. If the connector uses a different grammar, hash seed, granularity or object set, it is unsupported until independently verified. In particular, do not reuse Dynamo's SGLang HiCache key codec for vLLM by assumption.

Model presence as an idempotent set of `(pool, tenant, object_key, medium)`, not event-count-based replica reference counting: duplicate `stored`/`removed` events must not fabricate or underflow copies. A `removed` retracts only its medium; `cleared` retracts the Store-defined `backend_id + tenant_id` scope. An upsert's remove followed by store must be applied in stream order. Store object groups may optimize checks only when their completeness semantics are verified; otherwise verify every required key.

### Query and scoring contract

Extend the existing read-only placement/provider boundary only as needed to carry the prepared token IDs, cache identity, eligible target and access capability. `MatchQuery`'s router-local block hashes and today's `CacheKey` alone are insufficient to reproduce Store connector keys or establish tenant/layout compatibility. Reuse existing local `KvBlockIndexer`; the pool observation can be implemented as an adapter to the unified placement model, not as an obligation to replace the radix tree.

For each eligible target, derive ordered, aligned logical chunks with the target's verified codec, consult the current pool snapshot, and combine only contiguous, restorable evidence with that target's local tier segments. Never sum overlapping local and shared copies. Bound the candidate prefix by the request and engine's recomputation/alignment rules, including the last-token/logits constraint where applicable. Bound prompt tokens/chunks, eligible targets and pools, per-chunk object fanout, CPU work and query time; reuse derivations among targets with identical verified layouts. An exceeded budget withholds shared credit and preserves independent local scoring. Apply each batch atomically with its source progress and use a source-generation fence or equivalent so a query cannot combine an invalidated generation with a newer multi-object snapshot. A failed lookup, unsupported profile, stale pool, incomplete objects or unverified access yields **no shared credit**, not a fabricated hit or a routing error. Actual engine/connector lookup remains authoritative at execution time; an event-derived hit is a routing estimate, not a read lease or guaranteed hit.

The current scorer supports a device prefix plus a non-device continuation; it should not be assumed to implement arbitrary multi-tier stitching. For v1, preserve existing scoring semantics and admit shared continuation only when representable without double credit. If multiple successive or overlapping host/shared/disk segments are needed, specify and test a separate deterministic per-interval merge and tier-cost rule before enabling it. Tier discounts are configurable estimates, not measured transfer latency. Preserve healthy-worker filtering, load, admission and existing fallback even if the shared source fails.

### Example

```text
Request: 65 tokens; hypothetical block boundary: 16 tokens
W0/rank0 GPU:         [0................32)
Pool memory:          [0................................64)
Verified W0 → pool:    yes
Verified W1 → pool:    no

W0 candidate evidence: GPU [0,32) + shared continuation [32,64)
W1 candidate evidence: no shared credit (no verified access contract)
```

This is an illustrative placement calculation, not a measured hit. If any object needed for the shared continuation is removed, that portion loses credit. A concurrent eviction or transfer failure can still make the engine miss after a routing decision.

## Freshness and failure semantics

The documented Store Master stream has no startup snapshot and no replay. A new subscriber cannot know about objects stored before it joined. A gap, disconnect, publisher reset/sequence rollback, bounded queue overflow, source replacement, unknown generation or corrupt batch can hide removals. Sequence is scoped to the publisher stream: invalidate all scopes carried by that stream unless the protocol proves a narrower affected scope, while preserving independent worker sources and other publishers. Do not claim `EXACT` or automatically restore full trust merely because a socket reconnects, a timeout elapses, or a new `stored` event arrives.

Use explicit source states such as `UNINITIALIZED`, `PARTIAL`, `READY`, and `STALE`. `PARTIAL` means observations are incomplete and may be stale during transport uncertainty; an unobserved object is unknown, not a trusted miss. Under #294, this source remains **shadow-only** until a valid freshness contract is established: partial observations must not change active cache credit. Silence alone is not evidence of disconnection or freshness when the producer has no heartbeat; TTL and connection health do not prove correctness or replace retractions. An approximate active-scoring mode, if desired, is a separate future proposal requiring an explicit change to #294 and its acceptance criteria.

An `EXACT`-eligible full view requires an authoritative baseline with a publisher epoch and event watermark plus buffered, ordered handoff, or another explicitly verified equivalent. A plain key scan without a matching watermark is not a consistent snapshot. Per-key/batch probes, if added later, are point-in-time checks rather than leases; define their cost, timeout, error semantics and supported tier separately. A `cleared` event is a barrier only for its documented backend+tenant scope and only if subsequent continuity is established. If the producer cannot supply these guarantees, keep this source partial/shadow or use a provider with the needed recovery contract.

## Hybrid models and multimedium boundaries

V1 does not grant shared-pool credit to a hybrid model merely because one attention group's Store objects exist. Correct credit requires each required group to have authoritative lifecycle evidence and its own restoration rules, plus a common same-target boundary as in #489 / #512–#517 and #554 where applicable. Checkpoint positions, sliding windows, compression, partial pages, group dependencies, and tier/connector capabilities all need an engine-validated contract. A missing group is `unknown`, not a dense-only hit. V1 excludes these cases until tests prove them.

## Configuration and operability

Initially disable the feature by default. A deployment would explicitly configure Store endpoint, pool/backend and tenant, supported producer/codec version and layout, target-to-pool access mapping, memory limits, shadow mode, and (only when active-credit gates are met) applicable tier weights. Reject incompatible or incomplete configuration. Respect existing security/authorization controls; a pool event or a matching hash alone never grants a worker access to a tenant's cached data.

Mooncake needs event publishing enabled in its build and runtime; `kv_events_emit_object_key=false` suppresses per-object events. Monitor source state, last accepted sequence/age, gaps/restarts, dropped/invalid events, codec failures, observed object count, capacity invalidations, eligible/ineligible targets, shared-credit tokens and lookup latency. Use low-cardinality labels only. Store's `/kv_events/status` is useful for diagnostics but does not by itself establish a consistent snapshot or delivery completeness.

## Delivery and validation

1. **Contract and shadow ingestion:** versioned event decoder, bounded per-pool presence and state machine; expose metrics only. Pin and document exact vLLM/Mooncake versions and supported single-group layout.
2. **Identity and codec:** golden vectors from real connector keys for namespace, hash, chunk and all physical shards; negative fixtures for unsupported versions and incomplete objects. Verify pool/target bindings and avoid engine-connector/Store double attribution.
3. **Query and scoring:** integrate the local read-only placement port and one representable non-device continuation, preserving existing behavior when disabled; distinguish unknown, trusted miss and a shadow-only observed hit. Do not activate shared credit before the recovery gate below.
4. **Acceptance:** run deterministic tests for duplicate/upsert/medium removal/clear, late join, gap, reset, disconnect, queue/cap overflow, isolation between pools and local owners, tenant/LoRA/salt mismatch, inaccessible worker, partial object set, alignment, overlapping tiers and hybrid fail-closed. Compare Router predictions against actual engine-confirmed reuse under a real vLLM + Mooncake Store deployment, including warm Store before subscription, evictions and transport failure. Report false-positive and missed credits, TTFT, compute/transfer cost, CPU, memory and p95/p99 Router latency; no performance claim is assumed here.
5. **Recovery and expansion:** add only with an authoritative snapshot/watermark or equivalent contract; separately design multi-tier stitching, hybrid groups and additional connector key layouts.

## Alternatives and open questions

- **Conductor provider (#414 / #528):** centralizes event consumption and supports multiple Routers and engine types. Direct subscription avoids a per-request remote provider call and a separate index service, but multiplies event connections and state per Router replica. Compare deployment cost, latency, availability, consistency and recovery on matched workloads.
- **Engine-published shared-store residency:** [vLLM #58520](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58520) explores publishing complete block residency via the engine stream. That may avoid object-key coupling; confirm removal, ownership, completeness and retrieval semantics before choosing it as the sole source. Coordinate with [vLLM #65548](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65548) on source identity and locality.
- **On-demand Store probes:** simpler residency checks but put remote I/O and timeout pressure on the path unless prefetched; probes do not themselves reserve data. Keep off the request path in v1.
- **Open:** Which connector versions and hash roots can be discovered authoritatively? Can the Store expose a snapshot with epoch/watermark? How is pool access capability attested and revoked? What is the supported source-authority rule during migration? What bounded-staleness policy is acceptable for opt-in hints?

items.title: AdapterRouter should resolve via factory + config + secret manager (not static registry)
items.body:
## Why

Per-tenant adapter routing is the prerequisite for SaaS-multi-RPMS. The naive shape \`AdapterRouter.register(\"tenant-x\", RpmsAdapter.new(...))\` is simple but mishandles credential rotation, multi-process state, lifecycle, and secrets-in-memory. We should build the right shape from the start.

## What

A resolver-style router:

\`\`\`ruby
Corvid::AdapterRouter.resolve(tenant_identifier)
# Looks up TenantConnectionConfig (tenant_id, adapter_type, secret_ref, endpoint, ...)
# Resolves secrets via Corvid::SecretReader (defaults to ENV; hosts plug Vault/SSM)
# Calls Corvid::AdapterFactory.build(config) -> returns an adapter instance
# Caches result with short TTL or until config-change invalidation
\`\`\`

Components:

- \`Corvid::TenantConnectionConfig\` — schema record per tenant: adapter type, endpoint, secret_ref, optional connector_id
- \`Corvid::SecretReader\` — abstract; default ENV reader; production hosts plug Vault / AWS Secrets Manager
- \`Corvid::AdapterFactory.build(config)\` — returns an adapter instance with appropriate connection lifecycle
- \`Corvid::AdapterRouter.resolve(tenant_id)\` — short-TTL cache or webhook-invalidated; rebuilds on stale

## Depends on

- #388 (ADR 0006) — decides whether the adapter is direct (\`RpmsAdapter\`) or connector-shaped (\`RpmsConnectorAdapter\`). Both satisfy \`Corvid::Adapters::Base\`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Schema migration for \`tenant_connection_configs\`
- [ ] \`SecretReader\` abstraction + ENV default
- [ ] \`AdapterFactory\` + \`AdapterRouter.resolve\` + cache invalidation
- [ ] Two-tenant test: two \`TenantConnectionConfig\` records with different adapter types; routing returns correct adapter for each
- [ ] Documented credential-rotation flow

items.title: [E12-T19] purge_source pull model: tenant erasure-worker polls source_purges
items.body:
## Summary
Each firm tenant's erasure-worker enqueues its own source request from a PUBLIC purge row and erases quoted FCA text.

## Description
The command and the PUBLIC-side purge (bump `source_epoch`, write `source_purges`, suspend the connector) are E11; this ticket owns the pull. In every erasure-worker run, under THAT tenant's `fa_worker` role, SELECT `source_purges` rows not yet handled and INSERT its own `deletion_requests` row (scope `source`, source `fca_api`, `subject_ref` = `purge_id`), idempotent on `(tenant_id, purge_id)` (unique index of E12-T5; use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). Then execute it like any request: delete the messages and cached answers that quote FCA text (found via `retrieval_chunk_ids` and `source_document_ids` against the purged documents), with the usual steps and receipt. There is no cross-tenant write and no cross-tenant role (ADR-002 D13a, ADR-039). FCA content never entered Kafka or BigQuery, so those stores need no step. A stopped tenant catches up at its next run (`demo-up` runs the erasure job first). Out of scope: PUBLIC erasure, the drill schedule (quarterly, ops).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given fixtures with 2 firm tenants and a `source_purges` row, when each tenant's worker runs once, then each has exactly one `deletion_requests` row for that `purge_id`, and re-running adds no row (#15; idempotency).
- [ ] Given messages and cached answers quoting FCA text in firm A, when the request executes, then they are gone and a receipt is issued; messages not citing FCA are untouched (#15).
- [ ] Given the L0 leak matrix, then `fa_etl_public` has no INSERT on any firm `deletion_requests` and no cross-tenant role exists (grants test).
- [ ] Given a tenant worker that was stopped during the purge, when it starts later, then it enqueues and executes the pending purge (catch-up test).
- [ ] Given the Kafka and BigQuery fixtures, then they contain no FCA text or chat answer text after the purge (absence scan, #15).

items.body:
> **Refinement status (2026-11-03)**: refined against ADR 0008 (accepted, D-087). Ready. The original body is kept in the refinement comment.

## Problem

ADR 0008 gives a canonical shape to the GRC slice only. A source that produces assets, threats, incidents or remediation work still has nowhere to map. The verbs that point at them (`Finding --affects--> Asset`, `--caused_by--> Threat`, `--requires--> Action`, `Risk --treated_by--> Mitigation`, `ControlImplementation --applies_to--> Asset/System/Service`) have a target marked "shape deferred". Assets, vendors included, still carry no `observed_at`, `confidence` or `provenance`. So a compliance officer cannot say how sure the product is that a host exists or when it was last seen, and an auditor cannot trace an asset back to the discovery that created it.

## Persona

Compliance officer / risk manager: one shape for an asset, a threat, an incident and a remediation action, whichever module or connector produced it.
Auditor: trace any asset or action to its source and observation date.

## Regulatory anchor

ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 7.5.3 (identification and source of documented information). The ADR cites a clause only where a field exists because of it, and claims no conformance.

## Scope IN

- One ADR, `docs/adr/00NN-canonical-model-part-2.md`, the next free number on `origin/master` at writing time (0009 if #1239 has merged and nothing else took it), status `proposed`.
- Field specifications for `Asset`, `Threat`, `Incident`, `Mitigation`, `Action`, `Owner`, `System`, `Service`, `Policy`, `Signal`, on ADR 0008's envelope (D2), source registry (D3), time rule (D4) and vocabulary (D5), **without redefining any of them**.
- The `assets` envelope retrofit deferred by ADR 0004 D1/D8 and moved here by D-083.
- The asset-to-asset verbs of `AssetDependency` joining ADR 0008 D5.
- The mapping from today's persisted models to these entities, in ADR 0008 D7's format.

## Scope OUT

- Any Go code, migration or test (D-030). Types and tests go in a follow-up issue opened on acceptance, as #1240 did for ADR 0008.
- Any change to ADR 0008's seven entities, envelope or confidence rule. A needed change there is an amendment to 0008, named in this ADR with its reason, not a competing shape.
- Any change to `Risk.Score`, SmartScore or the `AssetCriticality` range (0.1–3.0).
- `openrisk-schema.json` (#542).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Entities with data.** Given the ADR, when a reviewer reads it, then `Asset`, `Threat`, `Incident`, `Mitigation`, `Action` and `Owner` are fully specified: every field with its type, optionality and a one-line rationale, each mapped from a model that exists today (criterion 6).
2. **Entities without data, invent nothing.** `System`, `Service`, `Policy` and `Signal` have no domain model today. `type … struct` exists in `internal/domain` for none of them, and `pkg/pwpolicy` is password policy, not a governance `Policy`. Given the ADR, then each of the four is either:
   - specified with a named consumer issue that needs it, and that issue cited; or
   - kept "shape deferred" with the reason and the issue that will hold it.

   No field is specified for an entity no code or issue will read.
3. **Action unifies what exists, or says why not.** Given the ADR, when the `Action` section is read, then it states for each of the following whether it maps to `Action`, maps elsewhere or stays outside, with the reason:
   - `MitigationSubAction` (`mitigation_subaction.go:24`);
   - `IncidentAction` (`incident.go:81`);
   - `RemediationPlan` (`compliance_audit.go`);
   - `CorrectiveAction` (`incident_postmortem.go:181`);
   - the `vulnerabilities.ticket_*` columns.
4. **Asset envelope retrofit.** Given `assets` (`asset.go:77`), vendor assets included, when the ADR is read, then it defines `observed_at`, `confidence`, `provenance`, `source`, `source_id` and `source_version` for an asset:
   - discovered by the scanner or agent;
   - imported from a file;
   - created by hand;
   - reported by a connector.

   It states the backfill value for existing rows, and it states that ADR 0004's vendor rules (D1, D2) still hold.
5. **Asset verbs.** Given `AssetDependency`'s `DependencyType` (`asset_dependency.go:20`), when the ADR is read, then every value is in the vocabulary with direction and cardinality. The aliases `hosted_on` and `stores_data_in` are resolved to one stored verb each, as `CanonicalTopologyType()` already does. No new synonym is added (ADR 0004, alternative E).
6. **Mapping.** Given each persisted model holding data for these entities, when the mapping table is read, then every column is mapped, listed as "no canonical home" or listed as "lost", with the file path. At least these models are covered:
   - `Asset` and `AssetSnapshot` (`asset.go`);
   - `AssetDependency`;
   - `HostInventory` and `HostPackage` (`host_inventory.go`);
   - `Incident`, `IncidentTimeline` and `IncidentAction` (`incident.go`);
   - `Mitigation` and `MitigationSubAction`;
   - `RemediationPlan`;
   - `CorrectiveAction`;
   - the `Ownership` block, `Team` and `TeamMember` (`team.go`);
   - the CTI threat data read by `threat.go` (`cti_vulnerabilities`) and `CTIThreatDismissal`.
7. **Tables without `tenant_id`.** Given a mapped table with no `tenant_id` of its own (at least `incident_timelines`, per ADR 0001 D5), when the ADR is read, then it names the parent gate (`ThroughParent`) for every read and every edge write, per ABSOLUTE RULE 2 and ADR 0008 D5.
8. **Global vs tenant threat data.** Given `Threat`, when the ADR is read, then it states which part is global catalogue (referenced through `provenance.external_refs`, never as a tenant record) and which part is tenant-scoped. Every canonical `Threat` record carries a non-null `tenant_id` (ADR 0008 D2).
9. **Deferred targets closed.** Given ADR 0008 D5's "shape deferred" targets, when this ADR is read, then each one is either specified here or still deferred with its holding issue named.
10. **Tests named.** Given the follow-up implementation issue, when it is written from this ADR, then the ADR names how `TestCanonical_TenantIDRequired` and `TestCanonical_EveryEntityCarriesTheEnvelope` extend to the new entities, and which isolation test covers each `ThroughParent` gate of criterion 7.
11. **Score boundary.** Given `Asset.criticality`, when the ADR is read, then it is mapped read-only to the Score Engine's `AssetCriticality` input without changing its range or its mapping from the LOW–CRITICAL labels, and `confidence` on an asset is stated as never feeding the score.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] tenant_id: N/A, no query. Criteria 7, 8 and 10 carry the rule into the spec
- [ ] Tests: N/A, no use case. They are named (criterion 10) and written in the follow-up issue
- [ ] FR + EN strings, UI states, axe-core: N/A, no UI
- [ ] Security review (devsecops) of the envelope retrofit, the `ThroughParent` gates and the threat global/tenant split: no CRITICAL/HIGH
- [ ] tech-lead review of the full ADR, with sign-off that `Asset.criticality` and `Risk` keep the frozen formula
- [ ] Owner acceptance recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md` (new D-entry)
- [ ] Follow-up issue for the Go types and tests opened on acceptance, `status:needs-refinement`, linked here
- [ ] Claim matrix: no change expected; say so
- [ ] ROADMAP.md: Risk Data Plane line updated (part 2 proposed/accepted)

## Risk

`Asset` is the most-read shape in the product (inventory, topology, the Score Engine's criticality, vendors, scanner correlation). A retrofit that gets `observed_at` or `confidence` wrong on assets skews every finding's attribution and every vendor record at once. Specifying `System`, `Service`, `Policy` or `Signal` without data would publish a shape in #542 that no code fills, which RULE 12 forbids in spirit.

## Estimate

M–L. Six entities with real models, four to justify or defer, plus the largest mapping table in the model (assets).

---
Follows: ADR 0008 (#541, D-087) · Epic: #535 · Decisions: D-030, D-083, D-087 · Feeds: #542, #553 (`applies_to`)

items.title: [STORY] SP-API connector service integration

milestone.title: Phase 1: Foundation (Months 1-4)
milestone.description: Multi-tenant infra, OAuth, Listing Agent, Pricing Agent

items.body:
## User Story

**As a** backend developer,
**I want** a reusable SP-API connector service that handles authentication, rate limiting, and data transformation for all Amazon API calls,
**So that** all agents and services share a consistent, reliable interface to Amazon.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Centralized SP-API client with Login with Amazon (LWA) token management
- [ ] Automatic token refresh before expiry (refresh tokens encrypted per-tenant)
- [ ] Rate limit tracking per endpoint per seller: in-memory counter + Redis backing
- [ ] Adaptive throttling: slow down requests before hitting rate limits, not after
- [ ] Request queue with priority levels: agent-initiated (normal), user-initiated (high), notification-handler (critical)
- [ ] Response caching layer: cache stable data (catalog info) for hours, volatile data (prices, inventory) for minutes
- [ ] Error classification: retryable (429, 503) vs non-retryable (400, 403) with appropriate handling
- [ ] API call logging: every call logged with tenant_id, endpoint, response time, status for debugging and billing
- [ ] Sandbox mode: route calls to SP-API sandbox environment for testing
- [ ] Supported API groups: Listings, Catalog, Pricing, Inventory, Orders, Feeds, Reports, Notifications, Finances, A+ Content, Data Kiosk

## Technical Notes
- Use python-amazon-sp-api library or custom implementation with requests
- Implement as a shared microservice consumed by all agents
- Rate limits vary by endpoint and seller — maintain per-seller-per-endpoint counters

items.title: [invariant-ops] 問い合わせ紐付け・承認付き返信・console 通知 Connector を整備する
items.body:
## 目的

chatwoot 本体の改造やDB直読をせず、AgentsOS Connector、customer-graph、consoleを介して会話と対応履歴をCRM/判断に繋ぐ。優先2。顧客/商談の正本はTwenty、同意/送信可否はoutreach-policyに保つ。

### 実装項目

- [ ] tenantごとにAccount（自社tn_self）、同意の下でInboxを用意。cross-account検索はconsole側で権限付き集約し、super adminでtenant境界を迂回しない。
- [ ] `conversation_created` をcustomer-graphでメール/ドメインからci_id/person_idへ90%以上1分以内に解決（不明時は候補）。incoming `message_created` は既存会話/活動要約/返信照合へ、`conversation_status_changed` は活動終了とstage候補へ。contact custom attributesのci_id/person_id/tenant_idは参照として書き戻す。Webhook署名/認証方式を固定版で確認、検証と冪等排除/順不同処理を実装する。
- [ ] AgentsOS Connectorを唯一のchatwoot API経路とし、Job契約、approval_level、secret_ref/lease、budget、10秒kill switch、本文/HTTP証跡を実装する。L0草稿はprivate noteとconsole判断へ紐付け、返信はL2承認後。新規prospect返信は常にL2、既存顧客定型のL1はpolicyが明示許可した場合のみで送信直前に再検証する。
- [ ] consoleの承認通知は会話にリンクを投稿するだけとし、chatwoot返信で承認しない。Web Pushとchatwootを初期は両方、実機確認後に主経路を決定。承認リンクから該当画面へ1タップ、未読30分で再通知、夜間/週末メールまとめを設定と通知ログで追う。
- [ ] `ChatwootApi.postInternalNote({inbox,title,body,tenant_id})` の本番アダプタ、revops異常通知（成功率低下等→anomaly_found/resolved→内部会話）と、content-ops素材受信（添付をEvidence fileへ）を実装/結合する。trace/秘密をマスクし、重複通知を抑制する。
- [ ] 人間のchatwoot直接返信は許可するが、Webhookで `revops.lead.contacted` と証跡へ記録する。agent側の承認ゲートと人間の直接操作を区別。SNS DMに関する旧X/Instagram/LINEの記述は新規実装せず、ADR-007に従いLinkedInだけ必要性と重複受信を検討する。
- [ ] release tag固定・四半期更新・vault資格情報・障害/復元手順を用意し、MIT/enterprise境界と既存Connector対応範囲を検証する。

### console API（Connector/サイドカー）

`GET /v1/inbox/summary?tenant_id=`（open/unassigned/waiting_over_24h）、`GET /v1/inbox/conversations?status=&tenant_id=`（conversation/channel/contact_masked/ci_id/last_message/status/assignee/draft_id）、`GET /v1/notifications/log?days=`、`POST /v1/inbox/conversations/{id}/reply`（L2、イベントlead.contacted channel email/chat、genre leads）、`POST /v1/notifications`（L0、通知ログ）。通知投稿60req/分。UI表示の承認正本はconsoleに一つ。

### 受け入れ・テスト

- [ ] 未承認agent返信が送信されず、L1例外はpolicy依存、別tenant Connectorから会話不可、ci_id/候補への1分紐付け、通知1タップ、waiting_over_24h>=1の今日表示、30分未読再通知を検証する。
- [ ] 署名不正/再送/順不同、missing tenant/account権限、直接人間返信の記録、private noteの外部送信防止、失敗通知再試行、添付マスク/Evidence失敗、Connector停止/429とChatwoot停止、重複受信、kill switch、異常検知fixtureを試験する。Q-CW-01〜04とQ-INT-LC-01〜02を実装前に証拠付きで整理する。

### 状態・実装境界

本 Issue は invariant-ops の Draft 要件を外部 repo 側で実装・検証するためのバックログ。要件文書上の clone、型、fixture、fake の存在は本番接続完了を意味しない。着手時にこの repo の実装と API を調べ、差分表、固定 release tag、依存先、未決事項を更新する。完了していないチェックは未完了のままにする。

ADR-005 の順序（公式 API/SDK/Webhook → サイドカー → 理由を記録した最小 fork）を守る。独自サービスの API を追加する場合はサイドカー/担当コンポーネントに置き、本体の内部 API や DB へ無断で書き込まない。資格情報は vault の短命 lease と `secret_ref`、正本・tenant・承認の境界は維持する。ライセンスや未確認の製品仕様は本 Issue で法的・技術的に確定したとは扱わず、対象版の証拠を残す。

### 横断の完了条件

- [ ] INV-01〜INV-12 を適用し、承認、送信直前の policy 再検証、予算、10 秒以内の kill switch、テナント分離、マスク、構造化出力、証跡失敗時の失敗処理を該当境界で試験する。署名・支払・申告提出は人間の L3。外部作用の `succeeded` に空の `evidence_ids` を許さない。
- [ ] console 向け API は `X-Tenant-Id`/`tenant_id`（各応答行にも付与、`all` は owner のみ）、`console-ro`/`console-op`（ro から操作は 403）、`Idempotency-Key`（操作は必須、再送時同一結果）、cursor/limit/next_cursor（50/最大200）、ETag/If-None-Match、時差付き ISO8601、429/Retry-After、既定 ro 300/op 60 req/分を実装する。操作受付は 202、完了はイベントで反映する。引下げ・停止解除・予算引上げには該当時 `reauth_token`。
- [ ] 一覧・件数・時系列は原則 `rm_*` read model。各 repo の直接 API は詳細と操作を担当し、個別連携文書の一覧 API との分担は実装差分表で明示する。`genre` を Job/判断/イベントに伝搬し、console の業務画面にソフトウェア名を併記しない。
- [ ] 実 API の request/response と失敗を秘匿化した fixture、契約テスト、異常系、テナント越境、重複、権限、レート制限、依存停止、証跡・秘密混入の試験を残す。実顧客への送信、契約署名、公開、支払で試験しない。
- [ ] 要件 ID → 対応コード/設定 → テスト → 実行結果を記録する。固定版の更新・バックアップ・復元・ロールバック手順を用意し、未接続/未検証を成功と記載しない。

### 要件追跡（この repo の担当境界と跨 repo の結合条件）

以下は固定 SHA の正本へのリンク。関連コンポーネント全体をこの repo に移す指示ではない。各行のうちこの repo の責任を実装し、残りは担当コンポーネントとの依存・結合試験として追跡する。Q は解消・一部解消・未解消の原文状態を保ち、推測で閉じない。

#### [oss-modifications/chatwoot.md](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/oss-modifications/chatwoot.md)

- [ ] [AC-CW-01](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/oss-modifications/chatwoot.md#L79) 新規会話の 90 % 以上が 1 分以内に `ci_id` または候補に紐付く
- [ ] [AC-CW-02](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/oss-modifications/chatwoot.md#L80) 承認されていない返信が chatwoot から送信されない
- [ ] [AC-CW-03](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/oss-modifications/chatwoot.md#L81) 承認依頼の通知から console の該当画面へ 1 タップで到達できる
- [ ] [AC-CW-04](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/oss-modifications/chatwoot.md#L82) テナント A の Account の会話がテナント B の Connector から読めない
- [ ] [Q-CW-01](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/oss-modifications/chatwoot.md#L88) chatwoot の現行ライセンスと enterprise 部分の扱い。自己ホストで使う機能が MIT 範囲に収まるか / 上流 repo の LICENSE と `enterprise/` を確認
- [ ] [Q-CW-02](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/oss-modifications/chatwoot.md#L89) AgentsOS の既存 Connector 設計が Job 契約と承認レベルを持っているか / AgentsOS の repo を読む。own-repos-integration.md と合わせて確定
- [ ] [Q-CW-03](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/oss-modifications/chatwoot.md#L90) SNS の DM（X、Instagram、LINE）を chatwoot の Inbox で受けるか、platform-operator で受けるか / platform-operator の要件と合わせて決める。重複受信を避ける
- [ ] [Q-CW-04](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/oss-modifications/chatwoot.md#L91) push 通知の基盤（Web Push か、専用アプリか） / console の要件で決める

#### [requirements/11-human-console/integrations/listmonk-and-chatwoot.md](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/11-human-console/integrations/listmonk-and-chatwoot.md)

- [ ] [AC-INT-LC-03](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/11-human-console/integrations/listmonk-and-chatwoot.md#L69) `inbox/summary` の `waiting_over_24h` が 1 以上なら今日の画面に出る
- [ ] [AC-INT-LC-04](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/11-human-console/integrations/listmonk-and-chatwoot.md#L70) console の L2 承認要求が未読 30 分で chatwoot に再通知される（NFR-HC-07）
- [ ] [Q-INT-LC-01](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/11-human-console/integrations/listmonk-and-chatwoot.md#L76) 通知の主経路を Web Push と chatwoot のどちらにするか（iOS の PWA 制約、Q-HC-01） / 実機確認後に決める。両方送るのが初期値
- [ ] [Q-INT-LC-02](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/11-human-console/integrations/listmonk-and-chatwoot.md#L77) 問い合わせの返信を chatwoot の画面で人間が直接打つことを許すか / 許す。その場合も `lead.contacted` を Webhook で記録する

#### [requirements/02-customer-graph/README.md](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/02-customer-graph/README.md)

- [ ] [FR-CG-20](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/02-customer-graph/README.md#L108) formsales-mailops と content-ops が送信する本文・件名・Reply-To に、送信を一意に示すトークンを埋め込む規約を定め、受信時にトークンから送信 Job と担当者と商談を特定する
- [ ] [FR-CG-21](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/02-customer-graph/README.md#L109) トークンが無い受信については、In-Reply-To・References ヘッダ、差出人メールドメインと Company のドメイン、件名の類似、本文中の社名で候補を出し、信頼度付きで紐付ける。しきい値は FR-CG-07 と同じ
- [ ] [FR-CG-23](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/02-customer-graph/README.md#L111) 受信内容を「返信」「自動応答」「配信停止要求」「問い合わせ」「バウンス」「無関係」に分類し、配信停止要求とバウンスは `requirements/05-outreach-policy/` に即時通知する
- [ ] [FR-CG-24](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/02-customer-graph/README.md#L112) 照合できなかった受信は console のレビューキューに入れ、人間が紐付けた結果を学習データとして保存する
- [ ] [FR-CG-25](https://github.com/signal-alchemist/invariant-ops/blob/8090a2a2efc51046367f794cea62de4e7152285a/requirements/02-customer-graph/README.md#L113) 照合結果は Twenty の活動（Activity）として記録し、`revops.lead.replied` を発行する
